title: client: shared informer SetX functions are racy
body:
### What happened?

The functions SetWatchErrorHandler and SetTransform are racy with ShareInformer factory


Consider the following example:
```go
	informerFactory := informers.NewSharedInformerFactory(client, 0*time.Second)
	go func() {
		informerFactory.Start(stop)
	}()
	serviceInformer := informerFactory.Core().V1().Services().Informer()
	serviceInformer.SetWatchErrorHandler(func(r *cache.Reflector, err error) {
		// ...
	})
```

In the real world, the goroutine running Start is likely entirely decoupled from the rest; the code here is fairly obviously "wrong".

This has both a data race (I have a PR ready for this) and a logical race. There is no safe way to call these functions unless the entire application is sequenced in a manner such that all informers are created before Start is called. In our real world case, we have some informers that start after application start, which leads to races with other components calling Start().

### What did you expect to happen?

SetWatchErrorHandler and SetTransform can be called without races. That is, I can make an informer from a shared informer factory, set a watcher handler and transform, and ensure they are applied.

### How can we reproduce it (as minimally and precisely as possible)?

See incoming PR which has a test case

### Anything else we need to know?

title: Race when checking for CSI Node Expand support records misleading event
body:
### What happened?

When a CSI driver supports ControllerExpand but not NodeExpand, it is possible for misleading errors to be reported by the kubelet:
```
MountVolume.MountDevice failed while expanding volume for volume "pvc-649b2667-100e-4088-9e6b-c0fe2ef458e1" : Expander.NodeExpand found CSI plugin kubernetes.io/csi/pxd.portworx.com to not support node expansion
```

### What did you expect to happen?

The event should not be reported as ControllerExpand succeeded and NodeExpand is not supported in our NodeCapabilities:
https://github.com/libopenstorage/openstorage/blob/master/csi/node.go#L296-L299

### How can we reproduce it (as minimally and precisely as possible)?

Initiate a PVC resize operation with any CSI Driver that supports ControllerExpand and not NodeExpand. There is a race between the two controllers, so it might not happen all the time.


### Anything else we need to know?

In this code block:
https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/c0ec0c2a311cd223287ad6459e55fa3f8b9241c1/pkg/volume/util/operationexecutor/operation_generator.go#L2092-L2098

We should probably check the CSI Driver Node capabilities before assuming that all CSI Drivers support node expansion.

title: Make net.ipv4.tcp_keepalive_time a safe sysctl
body:
### What would you like to be added?

net.ipv4.tcp_keepalive_time is namespaced and it is used by several java clients for configuring the tcp behaviour. 




### Why is this needed?

1. It would be helpful to be able to configure this for applications without needing to modify the kubelet args. Notable for services with long running connections like elasticsearch   
Notably https://github.com/elastic/elasticsearch/issues/65213

2.  if kube-proxy is configured in IPVS mode which may kill long running connections if keep alives are not present  so having it readily configurable would be nice

title: Lots of pods on Outofmemory state
body:

The pods are getting scheduled on same node repeatedly and getting evicted with status OutOfmemory. 

### What did you expect to happen?

title: Configure which Workload APIs have default spreading
body:
### What would you like to be added?

Add a configuration option the PodTopologySpread plugin to decide which APIs to take into account for spreading.
Currently, the implicit list contains: ReplicaSet, ReplicationController, StatefulSet and Service.

/sig scheduling

### Why is this needed?

The ability to disable spreading for some workload APIs can lead to better resource utilization.

In particular, by disabling support for Services, [Jobs that require a headless Service](https://kubernetes.io/docs/tasks/job/job-with-pod-to-pod-communication/) wouldn't be affected by spreading.

title: Remove very old etcd versions from the bundled versions list
body:
We should start retiring old etcd versions from the etcd migrator's [bundled versions list](https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/a5575425b039bf7c15dfaa9a7acf257fdc4fde3f/cluster/images/etcd/Makefile#L29) so that we can actually obsolete this when [etcd storage versioning](https://github.com/etcd-io/etcd/issues/13168) is implemented.

We'd need a reasonable policy on what stays and what is removed. Maybe look to the supported etcd minor versions?

Note that even if we remove bundled versions, an older version of the migrator can still be used to catch up.

/sig api-machinery

/help

title: generic vs platform/backend-specific options in kube-proxy
body:
There was some discussion in #117297 about generic vs platform-specific options, especially around `--detect-local-mode`, which can be specified on Windows even though it doesn't actually make sense there. (Or at least, it's not _implemented_ there... I'm not sure if winkernel would benefit from it or not?)

Current version of kube-proxy config:

```
kind: KubeProxyConfiguration
apiVersion: kubeproxy.config.k8s.io/v1alpha1
bindAddress: 0.0.0.0
bindAddressHardFail: false
clientConnection:
  acceptContentTypes: ""
  burst: 10
  contentType: application/vnd.kubernetes.protobuf
  kubeconfig: ""
  qps: 5
clusterCIDR: ""
configSyncPeriod: 15m0s
conntrack:
  maxPerCore: 32768
  min: 131072
  tcpCloseWaitTimeout: 1h0m0s
  tcpEstablishedTimeout: 24h0m0s
detectLocal:
  bridgeInterface: ""
  interfaceNamePrefix: ""
detectLocalMode: ""
enableProfiling: false
healthzBindAddress: 0.0.0.0:10256
hostnameOverride: ""
iptables:
  localhostNodePorts: true
  masqueradeAll: false
  masqueradeBit: 14
  minSyncPeriod: 1s
  syncPeriod: 30s
ipvs:
  excludeCIDRs: null
  minSyncPeriod: 0s
  scheduler: ""
  strictARP: false
  syncPeriod: 30s
  tcpFinTimeout: 0s
  tcpTimeout: 0s
  udpTimeout: 0s
metricsBindAddress: 127.0.0.1:10249
mode: ""
nodePortAddresses: null
oomScoreAdj: -999
portRange: ""
showHiddenMetricsForVersion: ""
winkernel:
  enableDSR: false
  forwardHealthCheckVip: false
  networkName: ""
  rootHnsEndpointName: ""
  sourceVip: ""
```

So, things that are maybe mis-organized:

- `conntrack`: Platform-specific to Linux. (Ignored on Windows.) On Linux, it potentially has backend-specific _relevance_ (eg, it might not be important to a Cilium-like backend) but the actual implementation is in `cmd/kube-proxy` and is not backend-specific.
- `detectLocalMode`/`detectLocal`: Theoretically platform-agnostic but currently Linux-specific (and even iptables-specific) in implementation. (Ignored on Windows.) If we added Windows support we might need a different set of modes. For the future `nftables` backend, we will probably want the same modes as we have for `iptables` and `ipvs`, though we will need an nftables-based implementation of each one.
  - `clusterCIDR`: only used with `detectLocalMode: ClusterCIDR`, but for historical reasons is not part of the `detectLocal` block.
- `syncPeriod`/`minSyncPeriod`: Currently backend-specific (with separate `iptables` and `ipvs` versions), but they are used by all three existing backends in the same way (primarily for constructing a BoundedFrequencyRunner). (There is no `winkernel`-specific version of those options; the winkernel code actually uses the _iptables_ `syncPeriod`/`minSyncPeriod`...) In https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/pull/117436/commits/eacbf32344ec11e3da31c44541453b4ce972b5b9 in my refactoring branch, I make those options be backend-agnostic (with the BFR being constructed in backend-agnostic code), so I was thinking that we should deprecate the backend-specific versions and replace them with top-level options (along with the already-backend-agnostic `configSyncPeriod`).
  - [EDIT] Also, we currently use `iptables.syncPeriod` to configure the healthz server regardless of backend.
- `masqueradeAll`: Currently marked as an `iptables` option, but is used by both `iptables` and `ipvs`. AIUI, this is needed with some CNI plugins where replies to pod-to-service-IP-to-pod traffic would otherwise not get routed back through the host network namespace to get un-DNATted. Assuming such network plugins still exist, `masqueradeAll` would still be needed with `nftables` as well. Although at a high-level there is nothing Linux platform-specific about this, it may be addressing a problem that doesn't exist with Windows Kubernetes networking?
- `masqueradeBit`: Platform-specific to Linux. Currently marked as an `iptables` option, but is used by both `iptables` and `ipvs`. The current plan for `nftables` should _not_ need this.
- `oomScoreAdj`: Platform-specific to Linux. (Will cause a non-fatal error to be logged if set on Windows.)
- `portRange`: Backend-specific to `userspace` but not labeled as such and so we forgot to remove it. Oops.

----

So... first question: does it matter? Do we want to try to make this better?

If yes, should we create a `v1alpha2` or `v1beta1` version of the config file?

Should we have a `linux:` subsection for `conntrack` and `oomScoreAdj`?

Should we make `detectLocalMode` be Linux-specific, or alternatively, should we make it into separate/redundant options under `iptables:` and `ipvs:` (and `nftables:`)?

Should we make `syncPeriod`/`minSyncPeriod` be platform-agnostic? (If not, then presumably we should add `winkernel.syncPeriod` and `winkernel.minSyncPeriod` rather than having it use the iptables ones.)

Should we make `iptables.masqueradeAll` be either platform-agnostic or Linux-specific rather than iptables-specific? (It seems like the problem it fixes doesn't exist on Windows...)

Should we add `ipvs.masqueradeBit` so the ipvs backend doesn't have to use the iptables option?

Should we drop `portRange` since it was only used by `userspace`? (Can we do that in `v1alpha1`? We dropped some other userspace-only options before, we just missed this one...)

/sig network
/area kube-proxy
/area ipvs
cc @thockin @aojea 
cc @MikeZappa87 for Windows thoughts

title: "Connection reset by peer" due to invalid conntrack packets
body:
### What happened?

When packets with sequence number out-of-window arrived k8s node, conntrack marked them as INVALID. kube-proxy will ignore them, without rewriting DNAT. However, there is no corresponding session link on the host, and the host sends a reset packet, causing the session link to be interrupted

connection not reset

### What happened?

kubelet_pods.go:897] "Unable to retrieve pull secret, the image pull may not succeed." pod="default/xxxxx" secret="" err="failed to sync secret cache: timed out waiting for the condition"

title: Split /healthz into /livez & /readyz for kube-scheduler
body:
### What would you like to be added?

Quoted from @wojtek-t 's [comment](https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/pull/115754#discussion_r1192068894)

Splitting healthz/ into livez/ and readyz/ 



### Why is this needed?

```
I agree that splitting into livez/ and readyz/ is what we need here:

* livez/ inherits the existing behavior of healthz/ [it just becomes true once the component starts]
* readyz/ is failing when the component isn't initialized (i.e. it's only true after informers are already synced)

Now what we get is:

* non-leader with delayed caching will always be non-ready
* non-leader without delayed caching will be ready as soon as its cache initializes
* leader currently initializing can be distinguished from non-leader using the leader-election metrics

```

title: verify-typecheck checks binaries that don't actually get built
body:
In #118017 I tried to reorganize the kube-proxy build a bit, and ran into the problem that verify-typecheck failed because `cmd/kube-proxy` was no longer buildable on darwin/amd64 and darwin/arm64. This was surprising because we don't build kube-proxy on OS X.

It seems like verify-typecheck ought to be taking `KUBE_SUPPORTED_*_PLATFORMS` / `KUBE_*_TARGETS` from `hack/lib/golang.sh` into account when deciding what to check. There's no reason to be checking the OS X type compatibility of binaries that we don't build on OS X.

title: Network policies only take effect when pods are assigned to the same node
body:
### What happened?

I configured it according to the network policy demonstrated in the official document, and found that sometimes it takes effect and sometimes it does not. After investigation, I finally found that this example only takes effect when busybox and nginx are assigned to the same node, and it does not take effect if they are not on the same node.

url: https://kubernetes.io/docs/tasks/administer-cluster/declare-network-policy/

As shown in the figure, the first part is completely done according to the demonstration of the official document, just to keep the busybox container without '--rm', which can be seen through the command 'kubectl get pod, node -o wide', the first part busybox and nginx are always on the 'worker-130' node, and the expected result is correct. However, in the second part, I forcibly dispatched nginx to 'worker-131' and immediately lost the connection.

### What did you expect to happen?

title: Cancel volume operations when pod is deleted
body:
### What happened?

A pod was created with fsgroup and a very large CSI volume that ended up taking 40 hours to finish applying fsgroup. We realized the issue and tried to redeploy the pod with `fsGroupChangePolicy: OnRootMismatch`.  However, because the CSI volume is DeviceMountable, the volume operations are serialized per volume. So the new pod mount was waiting for the first pod mount to finish before proceeding. Our only option to speed this up was to restart kubelet so that the go routines would be cleared.

```
# First pod with recursive fsgroup policy
[I0515 08:03:03.088181 3067 reconciler.go:254] "operationExecutor.MountVolume started for volume \"pvc-01ce8478-4b29-45bf-a706-fdec57daab68\"
[I0515 08:03:03.697184 3067 operation_generator.go:658] "MountVolume.MountDevice succeeded for volume \"pvc-01ce8478-4b29-45bf-a706-fdec57daab68\" 
[W0515 08:03:33.707310 3067 volume_linux.go:49] Setting volume ownership for /var/lib/kubelet/pods/4e706e27-0a9b-4deb-b65f-3663d5f86919/volumes/kubernetes.io~csi/pvc-01ce8478-4b29-45bf-a706-fdec57daab68/mount and fsGroup set. If the volume has a lot of files then setting volume ownership could be slow, see https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/issues/69699

# 1st pod was deleted and 2nd pod created in between these times

# Finally finished fsgroup for the first pod
[I0516 21:22:41.969724 3067 operation_generator.go:703] "MountVolume.SetUp succeeded for volume \"pvc-01ce8478-4b29-45bf-a706-fdec57daab68\" 

# Tear down 1st pod which has been long gone
[I0516 21:22:42.044686 3067 reconciler.go:201] "operationExecutor.UnmountVolume started for volume \"sandboxing\" 
[I0516 21:22:42.107209 3067 operation_generator.go:863] UnmountVolume.TearDown succeeded for volume "pvc-01ce8478-4b29-45bf-a706-fdec57daab68"

# 2nd pod can finally mount
[I0516 21:22:42.145442 3067 reconciler.go:254] "operationExecutor.MountVolume started for volume \"pvc-01ce8478-4b29-45bf-a706-fdec57daab68\" 
[I0516 21:22:42.152939 3067 operation_generator.go:703] "MountVolume.SetUp succeeded for volume \"pvc-01ce8478-4b29-45bf-a706-fdec57daab68\"
```

### What did you expect to happen?

I think there's a couple of things we can do to improve the experience:
- Create a pod event for fsgroup taking a long time. We only have a kubelet log message today
- Periodically update the event + log instead of once after 30 seconds
- Add the ability to cancel the MountVolume go routine when a Pod is removed 

### How can we reproduce it (as minimally and precisely as possible)?

1. Create a pod with default `fsGroupChangePolicy` and volume with lots of files
2. Delete the pod and create a new pod with `fsGroupChangePolicy: OnRootMismatch` and scheduled on the same node as the first pod
3. The 2nd pod will not be able to mount until the first fsgroup processing is complete. 

### Anything else we need to know?

title: Indexed Jobs can break with high number of parallelism or completions
body:
### What happened?

Currently, the maximum number of completions is MAX_INT32, around 2e9 and the maximum parallelism is 1e5.

When using these values, and assuming a very unlucky case, the field `.status.completedIndexes` can fill up the maximum size for objects in etcd (around 1.5Mi)

/sig apps
/sig scalability

### What did you expect to happen?

An Indexed Job with the maximum number of completions and parallelism to be correctly tracked.

### How can we reproduce it (as minimally and precisely as possible)?

```yaml
apiVersion: batch/v1
kind: Job
metadata:
  name: sample-job
spec:
  completionMode: Indexed
  completions: 2000000000
  parallelism: 100000
  template:
    spec:
      containers:
      - name: bad
        image: python
        command:
        - python3
        - -c
        - |
          import os
          import time
          id = int(os.environ.get("JOB_COMPLETION_INDEX"))
          if id > 1000000000 and id % 3 == 0:
            time.sleep(10000)
      restartPolicy: Never
```

In other words, every index multiple of 3 takes too long to terminate.

### Anything else we need to know?

In the example above, the number of characters needed by the `completedIndexes` field is:

`(10+1)*2*1e5`, roughly 2Mi, where:
- 10 is the number of characters for a number
- 1 for the separating character.
- 2 for the consecutive numbers
- 1e5 for the number of "holes" in the `completedIndexes`, based on the parallelism.

### Kubernetes version

1.21 and newer (when IndexedJob was introduced)

title: APIServices can be deleted at the apiserver startup
body:
### What happened?

Initially reported at 1.24.10, but it seems to be present in master as well:

We observe that a part of apiservices objects have been removed by "system:apiserver" right after the kubernetes upgrade.

It looks like there is race between "autoregister controller" [1] deleting apiservices and "crd-autoregister controller" populating a map of desired apiservices, i.e. in logs we see:
```
INFO 2023-05-16T14:21:35.070841Z Starting autoregister controller
INFO 2023-05-16T14:21:35.070858Z Waiting for caches to sync for autoregister controller
INFO 2023-05-16T14:21:35.071116Z Starting crd-autoregister controller
INFO 2023-05-16T14:21:35.071128Z Waiting for caches to sync for crd-autoregister
INFO 2023-05-16T14:21:35.270943Z Caches are synced for autoregister controller
INFO 2023-05-16T14:21:35.471323Z Caches are synced for crd-autoregister
```

The unwanted APIServices delete happened at 14:21:35.438 GMT so between crd-autoregister sync and autoregister controller.

It looks like we attempt to wait with "autoregister controller" for crd-autoregister to initialize here: https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/5c1d2d4295f9b4eb12bfbf6429fdf989f2ca8a02/cmd/kube-apiserver/app/aggregator.go#L148-L154

but for some reason we don't enter the if branch.

@liggitt tried adding this diff at HEAD:
```
diff --git a/cmd/kube-apiserver/app/aggregator.go b/cmd/kube-apiserver/app/aggregator.go
index 397c151e66a..8b755ab3179 100644
--- a/cmd/kube-apiserver/app/aggregator.go
+++ b/cmd/kube-apiserver/app/aggregator.go
@@ -148,7 +148,11 @@ func createAggregatorServer(aggregatorConfig *aggregatorapiserver.Config, delega
 			// this prevents the autoregistration controller's initial sync from deleting APIServices for CRDs that still exist.
 			// we only need to do this if CRDs are enabled on this server.  We can't use discovery because we are the source for discovery.
 			if aggregatorConfig.GenericConfig.MergedResourceConfig.ResourceEnabled(apiextensionsv1.SchemeGroupVersion.WithResource("customresourcedefinitions")) {
+				klog.Infof("waiting for initial CRD sync...")
 				crdRegistrationController.WaitForInitialSync()
+				klog.Infof("initial CRD sync complete...")
+			} else {
+				klog.Infof("CRD API not enabled, starting APIService registration without waiting for initial CRD sync")
 			}
 			autoRegistrationController.Run(5, context.StopCh)
 		}()
```
and then started a default cluster with local-up-cluster gave:
```
I0518 08:31:16.826743   94479 aggregator.go:155] CRD API not enabled, starting APIService registration without waiting for initial CRD sync
```

which suggest we have a bug in master and the bug is around the "customresourcedefinitions if"

### What did you expect to happen?

APIServices are not deleted, there is no race between crd-autoregister and autoregister controllers

### How can we reproduce it (as minimally and precisely as possible)?

Restart apiserver with apiservices from crds?

Add a patch proposed by liggit@ and watch the initialization race.

### Anything else we need to know?

title: use ipsets in iptables proxier
body:
### What would you like to be added?

The IPVS proxy mode leverages IPSets to significantly decrease the number of iptable rules. Currently, IPTables proxier doesn't use IPSets and can benefit from them.

[there is a kep for nftables proxy mode](https://github.com/kubernetes/enhancements/pull/3824) which might replace iptables and ipvs proxier with nftables, [but that might take time](https://github.com/kubernetes/enhancements/pull/3824#discussion_r1096604360).



### Why is this needed?

Taking an example from the current IPTables proxier, the following rule will be written **n times** _(n being the number of cluster IPs)_. We can replace the n rules with a single one, IPSets with specialized data structures can efficiently match against the set which will significantly increase the packet throughput.

https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/bb67eb5bd237334d6d0343aa382b351002653404/pkg/proxy/iptables/proxier.go#L1076-L1083

[EDIT]
Performance won't increase significantly for clusters with few but long-lived connections as conntrack will kick in after the connection/flow is established bypassing all proxy rules.

[EDIT-2]
This has been raised before(but not discussed) https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/pull/108460#discussion_r960895453

title: helper function for unused storage feature in pkg/proxy/util
body:
`pkg/proxy/util/utils.go` (which is supposed to be utility functions for kube-proxy) contains the function `NewFilteredDialContext` and associated struct `FilteredDialogOptions`, which are not used by kube-proxy and have nothing to do with service proxying. They were added in #91785 as part of a storage-related feature.

However this feature was apparently only ever implemented for two storage backends (scaleio and storageos), both of which have since been removed (#101685, #111620). So the current state is that you can set the associated [options in the kube-controller-manager config v1alpha1 API](https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/pull/91785/commits/f2e23afcf13fef805ad5341bd7a5625de5982d6c#diff-5ad0cddac612ee34ef81af71efaeae956cc08c468cf20ac2bf719aba980a73a6), and kcm constructs a `proxyutil.FilteredDialogOptions` which then gets passed around the volume controller, but there is no code that ever actually _uses_ that object.

I would like to get this code out of `pkg/proxy/util`, because it doesn't belong there. I was originally going to suggest moving it to `pkg/volume/util` or something, but given that it's essentially unused, maybe we should just revert #91785?

/sig storage

title: Improve exponential backoff in reflector
body:
Currently, reflector uses two backoff managers: 
https://github.com/kubernetes/client-go/blob/2a5f18df73b70cb85c26a3785b06162f3d513cf5/tools/cache/reflector.go#L223
One is used for initial list call and other for watch call. 

Imagine following scenaraion when k8s apiserver is under very heavy load:
1. At the beginning, reflector spams k8s apiserver (with exponential backoff) with `List` calls until one of them succeeds (due to APF throtling and receiving `429`)
2. Reflector tries to run `Watch` request and uses separate backoffManager - so again spams k8s apiserver with `Watch` requests
3. If Watch does not succeed during Etcd compaction window (2.5 - 5 minutes usually) at some point it will receive `resourceVersionTooOld` and go back to point 1, spamming k8s apiserver again with List calls (because first backoffManager for List got reseted after 2 minutes of retries for Watch requests)

I propose we combine these two backoff managers into one. 
If we combine these two backoffManagers into one, it will work like this:
- At the beginning, reflector spams k8s apiserver (still with exponential backoff) with `List` calls until one of them succeeds
- Tries to make first watch call instantly (as there is no backoff on this path)
- If it fails, it will makre retries every (30, 60)s
- If watch request fails all the times during Etcd compaction window it will go back to List call, but already being throttled with (30, 60)s window. 

/sig scalability

title: Implement common interface in applyconfigs to make them identifiable as such
body:
### What would you like to be added?

Make all generated applyconfigs implement some common interface that makes them identifiable as such, similiar to `runtime.Object`. How exactly that interface looks doesn't matter, it could be a simple `IsApplyConfig() bool`.

### Why is this needed?

In order to be able to offer a good UX for SSA, dynamic clients such as controller-runtimes need a first-class `Apply` or similiar method. In order for that method to be easy to use, it needs to only accept applyconfigs. Because applyconfigs do not implement a common interface, this isn't possible today and such a method needs to accept `any`.

title: Allow framework plugins to be closed
body:
### What would you like to be added?

I would like `framework.Plugin` implementations, specifically scheduler plugins to be when the scheduler is being stopped. It could implement this by a type assertion on `io.Closer`, so that old schedulers don't have to implement it.

### Why is this needed?

For example, wasm plugins internally use mapped memory and it would be good to cleanly unmap them.

Without this we could use finalizers, but doing that has problems including [some overhead](https://lemire.me/blog/2023/05/19/the-absurd-cost-of-finalizers-in-go/).

title: k8s.io/kubernetes/cmd/kubeadm/app/cmd/phases/workflow TestBindToCommandArgRequirements fails in Go 1.21
body:
### What happened?

`FORCE_HOST_GO=y make test WHAT=./cmd/kubeadm/app/cmd/phases/workflow` fails with the latest Go 1.21 dev branch, with:

```
+++ [0520 15:18:01] Setting GOMAXPROCS: 48
+++ [0520 15:18:01] Running tests without code coverage and with -race
--- FAIL: TestBindToCommandArgRequirements (0.00s)
    --- FAIL: TestBindToCommandArgRequirements/leaf_command,_no_defined_args,_follow_parent (0.00s)
        runner_test.go:406: The function pointers where not equal.
    --- FAIL: TestBindToCommandArgRequirements/container_cmd_expect_none,_custom_arg_check_for_leaf (0.00s)
        runner_test.go:406: The function pointers where not equal.
FAIL
FAIL	k8s.io/kubernetes/cmd/kubeadm/app/cmd/phases/workflow	0.016s
FAIL
```



### What did you expect to happen?

Test should pass but it fails.

### How can we reproduce it (as minimally and precisely as possible)?

Build the latest Go tree from source (or wait for Go 1.21 rc1). Then run:

    FORCE_HOST_GO=y make test WHAT=./cmd/kubeadm/app/cmd/phases/workflow

### Anything else we need to know?

This test is in `cmd/kubeadm/app/cmd/phases/workflow/runner_test.go`.

It is comparing function pointers by using reflect on the function value and then checking .Pointer. This typically does work for ordinary functions, but the test is comparing closures instead. If the closures were created by calling the same function twice, they may be different closures. This is why Go does not support function equality directly at all (which is why the test is resorting to reflect and non-guaranteed behavior).

The closures appear to come from, among other places, cobra.ExactArgs:

```
% go doc -src cobra.ExactArgs
package cobra // import "github.com/spf13/cobra"

// ExactArgs returns an error if there are not exactly n args.
func ExactArgs(n int) PositionalArgs {
	return func(cmd *Command, args []string) error {
		if len(args) != n {
			return fmt.Errorf("accepts %d arg(s), received %d", n, len(args))
		}
		return nil
	}
}
% 
```

The Kubernetes test itself needs to be rewritten not to depend on function pointer equality. In fact, as the comment notes, in the earlier Go implementation, checking .Pointer made it appear that ExactArgs(1) == ExactArgs(3), because Pointer only looks at the code pointer, not the associated data pointer:

```
	// because cobra.ExactArgs(1) == cobra.ExactArgs(3), it is needed
	// to run test argument sets that both pass and fail to ensure the correct function was set.
```

The test is already running the function to test that it behaves correctly. The Pointer comparison should simply be deleted.

Happens at HEAD and in v1.27.1.

Test should pass.

### How can we reproduce it (as minimally and precisely as possible)?

See above.

### Anything else we need to know?

If there are N objects in claims.Items, then this loop

	for _, claim := range claims.Items {
		objects = append(objects, &claim)
	}

is appending the same pointer N times, pointing at the final item in the list. Adding `claim := claim` fixes that mistake, but then it makes the test fail. Something else about the test is buggy, but the bug was being masked by this bug.

In the repro case I added `scheduling := scheduling` to the loop a few lines down, just for good measure, but that one is not causing a problem. The `claim := claim` line by itself causes the test failure.

title: Scheduler: same Pod can exist in both scheduling cycle and scheduling queue
body:
### What happened?


1. A Pod named `PodA` is being scheduled.
2. PodA is updated by someone.
3. The scheduler's EventHandler notices the update in PodA. And let the scheduling queue know about the update via `PriorityQueue.Update` method.
4. `PriorityQueue.Update` checks where PodA exists in the scheduling queue. But, PodA is being scheduled and doesn't exist in scheduling queue.
5. `PriorityQueue.Update` adds the PodA to activeQ. ([ref](https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/0bff705acd8982e34b937116eb2016c9d6e4c4a6/pkg/scheduler/internal/queue/scheduling_queue.go#L680-L684))
6. PodA is being scheduled but exists in the activeQ at the same time.

---

With a similar scenario, it could also happen that the same Pod can exist in both the binding cycle and the scheduling queue, or in both the binding cycle and the scheduling cycle.

### What did you expect to happen?

If the Pod is being scheduled, the scheduling queue shouldn't append the Pod to activeQ.
This bug is easy to solve after in-flight Pods support in https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/pull/117844.

### How can we reproduce it (as minimally and precisely as possible)?

Update a Pod during a Pod is being scheduled.

title: Kubernetes List Api ResourceVersion changes for consecutive same request
body:
When I call a Kubernetes List Api (consecutively two times without any changes in the cluster) with `watch=null` for all namespaces for any resource with `resourceVersion = null`, I notice that the response for the first time has a list ResourceVersion (along with individual item ResourceVersion). The response for the second time has a **different** list ResourceVersion (along with individual item ResourceVersion, which are the **same** as the first version). 

For instance, the response of running `curl {base_url}/apis/apps/v1/deployments` command twice is different only in the list metadata ResourceVersion.
I expected the list ResourceVersion to be the same as the last time if the list ResourceVersion for any individual items is not changed.

Would you happen to know if this is expected? I wanted to store the cluster state in a DB and update the cluster only when the list ResourceVersion is different.
Because of the described behavior, I need to store the ResourceVersion for each item in the list and update the cluster when anything in this set has changed.

Do you know if the resourceVersion for the list is only helpful for watching events and cannot be used for my use case?

title: Pod Garbage collector fails to clean up  PODs from nodes that are not running anymore
body:
### What happened?

This happened after upgrading to Kubernetes 1.26 from 1.24

The succession of events we have observed:
- Our workloads use HorizontalPodAutoscaler to scale up due to traffic increase
- Cluster Autoscaler provisions new nodes to accommodate the new replicas
- Traffic goes down
- HPA downsize replicas
- Cluster Autoscaler notices nodes under the threshold of usage and PODs can be accommodated into other nodes
- Nodes are drained and downscaled
- Kubernetes still reports PODs in a "Running" or "Terminating" state in the node that no longer exists
- Kubernetes control plane reports "Orphan pods" on its audit logs

Kubernetes Garbage collector to clean up these PODs after the node is gone

title: nodeIP parameter is not implemented
body:
### What happened?

Hi! I have a cluster with nodes which have two network interfaces. eth0 with public IP address and eth1 with private one. After cluster initialization public IP addresses were assigned to all nodes as InternalIP. But I want to use local address as InternalIP for my cluster. 
I am trying to define nodeIP parameter in kubelet config.yaml file like this 
```
...
clusterDNS:
- 10.96.0.10
nodeIP: 10.114.0.3
clusterDomain: cluster.local
...
```
but after restart ok kubelet, node address hasn't been changed in `kubectl get nodes -o wide` output. I have also tried another spelling  **nodeIp**, as far as I haven't get in documentation how I can specify this parameter in yaml config file. After that I tried to add `--node-ip=10.114.0.2` option to kubelet.service file. And again, it doesn't work.  

### What did you expect to happen?

I expect that internal address of node will be assigned to local IP address on eht1 interface

### How can we reproduce it (as minimally and precisely as possible)?

add nodeIP parameter to kubelet config.yaml file like this

```

title: Current metrics in hpa considers pods in any state for external metrics
body:
### What happened?

When looking at the status of current metrics on an HPA; if the metric is external it's AverageValue will consider pods in any state. It seems that the recommender excludes these pods when doing it recomendation but it's very confusing when viewing this directly. I think these fields should line up with what the recommender is doing.

For example:

here's part of a hpa describe output which shows the current target ~69 requests with a target of 200
```
Metrics:                                                           ( current / target )
  "istio.io|service|client|request_count" (target average value):  69441m / 200
  resource cpu on pods  (as a percentage of request):              38% (3441m) / 50%
  ...
  Deployment pods:       47 current / 47 desired
  ```

The total number of requests (queried directly from the external metrics provider via a raw kubectl call) is `9094764`

using that value I can tell it should be displaying `193506m`.

Based on that value I can see it's pretty steady in its current state but looking at just the status field one would wonder why it wasn't scaling down.

This was due to having 84 pods in an `OutOfpods` state which was adding that into the calculation for displaying or setting the current metric on the HPA ( 9094764 / (47 + 84) = 69425)


After removing those pods in that state I could see the current metric being displayed correctly again


```
Metrics:                                                           ( current / target )
  "istio.io|service|client|request_count" (target average value):  196646m / 200
  resource cpu on pods  (as a percentage of request):              38% (3438m) / 50%
  ...
  Deployment pods:       46 current / 46 desired
```


### What did you expect to happen?

I would expect the current metric value to match what the recommender is using in its calculation of pod state

### How can we reproduce it (as minimally and precisely as possible)?

- setup an external metric based HPA that uses AverageValue
- Put a few pods into a OutOf* state ( I haven't confirmed what other states it might be considering)

title: Cronjob status.lastSuccessfulTime not populated by a manually triggered job
body:
### What happened?

Given a cronjob created with a scedule of "0 6 * * *" that failed at last run (status.lastSuccessfulTime is now "before" status.lastScheduleTime). 

Then I trigger the cronjob by hand `kubectl create job --from=cronjob/my-cronjob my-cronjob-manual-1234`and this jobs ends successfully. However status.lastSuccessfulTime is not updated, thus making it difficult to monitor failed cronjobs. 

### What did you expect to happen?

status.lastSuccessfulTime should be updated with a timestamp of the succeeded job endTime

### How can we reproduce it (as minimally and precisely as possible)?

Install the attached files:
```
kubectl apply -f configmap-ok.yaml
kubectl apply -f cronjob_test.yaml
```
Wait until cronjob has actually trigged, test with
```
kubectl get cronjob -o jsonpath='{.items[*].status}' | jq
```
to see that lastScheduleTime and lastSuccessfulTime are populated ok (as expected).
Then apply the fail config-map, now the job will not complete OK:
```
kubectl apply -f configmap-fail.yaml
```
Again wait until cronjob has trigged automatically, observe 
```
kubectl get cronjob -o jsonpath='{.items[*].status}' | jq
```
to see that lastScheduleTime is updated but lastSuccessfulTime is not.

Then apply the "OK" configmap and then create the job by hand:
```
kubectl apply -f configmap-ok.yaml
kubectl create job --from=cronjob/test-cronjob test-cronjob-manual-$(date +%s)
```
when the job has finished and completed ok, observe that lastSuccessfulTime is still not updated.
```
kubectl get cronjob -o jsonpath='{.items[*].status}'
```
Wait until next schedule and observe that the field is now updated.

title: Pod phase changed when container exits with 0 in 1.27
body:
/sig node

After https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/pull/115331 the phase of terminal pods killed with killPodFunc is determined based on the exit codes of the containers. This was discovered in the context of preemption while doing a cherry-pick to 1.26, and observing that the phase changed: https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/pull/118221.

Summary of the phase transitions when the pod container exits with 0 (when restartPolicy=Always):
| scenario                                         | 1.26             |  1.27 
| -----------                                          | -----------       |  -----------
|  preemption                                  |  Failed         | Succeeded
|  eviction due to node pressure                      |  Failed         | Succeeded
| node shutdown                            | Failed | Succeeded
| active deadline exceeded           | Failed          | Failed

Note that eviction due to exceeding storage limits isn't affected because it uses grace period=0. In that case, SIGKILL is sent directly, and the containers end with 137. 

Are the changed phases a bug?
- if a bug, how to approach fixing it?
- if not a bug, we should clean up the setting of the phase as Failed in the component status updates, like here: https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/master/pkg/kubelet/preemption/preemption.go#L106

Note: The change of phase for "node shutdown" was discovered earlier and uncovered a DaemonSet issue that was fixed: https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/issues/117018

[Umbrella Issue] Replace google/gnostic import with google/gnostic-models
body:
Currently, k/k and all dependencies depend on [gnostic v0.5.7-v3refs](https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/master/go.mod#L42) because we did not want to capture the additional dependencies introduced with later versions of gnostic. We use gnostic for OpenAPI protobuf serialization/deserialization. Gnostic was split into multiple modules for better encapsulation, and the only component we require is the openapi protobuf encoding module which is under github.com/google/gnostic-models. We should update all references of that.

- [x] https://github.com/kubernetes/kube-openapi/pull/402
- [x] https://github.com/kubernetes-sigs/kustomize/pull/5186
- [x] https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/pull/118384

Because module renames are backwards incompatible, our users are running into a upgrade issues. In order to upgrade properly, the three repos that were changed must be updated together: client-go 0.28, kube-openapi 20230601164746-7562a1006961 , kustomize 5.1.

Unfortunately since these three modules all follow different release cadences, a naive `go get -u` causes problems because client-go 0.28 is unreleased yet while the other modules are available. This creates issues such as: https://github.com/kubernetes/client-go/issues/1266.

The workaround for `go get -u` is to pin kube-openapi to an earlier version for clients using a version of client-go <0.28. This is temporary until client-go 0.28 is released.

```
go mod edit --replace k8s.io/kube-openapi@v0.0.0-20230601164746-7562a1006961=k8s.io/kube-openapi@v0.0.0-20230606174411-725288a7abf1
```

Obviously the alpha version of client-go can also be used to mitigate this problem (k8s.io/client-go v0.28.0-alpha.2) but it's generally recommended to be on a stable version.

For larger projects like flux, other projects that depend on one of the three projects above are part of the imports, and the chain needs to be synced before an upgrade. 

This includes:
- https://github.com/kubernetes-sigs/cli-utils
- https://github.com/kubernetes-sigs/controller-runtime
- https://github.com/sigstore/cosign
- https://github.com/kubernetes-sigs/cluster-api/

/sig api-machinery
/triage accepted

title: Issue for Aggregated Discovery for Beta (v1.27)
body:
In Kubernetes 1.26, Kubernetes Enhancement Proposal, KEP-3352[1]: Aggregated Discovery, enhanced the discovery mechanism and supported aggregated discovery optimizing response for discovery api. 

To support this KEP, Changes were made to both API server and client to support aggregated discovery mechanism. This feature was available alpha in Kubernetes 1.26 behind a feature flag, `AggregatedDiscoveryEndpoint`. 

In Kubernetes 1.27, aggregated discovery endpoint was promoted to beta and enabled by default[2]. Here is a class of problems that ended up getting triggered.

GOOD NEWS!! is that it is already fixed by https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/pull/116603 in 1.27 and a cherry pick https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/pull/116666 in 1.26

For example, With Prometheus adapter, we saw issues across repositories:

- https://github.com/helm/helm/issues/12061#issuecomment-1537935360
- https://github.com/vmware-tanzu/sonobuoy/issues/1910#issue-1690940687
- https://github.com/rook/rook/issues/12114#issuecomment-1518609858

One signature of this is following in the traceback:

```
k8s.io/client-go/discovery.convertAPIResource(...)
  /go/pkg/mod/k8s.io/client-go@v0.26.2/discovery/aggregated_discovery.go:88
```

title: [FG:InPlacePodVerticalScaling]  K8s fails to throttle pod so that it follows resized CPU limit
body:
### What happened?

I have a pod which initially has 0.5 CPU limit. I then resize it to follow 1.5 CPU limit and pod starts to use more resources until 1.5CPU. Problem arises when I resize pod CPU limit back to 0.5CPU.  Instead of throttling the pod, kubernetes doesn't do anything and pod continues to use up to 1.5CPU resource.

I have followed instructions [here](https://kubernetes.io/docs/tasks/configure-pod-container/resize-container-resources/) to resize limits of pods. I am monitoring it using metrics server and I can see that new limits are applied but when you increase limit and then decrease it, kubernetes  fails to throttle pod so that it follows new decreased limit.
 




### What did you expect to happen?

I expected kubernetes to throttle the pod so that it doesn't use more than 0.5CPU but all I observe is that it is using more CPU Resource than limit. 

### How can we reproduce it (as minimally and precisely as possible)?

you can use any pod stressing the CPU (for example  image:polinux/stress) and try to increase CPU resource limit and then decrease it.

test.yml:
```
apiVersion: v1
kind: Pod
metadata:
  name: pod-demo
  namespace: stress-test
spec:
  containers:
  - name: pod-demo
    image: polinux/stress
    resources:
      limits:
        memory: "600Mi"
        cpu: 0.2

```

Apply the yaml file:

After 1/2 minute resize to decrease the CPU limit:
```kubectl -n stress-test patch pod pod-demo --patch '{"spec":{"containers":[{"name":"pod-demo", "resources":{"requests":{"cpu":"100m","memory":"600Mi"} ,"limits":{"cpu":"200m", "memory":"600Mi"}}}]}}'```

title: EndpointSlice object is not removed when service selector is made to be empty
body:
### What happened?

Implementations like kube-proxy might direct service traffic to stale endpoint slice as if it was a valid endpoint.

### What did you expect to happen?

The EndpointSlice (have service object as owner reference) object must get removed when service selector is set to empty.

### How can we reproduce it (as minimally and precisely as possible)?

1. Create a Pod Deployment and Service with a corresponding selector label.
2. Ensure Endpoint and EndpointSlice (with service object as the owner reference) is created.
3. Edit the Service object by removing selector label.
4. Check how Endpoint and EndpointSlice objects are updated.

### Anything else we need to know?

**Actual Result:**

The Endpoint and EndpointSlice (having service object as owner reference)  object is untouched, a new EndpointSlice mirror object (having Endpoint object as owner reference) is created. 

An update on the Endpoint object also modifies EndpointSlice mirror object and not the old endpointslice object (which is a desired behavior).

**Observation:**

The PR https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/pull/105997 adds/removes mirrored EndpointSlice when selector is updated from non empty to empty and vice versa.
But EndpointSlice controller doesn't delete EndpointSlice object when service's selector is set to empty.

title: Use `secrets` field in `NodePublishVolumeRequest` for sa tokens
body:
If the `TokenRequests` field is set in the `CSIDriver` spec, the tokens are generated and funneled from kubelet to driver as part of volume attributes map. The key for the tokens in the map is `csi.storage.k8s.io/serviceAccount.tokens`.  The service account tokens can be used for workload identity in cloud providers. Especially in case of Secrets Store CSI Driver, these service account tokens are used to access external secrets store to get secrets and mount in the volume. 

As these tokens are sensitive information, it doesn't feel right to include these in the volume context map along with pod name, namespace, service account name which are non-sensitive information. There is a dedicated [secrets field in the proto](https://github.com/container-storage-interface/spec/blob/master/lib/go/csi/csi.pb.go#L4063-L4066) which today is being used for `nodePublishSecretRef` that would be more appropriate for tokens.

To provide more context on "why this issue", we had a CVE in the Secrets Store CSI Driver (ref: [CVE-2023-2878](https://github.com/kubernetes-sigs/secrets-store-csi-driver/security/advisories/GHSA-g82w-58jf-gcxx)) where the service account tokens were logged as part of the GRPC request in the driver. We use the [protosanitizer](https://github.com/kubernetes-csi/csi-lib-utils/blob/master/protosanitizer/protosanitizer.go) in the driver to sanitize the requests before logging but given volume context is not really considered a "secret", the tokens were skipped and logged. We got around this by building custom logic for logging in the driver to strip the tokens but this is something every driver would need to do to be careful and not log the tokens. A change could be made in protosanitizer to sanitize this but given volume context is a map, either entire map needs to be marked a secret or sanitizing has to be done on a field by field basis. Although this prompted me to create this issue, I think volume context is not really "secrets" and appropriate field for sensitive sa tokens would be the secrets field.

/sig storage

title: Testing: ./consume-cpu/consume-cpu binary in resource-consumer tool didn't consume the specified millicores
body:
### What happened?

I tried to use resource-consumer tool to generate enough workload on my nodes to crash them (either generating a NodeNotReady or SystemOOM event). However, when I used ./consume-cpu/consume-cpu binary in an Deployment with resoure-consumer image and told it to consume a specific amount of millicores, it never consumed that amount of cpu but always lower than that. 

### What did you expect to happen?

The ./consume-cpu/consume-cpu should consume the exact amount that I specified for the argument --millicores=<cpu usage>

### How can we reproduce it (as minimally and precisely as possible)?

Create a cluster with 3 nodes, each has 2 vCPU and 7GiB of memory, so total capacity for all nodes is 6 vCPU and 21 GiB of memory. Run the below deployment in the cluster: 
```
apiVersion: apps/v1
kind: Deployment
metadata:
  name: resource-consumer
  namespace: default
spec:
  replicas: 12
  selector:
    matchLabels:
      app: resource-consumer
  template:
    metadata:
      labels:
        app: resource-consumer
    spec:
      containers:
      - name: resource-consumer

          - --millicores=500
        resources:
          requests:
            cpu: 10m
```
This should be able to consume all 6 vCPU of the nodes. Wait for 30 seconds or so then run `k top pods -kube-system` to check the resource usage. Also, run `k describe nodes` to check for events to see if nodes were crashed or not.

title: CVE-2023-2878: secrets-store-csi-driver discloses service account tokens in logs
body:
A security issue was discovered in [secrets-store-csi-driver](https://github.com/kubernetes-sigs/secrets-store-csi-driver) where an actor with access to the driver logs could observe service account tokens. These tokens could then potentially be exchanged with external cloud providers to access secrets stored in cloud vault solutions. Tokens are only logged when [TokenRequests is configured in the CSIDriver object](https://kubernetes-csi.github.io/docs/token-requests.html) and the driver is set to run at log level 2 or greater via the -v flag.

This issue has been rated **MEDIUM** [CVSS:3.1/AV:L/AC:L/PR:L/UI:N/S:C/C:H/I:N/A:N](https://www.first.org/cvss/calculator/3.1#CVSS:3.1/AV:L/AC:L/PR:L/UI:N/S:C/C:H/I:N/A:N) (6.5), and assigned **CVE-2023-2878**

**Am I vulnerable?**

You may be vulnerable if [TokenRequests is configured in the CSIDriver object](https://kubernetes-csi.github.io/docs/token-requests.html) and the driver is set to run at log level 2 or greater via the -v flag.

To check if token requests are configured, run the following command:

```shell
kubectl get csidriver secrets-store.csi.k8s.io -o jsonpath="{.spec.tokenRequests}"
```

To check if tokens are being logged, examine the secrets-store container log:

```shell
kubectl logs -l app=secrets-store-csi-driver -c secrets-store -f | grep --line-buffered "csi.storage.k8s.io/serviceAccount.tokens"
```

**Affected Versions**

- secrets-store-csi-driver < 1.3.3

**How do I mitigate this vulnerability?**

Prior to upgrading, this vulnerability can be mitigated by running secrets-store-csi-driver at log level 0 or 1 via the -v flag.

**Fixed Versions**

- secrets-store-csi-driver >= 1.3.3

To upgrade, refer to the documentation: [https://secrets-store-csi-driver.sigs.k8s.io/getting-started/upgrades.html#upgrades](https://secrets-store-csi-driver.sigs.k8s.io/getting-started/upgrades.html#upgrades)

**Detection**

Examine cloud provider logs for unexpected token exchanges, as well as unexpected access to cloud vault secrets.

If you find evidence that this vulnerability has been exploited, please contact [security@kubernetes.io](mailto:security@kubernetes.io)

**Acknowledgements**

This vulnerability was reported by Tomer Shaiman `@tshaiman` from Microsoft.

title: the kubelet should respect the pod priority when initializing after restart
body:
### What happened?

this is a followup of https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/issues/109595
We improved the kubelet behavior by [making the devicemanager actually deliver the requested devices, failing admission otherwise](https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/pull/116376). The workload/controllers can now detect the inconsistencies and retry rather than silently crash.

However looking deeply at how kubelet initializes itself after restart, we see the kubelet is not taking into account the pod priorities:

```

Some random examples: 
```
sriov-device-plugin-22z44    system-node-critical    2000001000
```
yet processed **after**
```
node-exporter-dhln9    system-cluster-critical    2000000000
```
and even **after**
```
collect-profiles-*    openshift-user-critical    1000000000
```
(please just note the priority, lower than `system-node-critical`)

EDIT 20230605
this is because the kubelet actually sorts the pods it receives, [but by creation time](https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/v1.28.0-alpha.1/pkg/kubelet/kubelet.go#L2521). It should sort pods first by priority, **then** by creation time.

### What did you expect to happen?

when initializing after restart, thus when effectively recovering the node state, the kubelet should process pods in decreasing priority order, start from highest priority down to the lowest priority.
EDIT 20230605
Within the same priority, the kubelet should [keep sorting the pods by creation time](https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/v1.28.0-alpha.1/pkg/kubelet/kubelet.go#L2521)

This minimizes the disruptions, minimizes or avoid admission errors and thus minimizes the pod downtime.

### How can we reproduce it (as minimally and precisely as possible)?

The pod priority is not taken into account when kubelet initializes,
EDIT 20230605
[but only by creation time.](https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/v1.28.0-alpha.1/pkg/kubelet/kubelet.go#L2521)
The behavior observed from logs, and a cursory look at code.

### Anything else we need to know?

EDIT 2030605 obsolete
~~I'm not sure this is a bug or an improvement. Looking at how kubelet handles [the config sources](https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/master/pkg/kubelet/config/config.go#L158)~~
~~seems to suggests there it is (used to be?) a reason to relay events from apiserver in order. However in the important corner case of kubelet initializing after a restart, I don't think this applies because updates are effectively received at the same time, so honoring pod priority looks the best thing.~~

This fix should compose nicely with admission improvements mentioned in https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/issues/109595#issuecomment-1540565113

title: kube-controller-manager should not cache managedFields
body:
### What would you like to be added?

Remove [`managedFields`](https://github.com/kubernetes/apimachinery/blob/v0.27.2/pkg/apis/meta/v1/types.go#L271) from the cached used by controllers in `kube-controller-manager`. If feasible, this work will be applied to other components having similar use patterns but have no use of `managedFields` at all.

### Why is this needed?

Roughly the content in `managedFields` is a copy of whole object so it takes roughly 40% of total object size, which is a significant memory overhead. Removing it for controllers can improve memory efficiency

title: make scheduler_perf easy to use from external
body:
### What would you like to be added?

Currently many parts of `scheduler_perf` is implemented in [scheduler_perf_test.go](https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/master/test/integration/scheduler_perf/scheduler_perf_test.go), 
and that prevents external scheduler from using scheduler_perf.

### Why is this needed?

In [kube-scheduler-wasm-extension](https://github.com/sanposhiho/kube-scheduler-wasm-extension), I'd like to check an overall scheduling performance via scheduler_perf because the performance is a critical point for the project.
But, I believe it's a common use case for other custom schedulers as well.

/sig scheduling

title: Failed to mount the hostPath /proc/net/
body:
### What happened?

I want to deploy a pod in my cluster to monitor NIC information on nodes. I mount `/proc/net/` of the host directory to my pod in hostPath mode.
However, when I enter the container, I find that the owner of the mount point is incorrect, and the content in the corresponding directory is not the content of `/proc/net/dev` on the host, but the content of `/app/proc/net/dev` in the container.
What's even more amazing is that when I remove the "/" at the end of the host directory (`/proc/net`) and go back to the container, the directory and content are correct.
I don't know if this is a problem of k8s or runc.

Can anyone helps? Thanks a lot.

### What did you expect to happen?

The content of `/app/proc/net/dev` in the container is the same as the content of `/proc/net/dev` on the host.

### How can we reproduce it (as minimally and precisely as possible)?

1.Start up a local k8s cluster with Kubernetes v1.25.3 by hack/local-up-cluster.sh;

2.Apply a Pod with busybox with hotsPath `/proc/net/` to `/app/proc/net/` of container;
```
apiVersion: v1
kind: Pod
metadata:
  name: busybox
  namespace: default
spec:
  containers:
  - name: busybox
    image: registry.k8s.io/e2e-test-images/busybox:1.29-2
    command: ["/bin/sh","-c","sleep 3600;"]
    imagePullPolicy: IfNotPresent
    volumeMounts:
    - mountPath: /app/proc/net
      name: net
  volumes:
  - hostPath:
      path: /proc/net/
      type: ""
    name: net
  securityContext:
    runAsGroup: 2000
    runAsUser: 3001
```
3.Run the Kubectl exec command to access the busybox container and check whether the content of `/app/proc/net/dev` is the same as that of `/proc/net/dev` on the host;
![image](https://github.com/opencontainers/runc/assets/46313756/50abdc2f-ccec-4e18-a20d-91f455b80323)


4.When I change the hotsPath from `/proc/net/` to `/proc/net`, it works as what I want.

title: Pod graceful deletion hangs if the kubelet already rejected that pod at admission time
body:
### What happened?

We observed the following series of events:

1) Pod is created with some attributes that later result in the pod being rejected at kubelet admission time
2) The pod is scheduled to a node
3) The pod is gracefully deleted by a controller, i.e. a deletion timestamp is set on the pod
4) The pod is rejected at kubelet admission time
5) The pod never gets deleted and is stuck: despite having the deletion timestamp set. It seems that kubelet does not issue the final force delete for the pod.

This is problematic in many scenarios, but one specific case it was hit was when the pod is backed by a daemonset controller. This issue manifested in way where since the pod never got deleted in step 5 above, the daemonset controller did not create a new pod to run the on the node and thus node was was not running a replica of the daemonset controller pod.

This seems to a be regression in k8s 1.27, I was not able to repro this behavior in 1.26.

### What did you expect to happen?

It is expected at during the series of events above, after the pod is failed at kubelet admission time, since the pod has a deletion timestamp set, the kubelet should forcefully delete the pod. The pod should not hang in deletion forever. 

### How can we reproduce it (as minimally and precisely as possible)?

Create a 1.27 kind cluster:

```
kind delete cluster


kind_config="$(cat << EOF
kind: Cluster
apiVersion: kind.x-k8s.io/v1alpha4
networking:
  ipFamily: ipv4
nodes:
# the control plane node
- role: control-plane
- role: worker
  kubeadmConfigPatches:
  - |
    kind: JoinConfiguration
    nodeRegistration:
      kubeletExtraArgs:
        v: "4"
        read-only-port: "10255"
EOF
)"

kind create cluster --config <(printf '%s\n' "${kind_config}") --image  kindest/node:v1.27.1@sha256:b7d12ed662b873bd8510879c1846e87c7e676a79fefc93e17b2a52989d3ff42b
```

Stop kubelet
```
$ docker exec -it kind-worker /bin/bash
root@kind-worker:/# systemctl stop kubelet
```

Create a pod bound to the node which will trigger a admission error. The below node selector label does not exist, so we expect that the pod should be rejected in admission.

```
apiVersion: v1
kind: Pod
metadata:
  name: ubuntu-sleep-2
spec:
  nodeSelector:
    this-label: does-not-exist
  nodeName: "kind-worker"
  containers:
  - name: ubuntu
    image:  gcr.io/google-containers/ubuntu:14.04
    command: ["/bin/sleep"]
    args: ["infinity"]
    resources:
      requests:
        cpu: "1"
        memory: "10Mi"
      limits:
        cpu: "1"
        memory: "10Mi"
```

While kubelet is down issue a graceful deletion to set a deletion timestamp on the pod

```
kubectl delete pod ubuntu-sleep-2
```

Verify deletion timestamp is set (pod is pending)

```
$ k get pod ubuntu-sleep-2 -o yaml

title: Documented resource quota keys `services.loadbalancers` and `services.nodeports` don't have an effect
body:
### What happened?

We've configured a a resource quota to restrict the number of LoadBalancer services which can be created in a namespace according to the documentation in https://kubernetes.io/docs/concepts/policy/resource-quotas/#object-count-quota.

However, setting `count/services.loadbalancers` in a `ResourceQuota` doesn't have any effect, and existing LB services don't appear to be counted against the quota either.

I've been able to replicate the issue in a Kind cluster using Kubernetes v1.27.1:

```
simon@phoenix:~ $ kind --version
kind version 0.19.0
simon@phoenix:~ $ kind create cluster
Creating cluster "kind" ...

You can now use your cluster with:

kubectl cluster-info --context kind-kind

Not sure what to do next? 😅  Check out https://kind.sigs.k8s.io/docs/user/quick-start/
simon@phoenix:~ $ kubectl -n default apply -f - <<EOF
apiVersion: v1
kind: ResourceQuota
metadata:
  name: no-lb-services
spec:
  hard:
    count/services.loadbalancers: 0
EOF
resourcequota/no-lb-services created
simon@phoenix:~ $ kubectl -n default get resourcequota
NAME             AGE   REQUEST                             LIMIT
no-lb-services   6s    count/services.loadbalancers: 0/0   
simon@phoenix:~ $ kubectl -n default create service loadbalancer test --tcp 8000
service/test created
simon@phoenix:~ $ kubectl -n default get resourcequota
NAME             AGE   REQUEST                             LIMIT
no-lb-services   38s   count/services.loadbalancers: 0/0   
simon@phoenix:~ $ kubectl -n default get services
NAME         TYPE           CLUSTER-IP     EXTERNAL-IP   PORT(S)          AGE
kubernetes   ClusterIP      10.96.0.1      <none>        443/TCP          15m
test         LoadBalancer   10.96.198.74   <pending>     8000:32483/TCP   14m
```

 

### What did you expect to happen?

`kubectl create service loadbalancer test --tcp 8000` fails with an error along the lines of (paraphrased from an error for a quota with `count/services=0`):

```
error: failed to create LoadBalancer service: services "test" is forbidden: exceeded quota: no-lb-services, requested: count/services.loadbalancers=1, used: count/services.loadbalancers=0, limited: count/services.loadbalancers=0
```

### How can we reproduce it (as minimally and precisely as possible)?

```
kind create cluster
kubectl create -f - <<EOF
apiVersion: v1
kind: ResourceQuota
metadata:
  name: no-lb-services
spec:
  hard:
    count/services.loadbalancers: 0
EOF
kubectl create service loadbalancer test --tcp 8000
```

### Anything else we need to know?

I've looked through the code a bit and found the following:

* https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/pull/54320 refactored the object counting to support all namespaced resources.
* The previously supported -- now "legacy" -- object count names are tracked in https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/f812ac54451828d4f70302ba4c775ceedbea22a9/pkg/quota/v1/evaluator/core/registry.go#L27-L33
* The service quota evaluator still has code to count LB and NodePort services: https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/f812ac54451828d4f70302ba4c775ceedbea22a9/pkg/quota/v1/evaluator/core/services.go#L112-L145

title: Cleanup the Job controller exponential backoff delay
body:
/sig apps

The code around Job controller exponential backoff delay has a lot of heritage. The purpose of this issue is to collect and discuss cleanup ideas. It was initiated by the backoff discussion under the KEP: https://github.com/kubernetes/enhancements/pull/3967#discussion_r1219690984.

Some fixes initiated by the discussion and small cleanups are already handled by the PR: https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/pull/118470.

The source of the issue might be that the “backoff” delay is used in two different contexts:
- Value of the exponential backoff delay is computed based on the number of consecutive failures. It’s main purpose is to throttle pod creation rate when the pods fail: https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/master/pkg/controller/job/job_controller.go#L1415-L1419. 
- Value computed by the number of requeues in the queue https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/master/pkg/controller/job/job_controller.go#L1546-L1564

First, I suggest splitting the naming of these two different backoffs. Let’s use “api error backoff delay” and “pod failure backoff delay”. It would be good if the naming in the code reflected this difference.

Second, the “api error backoff delay” is used in non-obvious places:
- When handling a pod which is transitioning to failed phase: https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/4c40d749006a8895f6718f2b624a3dbe975988ab/pkg/controller/job/job_controller.go#L321 (seems ok to drop)
- Where there is API conflict: https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/4c40d749006a8895f6718f2b624a3dbe975988ab/pkg/controller/job/job_controller.go#L879

Also, I suggest having the following methods to requeue `syncJob` to make the intention clearer to the reader:
- `enqueueControllerImmediately(key)` - no delay
- `enqueueControllerDelayed(key)` - delayed by `max(1s, api error backoff)`
- `enqueueControllerDelayedByApiErrors(key)` - delayed by `max(1s, api error backoff)` [not sure we need it since the queue itself has this method 
- `enqueueControllerWithCustomDelay(key, delay)` - delayed by `max(1s, delay)`. Here the delay would be computed for pod failure backoff, outside of the function.

However I’m not sure we need `enqueueControllerDelayedByApiErrors` since the queue itself rate rate limiting built-in. We should determine if this is legacy throttling on top of the built-in rate limiting, or it is needed for some scenarios.

title: PV controller is slow when there are many released PVs
body:
### What happened?

We have seen PVC binding (no dynamic provisioning) to take minutes when there are thousands of released PVs in the cluster. This is common when using local PVs in the cloud, where nodes get deleted more frequently and leave behind stale local PV objects.

It looks like PV controller is getting throttled by client-go, but the API server does not seem loaded, and there does not seem to be a signficant amount of UPDATEs from the PV controller (10 in a few minutes).
```
Waited for 14.99364385s due to client-side throttling, not priority and fairness, request: PUT:<apiserver>:443/api/v1/namespaces/default/persistentvolumeclaims/<pvc name>/status
```

From code inspection, here's what I've found so far:

Potentially unnecessary Get() calls: 
- https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/v1.27.0-alpha.2/pkg/controller/volume/persistentvolume/pv_controller.go#L643
- https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/fb57080e069fe2efe11734a4570a92873e673c35/pkg/controller/volume/persistentvolume/pv_controller.go#L1295

Unbind volume does not check if updated is needed: 
https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/fb57080e069fe2efe11734a4570a92873e673c35/pkg/controller/volume/persistentvolume/pv_controller.go#L1110

It looks like client-go throttling is done per rest client, so a lot of GETs could cause UPDATEs to get throttled:
https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/fb57080e069fe2efe11734a4570a92873e673c35/staging/src/k8s.io/client-go/rest/request.go#L624

### What did you expect to happen?

Released PVs should be less important than binding new PVCs

### How can we reproduce it (as minimally and precisely as possible)?

Create thousands of Released PVs in a cluster, try to bind a new PVC

title: Running pods with devices are terminated if kubelet is restarted
body:
### What happened?

In KubeVirt project, we now see a regression when running on Kubernetes `1.25.10 | 1.26.5 | 1.27.2`. If kubelet is restarted on a node, then all the existing and running workloads that use devices are terminated with `UnexpectedAdmissionError`:
```
Warning  UnexpectedAdmissionError  45s   kubelet            Allocate failed due to no healthy devices present; cannot allocate unhealthy devices devices.kubevirt.io/kvm, which is unexpected
Normal   Killing                   42s   kubelet            Stopping container compute
```
KubeVirt runs virtual machines inside pods and uses a device plugin to advertise e.g. `/dev/kvm` on the nodes.

Presumably, this PR changed the behavior: https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/pull/116376
Original issue: https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/issues/109595

### What did you expect to happen?

A potential restart of kubelet should not interrupt the running workloads.

### How can we reproduce it (as minimally and precisely as possible)?
with KubeVirt:

- run a KubeVirt VM
- `pkill kubelet`
- observe that the workload pod gets terminated

or with https://github.com/k8stopologyawareschedwg/sample-device-plugin

- make deploy
- make test-both
- pkill kubelet
- the pod gets restarted

### Anything else we need to know?

_No response_

body:
### What would you like to be added?

The ability to mount a mutable configmap without the kubelet opening a long-running constant watch for it. The pod spec should be something like this:
```yaml
spec:
  volumes:
  - name: my-config
    configMap:
      name: my-config-map
      watch: false # or true
```
Basically this is a fine-grained control for the performance benefits already achieved via immutable configmaps. Except for that it does not require the configmap to be immutable which makes it harder to update.

The description above applies to secrets as well.

### Why is this needed?

A very common approach to making static configurations in kubernetes is to store the configuration in a configmap and restart the pods that mount it automatically when the configuration changes (usually via checksum annotation in the pod template). Such configmaps are mutable by definition and trying to make them immutable complicates the setup significantly. This means a non-hacky setup requires to give up on immutable configmaps and absorb the additional load on api server as the kubelet has to watch mutable configmaps throughout the pod lifetime.

In large clusters this translates to thousands of constant watches that are theoretically unnecessary because the running pods do not react to updates coming from these watches.

We need a fine-grained control on whether a mounted configmap is watched regardless of its mutability.

title: DaemonSet does not recreate failed pods when they have deletionTimestamp
body:
/sig apps

When a terminal pod (Failed or Succeeded) has a deletionTimestamp it is ignored by DaemonSet and not recreated, because of this check: https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/master/pkg/controller/daemon/daemon_controller.go#L822-L824.

It was observed when working on what was isolated to Kubelet issue, that Kubelet would not force-delete pods in some scenarios: https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/issues/118472. 

The below reproduction steps use the 1.27.2 version with affected kubelet by the bug:

1. create kind cluster using 1.27.2 with config in `kind-config.yaml`

```yaml
kind: Cluster
apiVersion: kind.x-k8s.io/v1alpha4
nodes:
- role: control-plane
- role: worker
```

```sh
kind create cluster --config kind-config.yaml --image kindest/node:v1.27.2
```

2. create daemonset with the following spec:
```yaml
apiVersion: apps/v1
kind: DaemonSet
metadata:
 name: issue-daemonset
 namespace: default
spec:
 selector:
   matchLabels:
     name: issue-label
 template:
   metadata:
     labels:
       name: issue-label
   spec:
     os:
       name: "windows"
     containers:
     - name: ubuntu
       image:  gcr.io/google-containers/ubuntu:14.04
       command: ["/bin/sleep"]
       args: ["infinity"]
```
```sh
kubectl create -f ds.yaml
```
Observe the pod is created but marked Failed as non-admissible:
```sh 
kubectl get pods -oyaml
``` 
```sh
  status:
    message: 'Pod was rejected: Failed to admit pod as the OS field doesn''t match
      node OS'
    phase: Failed
    reason: PodOSNotSupported
    startTime: "2023-06-09T09:04:54Z"
```
3. Stop kubelet on the worker node

```sh
docker exec kind-worker systemctl stop kubelet
```
After a while observe that a replacement pod to be created by DS
```sh
kubectl get pods
```
```sh
NAME                    READY   STATUS    RESTARTS   AGE
issue-daemonset-tvrfr   0/1     Pending   0          10s
```
Observe that a replacement pod is created, but remains Pending (as the kubelet is down)

4. Delete the pending pod
```sh
kubectl delete pods/issue-daemonset-tvrfr
```
Observe that the delete hangs as Kubelet is stopped, and the pod is pending.

5. Start Kubelet again 
```sh
docker exec kind-worker systemctl start kubelet
```

Observe, that the pod now transitions to the `Failed` phase, but the delete hangs.

**Issue**: DaemonSet does not recreate a failed pod, because it has the `deletionTimestamp`. 

Note: the behavior is tricky to reproduce on a healthy system, because then the pod is typically force-deleted by Kubelet soon after transitioning to `Failed` phase.

However, it was also suggested as a potential DS issue (see [comment](https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/issues/118472#issuecomment-1579025614)), so opening the ticket to track the discussion.

title: DRA: integration with cluster autoscaler
body:
The problem that we need to solve for cluster autoscaling when the cluster uses dynamic resource allocation is to simulate how adding new nodes will affect pod scheduling. This matters when some DRA driver depends on resources on such new nodes.

One possible solution is outlined in https://github.com/kubernetes/enhancements/tree/master/keps/sig-node/3063-dynamic-resource-allocation#cluster-autoscaler

Another idea was to enable loading and calling WASM plugins. This would allow vendors to publish portable plugins and avoid inter-process communication. https://github.com/kubernetes-sigs/kube-scheduler-wasm-extension is exploring that as alternative for normal scheduler plugins. However, WASM has several challenges, primarily that all data exchanged between host and plugin guest needs to be encoded and decoded, which makes one of the goals (similar performance and overhead as built-in plugins) impossible.

title: DRA: delayed allocation: deallocate after use
body:
When a ResourceClaim:
- uses delayed allocation
- does not get created for a specific pod (i.e. not from a template)

then it currently gets allocated and remains allocated until:
- scheduling of a pod fails because the node originally chosen for the allocation isn't suitable, in which case the scheduler triggers deallocation via `claim.status.deallocationRequested`
- the user deletes the claim

What we want instead is that deallocation gets triggered when the last user of such an allocated claim gets removed from `claim.status.reservedFor`. To avoid races, deallocation must be done through `deallocationRequested`.

This can be implemented either as a controller or directly in the API server.
