title: Desired behavior of a startup failed restartable init container in a pod with `restartPolicy` set to `Never`
body:
When we use v1.28.0 with `SidecarContainers` feature,
(restartable init container = init container with container `restartPolicy` of `Always`)

a restartable init container, in a pod with `restartPolicy` set to `Never`, restarts when its `startupProbe` fails.

This is inconsistent with the [KEP](https://github.com/kubernetes/enhancements/tree/master/keps/sig-node/753-sidecar-containers#proposal),

> During the sidecar startup stage the restart behavior will be similar to init containers. If Pod restartPolicy is Never, sidecar container failed during startup will NOT be restarted and the whole Pod will fail. If Pod restartPolicy is Always or OnFailure, it will be restarted.

What should happen if a restartable init container in a pod with `restartPolicy` set to `Never` fails the `startupProbe`?

```yaml
apiVersion: batch/v1    
kind: Job    
metadata:    
  name: test-restartable-init    
  namespace: default    
spec:    
  template:    
    spec:    
      initContainers:    
      - command:    
        - sleep    
        - infinity    
        image: ubuntu    
        imagePullPolicy: Always    
        name: restartable-init    
        restartPolicy: Always    
        startupProbe:    
          exec:    
            command:    
              - "/bin/false"    
      containers:    
      - command:    
        - sleep    
        - 60s    
        image: ubuntu                                                                                                                                                                                       
        imagePullPolicy: Always                                                                                                                                                                             
        name: regular                                                                                                                                                                                          
      restartPolicy: Never
```

We may need a way for a job to recreate a pod (not restarting a container) if its restartable init container fails the startup.

Right now, I have three ways in mind.

1. Original KEP: Let a restartable init container not restart if it fails the startup and the pod's `restartPolicy` is `Never`.
1. Current implementation: We don't need this use case.
1. Introduce another `ContainerRestartPolicy` called `AlwaysAfterStartUp`.

cc @SergeyKanzhelev @tzneal @matthyx

title: Expose metrics for the `/godebug/non-default-behavior/*` go runtime metrics
body:
Recently, as part of go1.21's [extended backwards compatibility changes](https://go.dev/blog/compat), the [runtime/metrics](https://pkg.go.dev/runtime/metrics) packages [exposes metrics](https://pkg.go.dev/runtime/metrics#hdr-Supported_metrics) on the usage of codepaths that depend on non-default values of GODEBUG settings (see metrics of the form /godebug/non-default-behavior/*).

These metrics, IMO, are an excellent addition complementing the new minimum 2 year period of GODEBUG settings, and can help give users confidence in moving away from non-default GODEBUG settings eventually based on these metrics.

In the past, we've added custom metrics in Kubernetes for tracking usage of these non-default GODEBUG settings: https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/pull/109024. Once these go runtime metrics are exposed, we can deprecate the metrics added in https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/pull/109024.

This will be done in 2 stages:
- [ ] Add the `/godebug/non-default-behavior/*` metrics to the go collector in `client_golang`: https://github.com/prometheus/client_golang/issues/1337
- [ ] Use these newly added metrics in the go collector in the metrics [registry](https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/973ea2d376267d2fe1017f2f1dca94390dab702d/staging/src/k8s.io/component-base/metrics/legacyregistry/registry.go#L54C1-L55)

xref slack thread: https://kubernetes.slack.com/archives/C20HH14P7/p1693312274630799 

/sig architecture instrumentation
/assign 
/cc @dgrisonnet @liggitt

title: Add the skip return status support for PreEnqueue, and won't run PreFilter if PreEnqueue returned a Skip status
body:
### What would you like to be added?

Add the skip return status support for PreEnqueue, and won't run PreFilter if PreEnqueue returned a Skip status

### Why is this needed?

We have skip status for PreFilter to return, and when we skip prefilter, the following filter will not run, but we don't have skip choice for PreEnqueue, we'd better add this. 

After we support this:
When we skip for the preEnqueue, we can skip add the pod to activeQueue, it's more reasonable and saving time for plugin customer scheduler to optimize.

title: ValidatingAdmissionPolicy: variable expression type not recognized as return type in expression that evaluates the variable
body:
### What would you like to be added?

Variables field is added to ValidatingAdmissionPolicy in 1.28. Currently the usage of variables would expect a operator associated. 
e.g. (thanks to Mariam Fahmy for raising the issue)
```
apiVersion: admissionregistration.k8s.io/v1beta1
kind: ValidatingAdmissionPolicy
metadata:
  name: "chech-deployment-labels"
spec:
  matchConstraints:
    resourceRules:
    - apiGroups:   ["apps"]
      apiVersions: ["v1"]
      operations:  ["CREATE", "UPDATE"]
      resources:   ["deployments"]
  variables:
    - name: environment
      expression: "has(object.metadata.labels) && 'env' in object.metadata.labels && object.metadata.labels['env'] == 'prod'"
  validations:
    - expression: "variables.environment"
      message: "Deployment labels must be env=prod"
```
Above will fail with error: 
```
The ValidatingAdmissionPolicy "chech-deployment-labels" is invalid: spec.validations[0].expression: Invalid value: "variables.environment": must evaluate to bool
```
Meanwhile the `- expression: "variables.environment == true"` will pass.

The reason is when variables be evaluated to non dyn type(like bool or string), it will require special handling(like casting) since we use dyn type everywhere. 

### Why is this needed?

It might confuse user.

title: Transient Driver Registration on the CSINode can Result in Missed NodeUnstageVolume RPCs During Pod Migration
body:
### What happened?

In `unmountDetachDevices` (see [here](https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/03126c5465879491be33d5064e6f6f1c4ff2a276/pkg/kubelet/volumemanager/reconciler/reconciler_common.go#L279-L316)) we have the following code that will ultimately dispatch `NodeUnstageVolume` RPCs to the underlying CSI plugin.

Here is a pseudo-code representation of the current logic:

```
function unmountDetachDevices
	for all unmounted volumes in ASoW
		if volume not in DSoW &&
		   not operation pending on volume
			if device is mounted globally or
			   device is mounted uncertain
				Case A:
				unmount device
				(this will kick off the NodeUnstageVolume RPC; we want to be here)
			else
				Case B:
				just remove volume from ASoW
				(general badness since we don't issue a NodeUnstageVolume RPC)
```

In our testbeds, we have observed a number of occurrences where we fall into `Case B` when the CSI Node plugin for a particular driver is being bounced, which leads to the volumemanager failing to dispatch the `NodeUnstageVolume` RPC. If the pod migrates to another node, this will leave behind a Zombie LUN in our testbeds (we're using iSCSI).

A Zombie LUN can and often does result in corruption when other pods later migrate to the node in question.

Based on testing that we conducted, we discovered that this case occurs because the device is marked as unmounted.

Initially, we see the device marked as uncertain during reconstruction.

However, if the CSI Node driver pod is bounced in the exact window when a `NodeStageVolume` RPC is issued, then we end up [here](https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/03126c5465879491be33d5064e6f6f1c4ff2a276/pkg/volume/util/operationexecutor/operation_generator.go#L777C1-L798C2).

There we check to see if the error encountered is a “transient error” or a “final error”; if a “final error” is encountered, then the device state transitions from uncertain to unmounted. That is what is happening in our case.

The error is generated when the CSIClient cannot find the requested driver [here](https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/03126c5465879491be33d5064e6f6f1c4ff2a276/pkg/volume/csi/csi_client.go#L158C1-L161C3).

The driver registration code is socket based; based on our testing, if the Node plugin goes down for any reason the driver registration is removed from the CSINode.

Now for the `NodePublishVolume` path, this is mitigated by wrapping the error in a transient error [here](https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/03126c5465879491be33d5064e6f6f1c4ff2a276/pkg/volume/csi/csi_mounter.go#L109C3-L109C3) (I assume to avoid such state transitions?):

```
	csi, err := c.csiClientGetter.Get()
	if err != nil {
		return volumetypes.NewTransientOperationFailure(log("mounter.SetUpAt failed to get CSI client: %v", err))
	}
```

Based on our testing to date, adding parity [here](https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/03126c5465879491be33d5064e6f6f1c4ff2a276/pkg/volume/csi/csi_attacher.go#L290) to the `NodeStageVolume` path would help us avoid Zombie LUNs in our test setups due to missing `NodeUnstageVolume` calls:

```
	// lets check if node/unstage is supported
	if c.csiClient == nil {
		c.csiClient, err = newCsiDriverClient(csiDriverName(csiSource.Driver))
		if err != nil {
			return errors.New(log("attacher.MountDevice failed to create newCsiDriverClient: %v", err))
		}
	}
	csi := c.csiClient
```

This can be fixed by also wrapping this error in a transient error.

### What did you expect to happen?

We expected to see a `NodeUnstageVolume` call coming to the underlying NodePlugin (once it was finally back up).

### How can we reproduce it (as minimally and precisely as possible)?

* Force reconstruction on a node.
* Take down the CSI node plugin on the node while pods are mounting.
* Try to migrate the pod to another node; the underlying machinery will correctly wait for the plugin to come back up before proceeding.
* Later, bring up the CSI node plugin.
* While the pod migration might be successful, a `NodeUnstageVolume` should be missing if the correct timing windows were hit.

### Anything else we need to know?

_No response_

title: AdmissionWebhook MatchConditions cause flaking tests all around suite
body:
### Which jobs are flaking?

All e2e suites that allow concurrent execution. 
`pull-kubernetes-e2e-gce`, `pull-kubernetes-e2e-kind-kms`, etc

### Which tests are flaking?

All tests that involve cluster-scoped resources. See example run.

### Since when has it been flaking?

since https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/pull/118319

### Testgrid link

_No response_

### Reason for failure (if possible)

The MatchCondition expressions in https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/pull/118319 look like `object.metadata.namespace == 'production'`. reference to `namespace` will error for a cluster-scoped object without `namespace`. This problem will cause rejection if (1) MatchCondition tests are running (2) a concurrent test involves cluster-scoped objects.

Example run: https://prow.k8s.io/view/gs/kubernetes-jenkins/pr-logs/pull/120008/pull-kubernetes-e2e-gce/1696859184227684352/

### Anything else we need to know?

Some candidate solutions:
- Mark the tests in question as `[Distributive]`
- Limit down webhooks to match only a testing namespace, with MatchConstraints, and test something other than namespace in MatchCondition field.

### Relevant SIG(s)

/sig api-machinery

title: Node Graceful Shutdown is taking too long
body:
### What happened?

Pods usually have a 30s grace period when they do not define a terminationGracePeriodSeconds for termination. When NodeGraceful Shutdown is enabled the grace period gets set to the ShutdownGracePeriodSeconds, which is configured by the Kubelet. Let's say the Kubelet is configured with a ShutdownGracePeriodSeconds of 65 minutes. This means that pods without a termination grace period can terminate with a grace period of 65 minutes.

The Kubelet configuration includes:

```
...
shutdownGracePeriod: 65m
shutdownGracePeriodCriticalPods: 35m
```

alternatively, this alternate configuration does not work either:
```
...
shutdownGracePeriodByPodPriority:
  - priority: 0
    shutdownGracePeriodSeconds: 300
  - priority: 10000
    shutdownGracePeriodSeconds: 600
  - priority: 2000000000
    shutdownGracePeriodSeconds: 1200
  - priority: 2000001000
    shutdownGracePeriodSeconds: 1200
```

The Kubernetes E2E tests timeout when this configuration is applied as the default, since many E2E tests and pods do not set a terminationGracePeriodSeconds field.

The fix is to set the [graceful termination](https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/dd6bc2548e008e5d49a62dff73af1aa18712a1cb/pkg/kubelet/nodeshutdown/nodeshutdown_manager_linux.go#L368C1-L368C1) to 30 seconds by default, and allow the shutdown code to override the [grace period](https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/dd6bc2548e008e5d49a62dff73af1aa18712a1cb/pkg/kubelet/nodeshutdown/nodeshutdown_manager_linux.go#L372) if the pod sets one.

### What did you expect to happen?

I expect pods without a terminationGracePeriodSeconds to be terminated after 30 seconds with a large `shutdownGracePeriod` set within Kubelet.

### How can we reproduce it (as minimally and precisely as possible)?

Configure Kubelet with this config:

```
...
shutdownGracePeriod: 65m
shutdownGracePeriodCriticalPods: 35m
```

Create a pod without a terminationGracePeriodSeconds and observe the 65m grace period used.

title: Kubectl wait timeout flag is ignored when going through reverse proxy
body:
### What happened?

When using wait with the timeout flag like `kubectl wait pods -n default --all --for condition=Ready --timeout=9s -v=9` and with a kubeconfig points to rancher which uses the reverse proxy to contact the kube-api, the timeout flag is ignored. 

When debugging kubectl I noticed it is being stuck at https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/master/staging/src/k8s.io/client-go/tools/cache/listwatch.go#L111. When looking at the verbose output the watch request hangs where as when pointing directly at the kube-api endpoint we get an initial response for `GET https://<rancher-url>/k8s/clusters/local/api/v1/namespaces/default/pods?allowWatchBookmarks=true&fieldSelector=metadata.name%3Dasdfasdf-7c8566c66c-mvtf4&resourceVersion=7528907&timeoutSeconds=519&watch=true`.

The issue no longer happens if I use set the key `use-http2` to "false" in the nginx-ingress-controller configmap

We know this issue happens with RKE, and RKE2. It does not happen with K3s. The majors differences between these two sets is that RKE and RKE2 use the nginx-ingress-controller. K3s does not use the nginx-ingress-controller and uses traefik instead. K3s has custom kube-api logic while RKE and RKE2 do not.

### What did you expect to happen?

Normally in kubectl the code at https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/master/staging/src/k8s.io/client-go/tools/cache/listwatch.go#L111 returns a watch interface nearly immediately and the kubectl verbose output shows a near immediate response from the watch request.

### How can we reproduce it (as minimally and precisely as possible)?

Provision an rke cluster with the following cluster.yml:
```
kubernetes_version: v1.25.12-rancher1-1
nodes:
  - address: <node-ip>
    ssh_key_path: <ssh-path>

title: Should we remove `volumesNeedReportedInUse` for reconstructed volumes?
body:
### What would you like to be added/removed?

remove [`volumesNeedReportedInUse`](https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/master/pkg/kubelet/volumemanager/reconciler/reconciler_common.go#L148)for reconstructed volumes and [corresponding reconciler code](https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/master/pkg/kubelet/volumemanager/reconciler/reconciler_new.go#L69-L74) and [reconstruction code](https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/master/pkg/kubelet/volumemanager/reconciler/reconstruct_new.go#L98)

### Why is this needed?

`volumesNeedReportedInUse` was introduced in https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/pull/60888 to fix https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/issues/60645. 

This is to overcome the situation that volume is added to DSW at first and then deleted before it is added to ASW, which causes mounted volume neither in DSW nor ASW and won't execute unmount/detach: https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/issues/60645#issuecomment-370757877 

The reason the volume cannot be added to ASW in time is [because it is not marked as `reported in use` in DSW](https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/master/pkg/kubelet/volumemanager/reconciler/reconciler_common.go#L242) , which is [updated in an async goroutine](https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/master/pkg/kubelet/kubelet_node_status.go#L579).

However, there is another PR https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/pull/61071 also solved the issue. What it did is to check 
whether ASW already has the volume before deleting it from DSW, this makes sure that volume can be detached/unmounted after it is deleted from DSW.

I suggest that we can keep the second solution and remove `volumesNeedReportedInUse` related code to make the reconstruction process and reconcile loop cleaner?

title: alpha feature gate: LegacyServiceAccountTokenCleanUp failed to get configmap kube-apiserver-legacy-service-account-token-tracking
body:
### What happened?

installed k8s 1.28.1, 
and enable controller manager's feature gate LegacyServiceAccountTokenCleanUp as below:
   - --feature-gates=LegacyServiceAccountTokenCleanUp=true
   - --legacy-service-account-token-clean-up-period=1h

Then controller-manager shall be restarted, but in the log it shows error
```
I0831 08:04:39.997150       1 legacy_serviceaccount_token_cleaner.go:101] "Starting legacy service account token cleaner controller"
I0831 08:04:39.997165       1 shared_informer.go:311] Waiting for caches to sync for legacy-service-account-token-cleaner
I0831 08:04:40.297417       1 shared_informer.go:318] Caches are synced for legacy-service-account-token-cleaner
E0831 08:04:40.304939       1 legacy_serviceaccount_token_cleaner.go:119] "Getting lastest possible tracked_since time" err="configmaps \"kube-apiserver-legacy-service-account-token-tracking\" is forbidden: User \"system:serviceaccount:kube-system:legacy-service-account-token-cleaner\" cannot get resource \"configmaps\" in API group \"\" in the namespace \"kube-system\""
```
If manually binding a clusterrole to the serviceaccount:kube-system:legacy-service-account-token-cleaner and restart controller-manager, there is no such error then.

Please let me know whether I missed anything or this is an issue.

and one more, 
since the "kubernetes.io/legacy-token-last-used:" is recorded as dateOnly base,
so the clean shall take effect at least 1 day later？
labels:
    kubernetes.io/legacy-token-last-used: "2023-08-31"

and since DefaultCleanerSyncInterval = 24 * time.Hour, the cleaner works every 24 hours?
looks no way to change the default now by the user self?

### What did you expect to happen?

no controller-manager log error when enabling feature gate LegacyServiceAccountTokenCleanUp

### How can we reproduce it (as minimally and precisely as possible)?

just install k8s 1.28.1 and enable the feature gate LegacyServiceAccountTokenCleanUp

title: storage fuse process managed by pod/container cgroup
body:
### What would you like to be added?

fuse process's cpu/memory also should be added into the pod and container cgroup limit.

### Why is this needed?

Glusterfs volume, for example, the fuse process's parent process is 1. So it not add into the pod or container cgroup. But when large IO into the volume, the fuse process also using many memory and cpu:
//top  
13143 root      20   0 9302628   3.7g   6960 S  30.2   1.0  32960:40 glusterfs                                                                                                                                                                   
//cat /proc/13143/status  |grep -i rss
VmRSS:   3877220 kB
RssAnon:         3870260 kB
RssFile:            6960 kB
RssShmem:              0 kB

Due to these resource not added into cgroup limit. That might impact pod schedule and eviction.

These projects have all been listed on the [`unwanted_modules.json`]([a5fff9a](https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/commit/a5fff9a5d09422cb8632777d797b809595374b87)) (commit is HEAD at the time of this issue).

Depending on how the Gorilla project stabilizes itself, perhaps these entries can be removed from the unwanted_modules file.

title: evanphx/json-patch used by 1.28 drops a fix included in 1.27
body:
https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/pull/118384 updated evanphx/json-patch from 4.12.0 to 5.6.0, but `v5.6.0+incompatible` is *older* than `v4.12.0+incompatible` (both were tagged on master, and the `+incompatible` bit means this is referencing the content in the root of the repo and not the content inside the `v5` subdirectory) ... and dropped the following fix:

https://github.com/evanphx/json-patch/compare/v5.6.0...v4.12.0

This probably regresses https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/pull/105896

It's not clear why that PR bumped to 5.6.0, or if there's a newer commit we can use on master that will result in a pseudoversion off the 5.6.0 stream.

(We can't actually switch to /v5 of the module without also picking up v5 content that caused us compatibility problems in the past (https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/pull/91622#issuecomment-637087847))

/kind regression
/priority critical-urgent
/sig api-machinery
/assign @jefftree

title: Flag to Disable the 6-minute Force Detach Window
body:
### What happened?

Certain online upgrade workflows might need to restart kubernetes as a part of their upgrade procedure. This can lead to the following sequence:
* As a part of draining a kubernetes node, a pod might get deleted.
* The unmount of a pod could take more than 6 minutes.
* If the node is deemed unhealthy when the 6 minute timer fires for the pod being deleted (for example, because kubelet is still restarting), then the underlying PV will be force detached (via a `ControllerUnpublishVolume` RPC)

These workflows would likely benefit from disabling this feature in lieu of the Non-Graceful Node Shutdown feature that hit GA in kubernetes 1.28 (see [here](https://kubernetes.io/blog/2023/08/16/kubernetes-1-28-non-graceful-node-shutdown-ga/) for more details).

When these issues are encountered in our testbeds, we are left with Zombie iSCSI LUNs. If pods end up migrating to a node with such a Zombie LUN present, those pods might end up attaching themselves to the Zombie LUN leading to data corruption.

This data corruption has caused a number of our cluster-management applications to lose all access to their data, requiring them to be deployed from scratch (occasionally causing downtime for the entire cluster).

### What did you expect to happen?

The ControllerUnpublishVolume request to wait indefinitely until NodeUnstageVolume has succeeded.

### How can we reproduce it (as minimally and precisely as possible)?

See the “What happened?” section for more details.

title: Inability to receive WatchBookmarks from the etcd storage implementation
body:
### What happened?

In general, clients can request `WatchBookmark` events by specifying the `allowWatchBookmarks` query parameter. However, the server is not obliged to deliver any `WatchBookmark` events, as described in https://github.com/kubernetes/enhancements/tree/master/keps/sig-api-machinery/956-watch-bookmark#proposal

The motivation for this approach is that the frequency of `WatchBookmark` events from a storage system like etcd can be very high. As the number of watch requests increases, so does the server load.

In practice, watch requests destined for the watch cache will receive the events, while those destined for the etcd storage implementation will not.

I would like all storage implementations to be compatible and provide the same set of capabilities. This would make life easier for developers and end users, as the behaviour of the system would be consistent regardless of the actual storage used to handle a request.

### What did you expect to happen?

I would like all storage implementations to be compatible and provide the same set of capabilities. This would make life easier for developers and end users, as the behaviour of the system would be consistent regardless of the actual storage used to handle a request.

### How can we reproduce it (as minimally and precisely as possible)?

Today when you do `k get --raw '/api/v1/namespaces/default/events?watch=true&allowWatchBookmarks=true'` against a cluster built from the `master` branch you won't get any bookmark events.

body:
There are some cases when kube-proxy has to exit and restart, in order to do that we panic, but this has the problem that the log output shows a literal "panic" message and engineers, support, customers and automation gets confused, thinking that is a problem when is the expected behavior.

 , we can replace `panic` by `klog.FlushAndExit`

body:
### What would you like to be added?

I would like to add an AddGoFlags function to k8s.io/component-base/featuregate, [similar to the one found in k8s.io/component-base/logs/api/v1](https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/v1.28.1/staging/src/k8s.io/component-base/logs/api/v1/options.go#L308-L311).

### Why is this needed?

Some Kubernetes-related applications, such as [CSI Sidecar](https://github.com/kubernetes-csi/livenessprobe/blob/v2.10.0/cmd/livenessprobe/main.go#L122-L124), may not necessarily use the pflag package.

The k8s.io/component-base/logs/api/v1 package offers an [AddGoFlags function](https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/v1.28.1/staging/src/k8s.io/component-base/logs/api/v1/options.go#L308-L311) that accommodates go flag. However, a similar function is currently missing in k8s.io/component-base/featuregate.

Adding an AddGoFlags function to k8s.io/component-base/featuregate would enable applications to use k8s.io/component-base/featuregate while utilizing go flag. This would be beneficial, especially since [k8s.io/component-base/logs/api/v1 has feature gate settings related to structured logging](https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/master/staging/src/k8s.io/component-base/logs/api/v1/kube_features.go#L58-L70).

title: "kubectl delete pod" doesn't kill pod's process immediately when specifying --grace-period=0
body:
### What happened?

As far as we read the help of "kubectl delete", it looks like that --grace-period=0 immediately kills Pod's processes.
```
    --force=false:
        If true, immediately remove resources from API and bypass graceful deletion. Note that immediate deletion of
        some resources may result in inconsistency or data loss and requires confirmation.

    --grace-period=-1:
        Period of time in seconds given to the resource to terminate gracefully. Ignored if negative. Set to 1 for
        immediate shutdown. Can only be set to 0 when --force is true (force deletion).
```

In fact, processes gets killed if we set --grace-period=0 in ver1.18.
But it seems that the behehavior got changed between ver1.18 and ver1.27.

- ver1.18 ... grace-period=0 killes Pod's processes immediately
- ver1.27 ... grace-period=0 sends SIGTERM to Pod's processes first, then wait for Pod's terminationGracePeriodSeconds before sending SIGKILL. As a result, when I execute `kubectl delete pod grace-period=0 --force` , message "pod pod-name force deleted" is shown, but pod's process is not killed immediately. It lives during `terminationGracePeriodSeconds` .



### What did you expect to happen?

when execute "kubectl delete pod --force --grace-period=0" , process will have been deleted immediately unless wating during `terminationGracePeriodSeconds`

### How can we reproduce it (as minimally and precisely as possible)?

nginx-pod.yaml:
```
apiVersion: v1
kind: Pod
metadata:
  name: nginx
spec:
  terminationGracePeriodSeconds: 300
  containers:
  - name: nginx
    image: nginx:1.14.2
    command: [ 'sleep', '12345']
    ports:
    - containerPort: 80
```

title: Data loss due to node stage call missing during pod start up
body:
### What happened?

Steps done:
1. Create a pvc
2. Create a deployment consuming this pvc
3. Deployment pods we up and running, fio workload was running in this pod
4. Power off all the worker nodes for 20 min
5. Power on all the worker nodes

Old deployment pod was in terminating state. New deployment pod was created. This new pod was in running state and pvc was not mounted in the pod. Instead the root device was mounted on that location.

This can result in data loss.

Analyzing the dumps on the node were this pod was scheduled found below error message

[root@r7515-048-vm14 ~]# kubectl get po -n default
NAME                             READY   STATUS    RESTARTS   AGE
deployment-1-9b6cd7f9d-6wf2t     1/1     Running   0          3h33m
deployment-1-9b6cd7f9d-ljf8h     1/1     Running   0          3h33m

[root@r7515-048-vm14 ~]# kubectl exec -it deployment-1-9b6cd7f9d-6wf2t -n default – bash
[root@deployment-1-9b6cd7f9d-6wf2t /]# mount | grep podvol
/dev/mapper/rhel-root on /podvol type xfs (rw,relatime,attr2,inode64,logbufs=8,logbsize=32k,noquota)

/podvol was meant to mount the pvc instead the root device is mounted.

In the /var/log/messages of worker node were the pod was running found below messages

Aug 31 09:50:37 r7515-048-vm15 kubelet[1328]: E0831 09:50:37.105494    1328 nestedpendingoperations.go:348] Operation for "{volumeName:kubernetes.io/csi/org.veritas.infoscale^clust_1200/vrts_kube_dg-1200/vol_nzr0o08a4hy4t439ot50 podName: nodeName:}" failed. No retries permitted until 2023-08-31 09:50:37.605464638 +0530 IST m=+15.403186676 (durationBeforeRetry 500ms). Error: MountVolume.SetUp failed for volume "pvc-6627dab2-22cf-4347-ae96-90d13c5ecbff" (UniqueName: "kubernetes.io/csi/org.veritas.infoscale^clust_1200/vrts_kube_dg-1200/vol_nzr0o08a4hy4t439ot50") pod "deployment-1-9b6cd7f9d-6wf2t" (UID: "d4c33241-44d2-4f34-acdb-fced39e7b7f5") : kubernetes.io/csi: mounter.SetUpAt failed to get CSI client: driver name org.veritas.infoscale not found in the list of registered CSI drivers

After going through the Kubernetes csi code, the flow is as follows

GenerateMountVolumeFunc() checks for the device mount state and if the device is not mounted on the globalmount it calls attacher to mount the device. Attacher MountDevice takes care of nodeStage.

csi_mounter SetUp is called later which in turn calls nodePublish.

GenerateMountVolumeFunc()
...
                if volumeDeviceMounter != nil && actualStateOfWorld.GetDeviceMountState(volumeToMount.VolumeName) != Devi     ceGloballyMounted

{ ...                          // Mount device to global mount path                          err = volumeDeviceMounter.MountDevice(..) ..                       }
                 mountErr := volumeMounter.SetUp()

Corresponding code links

SetUp():  — Node publish https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/83f2d89dc987e152f27b31bf630c58ce855d954d/pkg/volume/csi/csi_mounter.go#L99

MountDevice(): — Node stage

https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/83f2d89dc987e152f27b31bf630c58ce855d954d/pkg/volume/csi/csi_attacher.go#L270

GenerateMountVolumeFunc() 

https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/83f2d89dc987e152f27b31bf630c58ce855d954d/pkg/volume/util/operationexecutor/operation_generator.go#L533

 On the same node there was a umount request for the same pvc. 

Aug 31 09:50:26 r7515-048-vm15 kubelet[1328]: E0831 09:50:26.293518    1328 nestedpendingoperations.go:348] Operation for "{volumeName:kubernetes.io/csi/org.veritas.infoscale^clust_1200/vrts_kube_dg-1200/vol_nzr0o08a4hy4t439ot50 podName:d4ab7809-56d7-4568-bb5d-898827d8f7c0 nodeName:}" failed. No retries permitted until 2023-08-31 09:50:26.793478948 +0530 IST m=+4.591200976 (durationBeforeRetry 500ms). Error: UnmountVolume.TearDown failed for volume "pvc-6627dab2-22cf-4347-ae96-90d13c5ecbff" (UniqueName: "kubernetes.io/csi/org.veritas.infoscale^clust_1200/vrts_kube_dg-1200/vol_nzr0o08a4hy4t439ot50") pod "d4ab7809-56d7-4568-bb5d-898827d8f7c0" (UID: "d4ab7809-56d7-4568-bb5d-898827d8f7c0") : kubernetes.io/csi: Unmounter.TearDownAt failed to get CSI client: driver name org.veritas.infoscale not found in the list of registered CSI drivers

After node power on there was both unmount and mount request for same volume. 

In the csi node previous logs found that this pod id matches with the previous app pod.

ts=2023-08-31T04:03:56.907Z level=info logger=driver host=r7515-048-vm15.vxindia.veritas.com:infoscale-csi-node-f55mp msg="NodePublishVolume request for volume" volume=vol_nzr0o08a4hy4t439ot50 source=/var/lib/kubelet/plugins/kubernetes.io/csi/org.veritas.infoscale/74d85482fcfb3089adf2e874147ed0b7172594ca3baa13469b943b080efa19a6/globalmount target=/var/lib/kubelet/pods/d4ab7809-56d7-4568-bb5d-898827d8f7c0/volumes/kubernetes.io~csi/pvc-6627dab2-22cf-4347-ae96-90d13c5ecbff/mount

When the csi pods were available, umount call completed successfully.

Aug 31 09:50:45 r7515-048-vm15 kubelet[1328]: I0831 09:50:45.199404    1328 reconciler.go:211] "operationExecutor.UnmountVolume started for volume \"pvc-6627dab2-22cf-4347-ae96-90d13c5ecbff\" (UniqueName: \"kubernetes.io/csi/org.veritas.infoscale^clust_1200/vrts_kube_dg-1200/vol_nzr0o08a4hy4t439ot50\") pod \"d4ab7809-56d7-4568-bb5d-898827d8f7c0\" (UID: \"d4ab7809-56d7-4568-bb5d-898827d8f7c0\") "

Aug 31 09:50:45 r7515-048-vm15 kubelet[1328]: I0831 09:50:45.210494    1328 operation_generator.go:890] UnmountVolume.TearDown succeeded for volume "kubernetes.io/csi/org.veritas.infoscale^clust_1200/vrts_kube_dg-1200/vol_nzr0o08a4hy4t439ot50" (OuterVolumeSpecName: "pvc-6627dab2-22cf-4347-ae96-90d13c5ecbff") pod "d4ab7809-56d7-4568-bb5d-898827d8f7c0" (UID: "d4ab7809-56d7-4568-bb5d-898827d8f7c0"). InnerVolumeSpecName "pvc-6627dab2-22cf-4347-ae96-90d13c5ecbff". PluginName "kubernetes.io/csi", VolumeGidValue ""

There can be a race condition, when mount request checked for the volume state it was mounted. It did not attempt staging and directly tried publish. Umount request unmounted the device. 

### What did you expect to happen?

Deployment pod consuming the pvc should be staged and published before marking the pod as ready.

### How can we reproduce it (as minimally and precisely as possible)?

We are working on reproducing the issue.

### Anything else we need to know?

_No response_

Identifying an untested feature Using APISnoop ## Untested Endpoints According to following APIsnoop query, there are three StorageClass endpoints that are untested. ```sql-mode select endpoint, path, kind from testing.untested_stable_endpoint where eligible is true and endpoint ilike '%StorageClass' order by kind, endpoint limit 10; ``` ```example endpoint | path | kind ---------------------------------------+-----------------------------------------------+-------------- deleteStorageV1CollectionStorageClass | /apis/storage.k8s.io/v1/storageclasses | StorageClass patchStorageV1StorageClass | /apis/storage.k8s.io/v1/storageclasses/{name} | StorageClass replaceStorageV1StorageClass | /apis/storage.k8s.io/v1/storageclasses/{name} | StorageClass (3 rows) ``` - - - ## Endpoints that are not Conformance tested - - - - # API Reference and feature documentation - [Kubernetes API Reference Docs](https://kubernetes.io/docs/reference/kubernetes-api/) - [Kubernetes API / Config and Storage Resources / StorageClass](https://kubernetes.io/docs/reference/kubernetes-api/config-and-storage-resources/storage-class-v1/) - [client-go - StorageClass](https://github.com/kubernetes/client-go/blob/master/kubernetes/typed/storage/v1/storageclass.go) # Test outline ``` Scenario: Test the lifecycle of a StorageClass Given the e2e test has created the settings for a StorageClass When the test creates the StorageClass Then the requested action is accepted without any error Given the e2e test has created the StorageClass When the test reads the StorageClass Then the requested action is accepted without any error Given the e2e test has retrived a StorageClass When the test patches the StorageClass with a new label Then the requested action is accepted without any error And the test finds the new StorageClass label with the required "patched" value Given the e2e test has patched the StorageClass When the test deletes the StorageClass Then the requested action is accepted without any error And the deletion of the StorageClass is confirmed Given the e2e test has no StorageClass When the test recreates a new StorageClass Then the requested action is accepted without any error Given the e2e test has created a StorageClass When the test updates the StorageClass label Then the requested action is accepted without any error And the test finds the StorageClass label with the required "updated" value Given the e2e test has created a LabelSelector for the StorageClass When the test lists the StorageClasses with a labelSelector Then the requested action is accepted without any error And the retrieved list has a single item Given the e2e test has updated a StorageClass When the test applies the deleteCollection action with a labelSelector Then the requested action is accepted without any error And the StorageClass with the label is not found ``` # E2E Test Using a number of existing e2e test practices a new [ginkgo test](https://github.com/ii/kubernetes/blob/create-storageclass-lifecycle-test/test/e2e/storage/storageclass.go#L43-L159) has been created to provide future Conformance coverage for the 7 endpoints. The e2e logs for this test are listed below. ``` [sig-storage] StorageClasses CSI Conformance should run through the lifecycle of a StorageClass /home/ii/go/src/k8s.io/kubernetes/test/e2e/storage/storageclass.go:43 STEP: Creating a kubernetes client @ 09/05/23 23:48:05.729 Sep 5 23:48:05.729: INFO: >>> kubeConfig: /home/ii/.kube/config STEP: Building a namespace api object, basename csi-storageclass @ 09/05/23 23:48:05.736 STEP: Waiting for a default service account to be provisioned in namespace @ 09/05/23 23:48:05.758 STEP: Waiting for kube-root-ca.crt to be provisioned in namespace @ 09/05/23 23:48:05.765 STEP: Creating a StorageClass @ 09/05/23 23:48:05.772 STEP: Get StorageClass "e2e-64xnx" @ 09/05/23 23:48:05.778 STEP: Patching the StorageClass "e2e-64xnx" @ 09/05/23 23:48:05.783 STEP: Delete StorageClass "e2e-64xnx" @ 09/05/23 23:48:05.79 STEP: Confirm deletion of StorageClass "e2e-64xnx" @ 09/05/23 23:48:05.796 STEP: Create a replacement StorageClass @ 09/05/23 23:48:05.801 STEP: Updating StorageClass "e2e-v2-bg6gz" @ 09/05/23 23:48:05.806 STEP: Listing all StorageClass with the labelSelector: "e2e-v2-bg6gz=updated" @ 09/05/23 23:48:05.817 STEP: Deleting StorageClass "e2e-v2-bg6gz" via DeleteCollection @ 09/05/23 23:48:05.822 STEP: Confirm deletion of StorageClass "e2e-v2-bg6gz" @ 09/05/23 23:48:05.83 Sep 5 23:48:05.834: INFO: Waiting up to 7m0s for all (but 0) nodes to be ready STEP: Destroying namespace "csi-storageclass-7858" for this suite. @ 09/05/23 23:48:05.841 ``` # Verifying increase in coverage with APISnoop ## Listing endpoints hit by the new e2e test This query shows the following StorageClass endpoints are hit within a short period of running this e2e test. ```sql-mode select distinct substring(endpoint from '\w+') AS endpoint, right(useragent,50) AS useragent from testing.audit_event where useragent like 'e2e%should%' and release_date::BIGINT > round(((EXTRACT(EPOCH FROM NOW()))::numeric)*1000,0) - 20000 and endpoint ilike '%StorageClass%' order by endpoint limit 10; ``` ```example endpoint | useragent ---------------------------------------+---------------------------------------------------- createStorageV1StorageClass | should run through the lifecycle of a StorageClass deleteStorageV1CollectionStorageClass | should run through the lifecycle of a StorageClass deleteStorageV1StorageClass | should run through the lifecycle of a StorageClass listStorageV1StorageClass | should run through the lifecycle of a StorageClass patchStorageV1StorageClass | should run through the lifecycle of a StorageClass readStorageV1StorageClass | should run through the lifecycle of a StorageClass replaceStorageV1StorageClass | should run through the lifecycle of a StorageClass (7 rows) ``` # Final notes If a test with these calls gets merged, **test coverage will go up by 7 points** This test is also created with the goal of conformance promotion. --- /sig testing /sig architecture /area conformance

title: (umbrella issue) Define, Deprecate, Roadmap the NodeNetworkUnvailable / NetworkUnavailable:false taints, tolerations, conditions - including CNI/CloudController reccomendations
body:
TLDR,  There are many moving parts in a K8s cluster that may use / depend on 
- the  `"node.kubernetes.io/network-unavailable" condition`  and/or
- `v1.TaintNodeNetworkUnavailable taint` Condition/Taint couple 

In ambiguous/ad-hoc sorts of ways.  This makes it confusing for users and vendors to know when they should/shouldnt manipulate the values of such TCs.  

## Solution

- We may need to make more well defined taints/tolerations that say things precisely about network state.  This might break systems relying heavily on the oversimplified "NetworkUnavailable" semantics we currently have.
- We need to deprecate, re-define, and document taints/tolerations for k8s networks...  This is a several week or month process b/c it will require lots of water carrying across vendors / sig-docs/sig-net/sig-node.

*By the way, lots of water-carrying here between vendors/sig-net, might be a good "first" issue for someone whose very eager to learn about the history/semantics of K8s networking and pod scheduling, and has many weeks to dedicate !*

## Detailed Summary

(9/12 Editing this issue to update it per comments...)

Many, many issues expose the complexity of node networking readiness.
- https://github.com/antrea-io/antrea/issues/2298
- https://github.com/flannel-io/flannel/issues/1431
- https://github.com/projectcalico/calico/issues/6165
- https://github.com/projectcalico/calico/issues/5233
- https://github.com/containernetworking/cni/issues/859
- https://github.com/containernetworking/cni/issues/628

There's proposals to get **CNI Status** into the CNI specification.  For now, the most urgent need appears to be to fully 
- DEFINE the **current taints, tolerations, and expectations** that CNI, cloud provider, and others should have
- FILE **bugs** against Kuberentes and CNI/cloud provider implementations that may/may not use the taints/tolerations in Kubernetes properly
- TALK to the Multi-networking and CNI providers individually to figure out what the lowest common denominator for node networking readiness and tainting is
- WRITE a **kep** to update all of these taints, tolerations, and so on so that they are consistently aligned to the indended use (and deprecate the taints which don't have a usable definition once we consider this broader world view of K8s networking)
- Original brainstorming doc... not relevant anymore but for historical reasons:  https://docs.google.com/document/d/1xlZYVw2iu447b5Us8V8gRC5uigjrjtOCX7RgQ19Oe4/edit

# Goals

I think the goals of this issue are something like: 

- The CNI and CRI/Kubelet would have a *well defined "taint namespace"* (not literally, but, some sort of semantic boundary)... related specifically to when CNIs were ready to make pods
- There would be **comprehensive guidance for CNIs and cloud controllers** on how / when to/ when not to modify these taints conditions
- Taints/Conditions related to network readiness, would have clear well-defined meaning in **multi-networking and multi-OS** environments w/ docs on them
- There would be no **cloud specific behaviour** in K8s related to these taints and conditions
- **Maybe this means we need to entirely rethink the value of high-level, networking related taints**

```[tasklist]
### Tasks
- [ ] https://github.com/kubernetes/website/issues/43018
- [ ] https://github.com/kubernetes/website/issues/42917
```

title: PodResources API of kubelet does not report the resources allocated to restartable init containers
body:
previous discussion: https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/pull/120461#discussion_r1317515863

https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/56cc5e77a10ba156694309d9b6159d4cd42598e1/pkg/kubelet/apis/podresources/server_v1.go#L51-L86

title: [discussion] DRA plugin raises UPDATE API request in scheduling cycle
body:
DRA (DynamicResourceAllocation) plugin tries to issue a synchronous API call in Reverse():

https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/c682d2b8c59f615d6896a1b1db22a5e7a5aaa23e/pkg/scheduler/framework/plugins/dynamicresources/dynamicresources.go#L883

However, raising direct API requests in main scheduling cycle should be cautious as a blocking call may impact the overall scheduling perf & throughput. There are some solutions:

- avoid the UDPATE call totally
- change UPDATE to PATCH

Moreover, if we _have to_ use UPDATE, given UPDATE underneath compares versions and hence may fail on resource conflicts, we may pursue wrapping it in retry logic to avoid unnecessary churning in multiple scheduling cycles.

/sig scheduling
/kind feature

title: kube-apiserver instability for k8s 1.27.5
body:
### What happened?

Since upgrading to Kubernetes `1.27.5` (from 1.27.4) we have experienced outages on our `kube-apiserver` pods where their container has been restarted due to failing liveness probes.

This has caused instability, usually via a number of important components within our clusters failing leader elections due to timeouts.
There haven't been many outages, but enough to be annoying. Prior to the upgrade the cluster was pretty rock solid.

### What did you expect to happen?

Not having the kube-apiserver fail its liveness probes and have its container restarted.

### How can we reproduce it (as minimally and precisely as possible)?

I'm not sure. The problem is infrequent and no unusual activity seems to be happening on the cluster that I can detect.
For us we upgraded from version 1.27.4 to 1.27.5 of k8s.

### Anything else we need to know?

We have values set for the number of in-flight requests for the API server set, as well as the `EventRateLimit` adminission controller enabled and configured like so:
```
apiVersion: eventratelimit.admission.k8s.io/v1alpha1
kind: Configuration
limits:
- burst: 500
  qps: 250
  type: Namespace
- burst: 250
  qps: 50
  type: User
```
Prometheus metrics suggest that we are not approaching these limits when the problem occurs.
These settings have been in place for our cluster for many months now across a number of k8s versions and haven't posed any problems, but mentioned them in case they are relevant.

The control-plane nodes had plenty of free resources at the time of the problems as well, using roughly 20% of their CPU, and under half their RAM (< 4GiB used on systems with 8GiB available).

The following Gist link contains the log from the kube-apiserver after it has been restarted gathered via `kubectl logs -p` to get the logs from the container that was restarted.
It also has the output from `kube-events-exporter` showing it reporting the failed liveness probes.

The configuration of the cluster between 1.27.4 where where had no problems and 1.27.5 is pretty much the same apart from k8s itself.

title: Cloud provider implementations do not show provider-specific options in usage string
body:
### What happened?

The `NewCloudControllerManagerCommand` function in `k8s.io/cloud-provider/app/controllermanager.go` accepts an `additionalFlags` parameter which it describes as a way to "controller specific flags to be included in the complete set of controller manager flags". However, when the usage string is shown (either via `$cmd --help` or when parsing options fails), these additional options are not included in the usage string.	

This was identified via code inspection while trying to figure out what options did in `openstack-cloud-controller-manager`.

### What did you expect to happen?

For e.g. `aws-cloud-controller-manager`, the output of `aws-cloud-controller-manager --help` should include a `Tagging Controller Options` section corresponding to [the flagset registered for that command](https://github.com/kubernetes/cloud-provider-aws/blob/v1.28.1/cmd/aws-cloud-controller-manager/main.go#L67-L83). This section should in turn list all of [the options added to that flagset](https://github.com/kubernetes/cloud-provider-aws/blob/v1.28.1/pkg/controllers/options/tagging_controller.go#L30-L38).

### How can we reproduce it (as minimally and precisely as possible)?

1. Build a cloud provider executable that includes additional options, such as `aws-cloud-controller-manager`
2. Run `$cmd --help`
3. Observe the additional options are not shown in the output

title: `NetworkPolicy`: connection-oriented semantics are undocumented
body:
### What would you like to be added?

It is undocumented (on e.g., https://kubernetes.io/docs/concepts/services-networking/network-policies/ or https://network-policy-api.sigs.k8s.io/reference/spec/#policy.networking.k8s.io%2fv1alpha1) that `NetworkPolicy` rules result in a `conntrack` rule, i.e., that `NetworkPolicy`s are connection-oriented rather than packet oriented, for TCP.

For example, the egress key in the last `NetworkPolicy` is redundant:

```yaml
---
apiVersion: networking.k8s.io/v1
kind: NetworkPolicy
metadata:
  name: defaultdeny
spec:
  podSelector: {}
  policyTypes:
    - Egress
    - Ingress
---
apiVersion: networking.k8s.io/v1
kind: NetworkPolicy
metadata:
  name: http
spec:
  egress: # This entire key is redundant.
    - ports:
        - protocol: TCP
          port: '1024-65535'
  ingress:
    - ports:
        - port: '80'
          protocol: TCP
  podSelector:
    matchLabels:
      app.kubernetes.io/component: webservice
  policyTypes:
    - Ingress
    - Egress
```

The docs are misleading, for example:

https://kubernetes.io/docs/concepts/services-networking/network-policies/ 

> A pod is isolated for egress if there is any NetworkPolicy that both selects the pod and has "Egress" in its policyTypes; we say that such a policy applies to the pod for egress. When a pod is isolated for egress, **the only allowed connections from the pod are those allowed by the egress list of some NetworkPolicy that applies to the pod for egress**. The effects of those egress lists combine additively.

In truth this refers to **the only new, unestablished connections ...**.

Indeed, given https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/issues/109672 and https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/issues/120214 it seems this design choice for TCP is not protocol-independent and an undeliberate architectural design.

### Why is this needed?

Securing networks is important. The current documentation is misleading as to what rules are required in a default-deny scenario with TCP.

### What happened?

Why PatchService method is used for deleting finalizers in cloud-controller-manager,
[https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/master/staging/src/k8s.io/cloud-provider/controllers/service/controller.go#L922 ](https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/master/staging/src/k8s.io/cloud-provider/controllers/service/controller.go#L922 )
```golang
// removeFinalizer patches the service to remove finalizer.
func (c *Controller) removeFinalizer(service *v1.Service) error {
	if !servicehelper.HasLBFinalizer(service) {
		return nil
	}
	// Make a copy so we don't mutate the shared informer cache.
	updated := service.DeepCopy()
	updated.ObjectMeta.Finalizers = removeString(updated.ObjectMeta.Finalizers, servicehelper.LoadBalancerCleanupFinalizer)

	klog.V(2).Infof("Removing finalizer from service %s/%s", updated.Namespace, updated.Name)
	_, err := servicehelper.PatchService(c.kubeClient.CoreV1(), service, updated)
	return err
}
``` 
This method updates with service/status,
```golang
// PatchService patches the given service's Status or ObjectMeta based on the original and
// updated ones. Change to spec will be ignored.
func PatchService(c corev1.CoreV1Interface, oldSvc, newSvc *v1.Service) (*v1.Service, error) {
	// Reset spec to make sure only patch for Status or ObjectMeta.
	newSvc.Spec = oldSvc.Spec

	patchBytes, err := getPatchBytes(oldSvc, newSvc)
	if err != nil {
		return nil, err
	}

	return c.Services(oldSvc.Namespace).Patch(context.TODO(), oldSvc.Name, types.StrategicMergePatchType, patchBytes, metav1.PatchOptions{}, "status")

}
```
[https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/master/staging/src/k8s.io/cloud-provider/service/helpers/helper.go#L132](https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/master/staging/src/k8s.io/cloud-provider/service/helpers/helper.go#L132)
It seems to go unnoticed by the API server, resulting in the API server being unaware when the finalizer field on the service is deleted, leading to a delay in the release of service-related NodePorts.

### What did you expect to happen?

service nodeport be released promptly when service is deleted.

### How can we reproduce it (as minimally and precisely as possible)?
create a loadblancer service with nodeport seted,then delete it and recreate.
```yaml
apiVersion: v1
kind: Service
metadata:
  labels:
    testid: svc-not-tolerate-unready-5d178209-1284-4cd3-9790-ba6118c5e1ba
  name: svc-not-tolerate-unready
spec:
  allocateLoadBalancerNodePorts: true
  externalTrafficPolicy: Local
  internalTrafficPolicy: Cluster
  ports:
  - name: http
    port: 80
    protocol: TCP
    targetPort: 80
    nodePort: 30999
  selector:
    testid: svc-not-tolerate-unready-5d178209-1284-4cd3-9790-ba6118c5e1ba
  sessionAffinity: None
  type: LoadBalancer
```
```shell
[root@test-1:~]$ kubectl apply -f svc-nodeport.yaml 
The Service "svc-not-tolerate-unready" is invalid: spec.ports[0].nodePort: Invalid value: 30999: provided port is already allocated

```
cloud-controller-manager add  a finalizer on service. delete this service and then cloud-controller remove finalizer. but nodeport is not released when service deleted.
ref #87217

i change like this, it seems like releasing nodeport when service is deleted
:
[https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/master/staging/src/k8s.io/cloud-provider/controllers/service/controller.go#L922 ](https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/master/staging/src/k8s.io/cloud-provider/controllers/service/controller.go#L922 )

func PatchService(c corev1.CoreV1Interface, oldSvc, newSvc *v1.Service) (*v1.Service, error) {
	// Reset spec to make sure only patch for Status or ObjectMeta.
	newSvc.Spec = oldSvc.Spec

	patchBytes, err := getPatchBytes(oldSvc, newSvc)
	if err != nil {

	}
	if oldSvc.DeletionTimestamp != nil {
		return c.Services(oldSvc.Namespace).Patch(context.TODO(), oldSvc.Name, types.StrategicMergePatchType, patchBytes, metav1.PatchOptions{})
	}
	return c.Services(oldSvc.Namespace).Patch(context.TODO(), oldSvc.Name, types.StrategicMergePatchType, patchBytes, metav1.PatchOptions{}, "status")

title: Pods are stuck ContainerCreating after volume detach error and KCM restart
body:
### What happened?

After KCM restart, any Pod that reuses a volume that failed to detach gets stuck ContainerCreating with message:

`
User "system:node:ip-10-0-243-205.us-east-2.compute.internal" cannot get resource "volumeattachments" in API group "storage.k8s.io" at the cluster scope: no relationship found between node 'ip-10-0-243-205.us-east-2.compute.internal' and this object
`

See steps to reproduce below, it's quite a complex condition. It happens when a pod is restarted, a CSI driver "busy" (i.e. times out) + KCM restarted at a wrong time.

### What did you expect to happen?

Pods start just fine.

### How can we reproduce it (as minimally and precisely as possible)?


1. Create a Pod that uses an attachable CSI volume.
2. Delete the Pod. Make sure it unmounts successfully, but any `ControllerUnpublish` fails with a transient error, such as timeout. The external attacher continues to detach the volume at this point.
3. Stop kube-controller-manager (KCM) and start a new one. Wait for any leader election etc - it's important for the new KCM to populate A/D controller with no pod using the detaching volume. Let the A/D controller to observe detach error.
4. Create a new Pod on the same node that uses the same volume.
5. Let the CSI driver to detach the volume (i.e. stop injecting any transient errors).

At this point:

- The external attacher succeeds detaching the volume, VolumeAttachment is deleted.
- The volume is marked as attached in node status (!!!) despite no VolumeAttachment exists. A/D controller does not even try to create a new VolumeAttachment, the volume is marked as attached in its Actual State of World (ASW).
- Kubelet tries to mount the volume, but WaitForAttach fails with: `cannot get resource "volumeattachments" in API group "storage.k8s.io" at the cluster scope: no relationship found between node '127.0.0.1' and this object`, basically forever.

I created [a script with a reproducer](https://people.redhat.com/jsafrane/detach-error/).

* The script expects that the cluster is created by `hack/local-up-cluster.sh`, because it restarts KCM in the middle.
* It uses my hacked hostpath CSI driver to inject detach errors. Sources are at https://github.com/jsafrane/csi-driver-host-path/tree/hack-detach-error / the last commit(s) there.

### Anything else we need to know?

There are two issues that together lead to this situation:

1. After `Detach()` fails, [A/D controller marks the volume as fully attached](https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/887ac275a2cfb6030df80bbe3066609336fa220a/pkg/volume/util/operationexecutor/operation_generator.go#L508-L511), i.e. puts it back to `node.status.volumesAttached`.
    * With the volume in `node.status.volumesAttached`, kubelet may try to mount it, while the external attacher tries to detach it. It is not as bad as it sounds, because kubelet can't read VolumeAttachment with the deletion timestamp and it will not call `NodeStage` / `NodePublish` of un-attached volume.
2. After KCM starts, all VolumeAttachments that don't have a Pod [are marked as Uncertain](https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/887ac275a2cfb6030df80bbe3066609336fa220a/pkg/controller/volume/attachdetach/attach_detach_controller.go#L763-L763) (that's good), but also [as mounted on node](https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/887ac275a2cfb6030df80bbe3066609336fa220a/pkg/controller/volume/attachdetach/cache/actual_state_of_world.go#L370-L370) (that's probably bad).
    * When the newly started KCM re-tries to detach the volume and gets an error again, it marks the volume as fully attached (same as the previous point) and adds it to `node.status.volumesAttached`.
    * Now the volume is both mounted + attached in ASW and A/D controller actually stops here and waits forever for kubelet to unmount the volume.


### Kubernetes version

<details>
Today's k/k master, 
```console
$ kubectl version
v1.29.0-alpha.0.456+887ac275a2cfb6-dirty
```

</details>


### Cloud provider

None
</details>


### OS version

<details>
N/A, it's KCM issue.
</details>

<details>
`hack/local-up-cluster.sh`, but seen in a downstream Kubernetes distro too.
</details>

title: kube-proxy discards command line args
body:
### What happened?

https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/pull/55261 introduced a change to reload config from file and this happens after parsing all the command line flags and hence discards all the command line flags. 

https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/35199e42a41f83520e640fbfa9f409516faa7501/cmd/kube-proxy/app/server.go#L245-L259

### What did you expect to happen?

kube-proxy should respect all the command line arguments and if for some reason we need to load config from file we must do it in a way that preserves all command line flags. 

I'm trying to add three additional configuration params to kube-proxy in  https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/pull/120354
1. **conntrack-tcp-be-liberal**
2. **conntrack-udp-timeout**
3. **conntrack-udp-timeout-stream**

I'm not able to use 2 and 3 via command line args. 1 works as I'm syncing it manually.

### How can we reproduce it (as minimally and precisely as possible)?

If I comment out the following line and rebuild kube-proxy for the local kind cluster, kube-proxy fails with the following logs:

```
I0912 12:58:03.614728       1 server_others.go:367] "GetConntrackMax: using scaled conntrack-max-per-core"
I0912 12:58:03.614756       1 conntrack.go:118] "Set sysctl" entry="net/netfilter/nf_conntrack_max" value=655360
E0912 12:58:03.614765       1 server.go:557] "Error running ProxyServer" err="open /proc/sys/net/netfilter/nf_conntrack_max: permission denied"
E0912 12:58:03.614775       1 run.go:74] "command failed" err="open /proc/sys/net/netfilter/nf_conntrack_max: permission denied"
```
I guess after commenting out the following line kube-proxy actually tries to run conntrack sysctls and since kind /proc/sys is read-only for kind it fails.

https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/35199e42a41f83520e640fbfa9f409516faa7501/cmd/kube-proxy/app/server.go#L259


### Anything else we need to know?

Current Flow:

```go
// 1. initialize options
// this internally calls newKubeProxyConfiguration() which generates kube-proxy config with default values
opts := NewOptions()

// 2. add command-line flags
opts.AddFlags(fs)

// 3. complete all the required flags, read config from the file losing defaults and
// values provided by command line flags
opts.Complete()

// 4. validate all the required options
opts.Validate()

// 5. run the kube-proxy
opts.Run()
```

In step 3 we lose all the default and pflag values.

body:
### What happened?

Below was stack trace of crash:
```
kubelet[2767716]: runtime: program exceeds 10000-thread limit
kubelet[2767716]: fatal error: thread exhaustion
 kubelet[2767716]: runtime stack:

From kubelet logs, Validated around 10000 threads, majority are with this stack trace

    PID USER      PR  NI    VIRT    RES    SHR S  %CPU  %MEM     TIME+ COMMAND
2849677 root      20   0  264.2g  78.5g  64520 S  5983   3.9  10338:12 kubelet
```
### What did you expect to happen?

Kubelet not to crash and keep memory and thread footprint low


### How can we reproduce it (as minimally and precisely as possible)?

By injecting error in loginD or dbus logic, this should be reproducible.


### Anything else we need to know?

Traced down the kubelet where [these threads ](https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/master/vendor/github.com/godbus/dbus/v5/default_handler.go#L331)are getting created in Loop:
Reference to kubelet code: https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/release-1.24/pkg/kubelet/nodeshutdown/nodeshutdown_manager_linux.go#L181
 ```
// Start starts the node shutdown manager and will start watching the node for shutdown events.
func (m *managerImpl) Start() error {
	stop, err := m.start()
	if err != nil {
		return err
	}
	go func() {
		for { >>> NEVER ENDING FOR LOOP, Till m.start send stop()
			if stop != nil {
				<-stop
			}

			time.Sleep(dbusReconnectPeriod)
			klog.V(1).InfoS("Restarting watch for node shutdown events")
			stop, err = m.start()
			if err != nil {
				klog.ErrorS(err, "Unable to watch the node for shutdown events")
			}
		}
	}()

func (m *managerImpl) start() (chan struct{}, error) {
	systemBus, err := systemDbus() >>>> Created Dbus thread to deliver signal which we see in logs
	if err != nil {
		return nil, err
	}
	m.dbusCon = systemBus

	currentInhibitDelay, err := m.dbusCon.CurrentInhibitDelay()
	if err != nil {
		return nil, err        >>> If Error happens here or anywhere below, Dbus connections are not closed, thereby threads of dbus just keeps hanging
	}

      .....
       .....
	........
}
```
systemDbus() --> systemd.NewDBusCon() --> [dbus.SystemBus](https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/release-1.24/pkg/kubelet/nodeshutdown/systemd/inhibit_linux.go#L52C15-L52C31)()  --> [ConnectSystemBus()](https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/master/vendor/github.com/godbus/dbus/v5/conn.go#L132) --> [conn.Auth()](https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/master/vendor/github.com/godbus/dbus/v5/conn.go#L159) --> [go.conn.inworker()](https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/master/vendor/github.com/godbus/dbus/v5/auth.go#L118) --> [conn.HandleSign()](https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/master/vendor/github.com/godbus/dbus/v5/conn.go#L432) --> [conn.SignalHandler.DeliverSignal()](https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/master/vendor/github.com/godbus/dbus/v5/conn.go#L472) --> [signalChannelData.deliverSignal](https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/master/vendor/github.com/godbus/dbus/v5/default_handler.go#L320) (this is what we see in stack trace)

title: Kubelet log query errors "input contains unsupported characters"
body:
### What happened?

I enabled the [kubelet log query feature](https://kubernetes.io/docs/concepts/cluster-administration/system-logs/#log-query) on EKS 1.27.4 using Ubuntu 20.04.6.

When I try to query the kubelet logs or log files from the system I get the error "input contains unsupported characters"

```
kubectl get --raw "/api/v1/nodes/i-0ede67f2d75dfe308.us-west-2.compute.internal/proxy/logs/?query=snap.kubelet-eks.daemon.service"
Error from server (NotAcceptable): query: Invalid value: "snap.kubelet-eks.daemon.service": input contains unsupported characters

kubectl get --raw "/api/v1/nodes/i-0ede67f2d75dfe308.us-west-2.compute.internal/proxy/logs/?query=cloud-init.log"
Error from server (NotAcceptable): query: Invalid value: "cloud-init.log": input contains unsupported characters
```
The systemd kubelet service runs as a snap called `snap.kubelet-eks.daemon.service` and I _think_ that might be the source of this problem (running the kubelet in a snap), but I'm not sure if it's intended to work. The fact that I couldn't see /var/log file query was surprising and the error message is misleading which is why I'm opening an issue here.

I followed the same configuration steps on Amazon Linux 2 and it works as expected.


### What did you expect to happen?

Log query should work on Ubuntu or provide a clearer error message.

### How can we reproduce it (as minimally and precisely as possible)?

This should be reproducible on any Kubernetes cluster running Ubuntu with Kubelet in a snap, but this is what I did.

Install [eksdemo](https://github.com/awslabs/eksdemo) to make cluster creation and karpenter setup easier)
```
eksdemo create cluster log-testing --os Ubuntu2004 --prefix-assignment
```
Install Karpenter as a node autoscaler. This will automatically create a provisioner and AWSNodeTemplate objects.
```
eksdemo install autoscaling karpenter -c ubuntu -A Ubuntu
```
Modify the AWSNodeTemplate with userdata that can customize Ubuntu with log query enabled
```
cat << EOF | kubectl apply -f -
apiVersion: karpenter.k8s.aws/v1alpha1
kind: AWSNodeTemplate
metadata:
  name: default
spec:
  amiFamily: Ubuntu
  securityGroupSelector:
    aws:eks:cluster-name: ubuntu
  subnetSelector:
    Name: eksctl-ubuntu-cluster/SubnetPrivate*
  userData: |
    #!/bin/bash
    set -e

    # This probably isn't the best way to do this but it worked
    sed -i 's/args="$KUBELET_EXTRA_ARGS"/args="--feature-gates=NodeLogQuery=true $KUBELET_EXTRA_ARGS"/g' /etc/eks/bootstrap.sh
    sed -i '/# writes kubeReserved and evictionHard/a echo "$(jq .enableSystemLogHandler=true $KUBELET_CONFIG)" > $KUBELET_CONFIG' /etc/eks/bootstrap.sh
    sed -i '/# writes kubeReserved and evictionHard/a echo "$(jq .enableSystemLogQuery=true $KUBELET_CONFIG)" > $KUBELET_CONFIG' /etc/eks/bootstrap.sh
EOF
```
Deploy a workload that uses hostname spread to get more nodes.
```
cat << EOF | kubectl apply -f -
apiVersion: policy/v1
kind: PodDisruptionBudget
metadata:
  name: myapp
spec:
  minAvailable: "80%"
  selector:
    matchLabels:
      app: myapp
---
apiVersion: apps/v1
kind: Deployment
metadata:
  name: myapp
spec:
  replicas: 3
  selector:
    matchLabels:
      app: myapp
  template:
    metadata:
      labels:
        app: myapp
    spec:
      containers:
      - image: public.ecr.aws/eks-distro/kubernetes/pause:3.2
        name: myapp
        resources:
          requests:
            cpu: "1"
            memory: 256M
      topologySpreadConstraints:
      - labelSelector:
          matchLabels:
            app: host-zone-spread
        maxSkew: 2
        topologyKey: kubernetes.io/hostname
        whenUnsatisfiable: DoNotSchedule
      - labelSelector:
          matchLabels:
            app: host-zone-spread
        maxSkew: 5
        topologyKey: topology.kubernetes.io/zone
        whenUnsatisfiable: DoNotSchedule
EOF
```
When the new Ubuntu node is created you can log into the node with session manager. I like to use [ssm-helpers](https://github.com/disneystreaming/ssm-helpers)
```
brew install disneystreaming/tap/ssm-helpers
ssm session
# select the new node
```
You can verify that the kubelet is running and logging is enabled
```
sudo systemctl status -l snap.kubelet-eks.daemon.service
```
Now you can try to query logs
```
kubectl get --raw "/api/v1/nodes/$NODE/proxy/logs/?query=snap.kubelet-eks.daemon.service"
```


### Anything else we need to know?

This works with AL2. You can test with a different AWSNodeTemplate that uses AL2 instead
```
cat << EOF | kubectl apply -f -
apiVersion: karpenter.k8s.aws/v1alpha1
kind: AWSNodeTemplate
metadata:
  name: default
spec:
  amiFamily: AL2
  securityGroupSelector:
    aws:eks:cluster-name: ubuntu
  subnetSelector:
    Name: eksctl-ubuntu-cluster/SubnetPrivate*
  userData: |
    #!/bin/bash
    set -e

    cat << EOF > /etc/systemd/system/kubelet.service.d/90-kubelet-extra-args.conf
    [Service]
    Environment="KUBELET_EXTRA_ARGS=--feature-gates=NodeLogQuery=true $KUBELET_EXTRA_ARGS"

title: Kube API Server should close keepalive connections using unauthorized client certificates
body:
### What happened?

A long-running app using kubernetes client-python and authenticating with client certificates started to see authentication errors despite having a valid certificate on disk. The issue turned out to be because the certificate was rotated on disk but the urllib3 connection pool continued to re-use keepalive connections that were established using the older certificate. 

The kube API server is unique because it checks the full validity of a certificate on every request rather than just using the certificate metadata for authorization. Most TLS servers that accept client certs only verify the client certificate expiration during the handshake, so clients such as urllib3 are not prepared to handle this. They will continue reusing a connection established with an old cert indefinitely unless the connection dies.

### What did you expect to happen?

I expect apps using connection pooling and client certificates to work against the kubernetes API. The kubernetes API is unlike other TLS APIs due to how it verifies the cert expiration on every request, but that is beneficial to security. An easy solution would be to make the API server close the keepalive connection after detecting an invalid cert to force clients to re-establish the connection.

### How can we reproduce it (as minimally and precisely as possible)?

Create an HTTP connection to the API server in your favorite language using a certificate that will expire soon. Your handshake will succeed. Wait until the cert expires and make more connections using the same connection. You will start to get 401 errors back but the connection remains open.

body:
All cluster events during scheduling are piled up in [inFlightEvents](https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/master/pkg/scheduler/internal/queue/scheduling_queue.go#L187).
In the current design, we need them to evaluate which queue to push failed Pods to. 
But, given it needs to record all cluster events that happen during pod's scheduling, it increases the scheduler's memory consumption -- especially in a busy cluster.

Also, in the first place, maybe we have a memory leak around the inFlightEvents, see:

title: Garbage collector for container images is unpredictable and inconsistent
body:
### What happened?

The garbage collector for container image lifecycle does not seem to adhere to the documentation and the provided parameters.

From [the docs](https://kubernetes.io/docs/concepts/architecture/garbage-collection/#container-image-lifecycle), _the configured HighThresholdPercent value triggers garbage collection, which deletes images in order based on the last time they were used, starting with the oldest first. The kubelet deletes images until disk usage reaches the LowThresholdPercent value._

From some tests, this does not appear to be the case. Often, the GC will delete way more images than requires, often dropping below `LowThresholdPercent` and deleting 3 to 4 at a time.

### What did you expect to happen?

The GC should delete images until `LowThresholdPercent` is reached.

### How can we reproduce it (as minimally and precisely as possible)?

1. Either create some dummy images (we created a set of images with increasing sizes, but any will do the job), or identify some appropriate image already available on Docker Hub.
2. For each image, deploy a pod and then delete it. The image will remain in the cache.
3. After a while, the disk space will reach the `LowThresholdPercent` first and `HighThresholdPercent` later. The GC will be triggered.
4. The GC should in theory delete the earliest unused image. This does not always happen: priority is sometimes given to other images, or more than one is deleted, in a seemingly random order.

### Anything else we need to know?

The bug is hard to reproduce and needs some trial and error. Sometimes, images are correctly deleted in order and one at a time, other times the behaviour is apparently random.

If this behaviour is expected, then the docs should be appropriately corrected to mention the choices the GC makes. This is important as I/O spikes in the GC may cause SLA issues in other services deployed in the node.

title: Updating pods during scheduling may produce dirty data
body:
### What happened?

If we update a pod（such as update annotation） during the scheduling process, the scheduler's podInformer will generate an update event. If the pod has not been assumed at this time, this event will be added to the scheduling queue. When the pod is scheduled succeed, since the pod is still in the scheduling queue, the pod may be scheduled again. 

If there are many pods in the scheduling queue, the pod cannot be scheduled until 30 seconds later. At this time, the pod information in assumedPods has been cleared, and the pod will be scheduled again. Since the pod has been scheduled succeed, this scheduling will fail, and the scheduler will continue to retry, repeating the cycle. This pod will always become dirty data in the scheduler unless the scheduler is restarted.


### What did you expect to happen?

If the pod has been scheduled succeed, the scheduler should not schedule dirty data in the queue.

### How can we reproduce it (as minimally and precisely as possible)?

1. Create a pod；
2. When the pod starts scheduling, update the pod before assume（This step can be achieved by adding breakpoints through local debugging）；
3. After the update event generated by the pod enters the scheduling queue, we should guaranteed the pod  to be scheduled again after 30 seconds（Implemented through local breakpoint debugging）；
4. The pod has been scheduled, but the scheduler is still scheduling the pod in a loop.

title: Image locality scheduler with container layers awareness
body:
### Describe the issue

Hi,

We are currently working on a new K8s scheduler plugin prototype called Image Layer Locality, and I'm looking for some feedback.

The idea of this scheduler is to take into account the container layers in order to minimize the time to download the container images. The upstream scheduler already has an image locality plugin, but it only takes into account the image name. The Image layer locality scheduler is going one step forward by scoring nodes using the percentage of the container images already available and thus take advantage of the image layer caching.

### Advantages

- Could really reduce deployment time for large images for workloads with containers that shares container layers
- Based on the same mechanism as Image locality scheduler plugin, code change is light

### Limitations

- Only useful when the containers in the workload are sharing layers
- Like in the image locality plugin, it requires some spread policy to avoid allocation to always select the same node (the one with large layers already present)
- The first time a container image is encountered by the scheduler, it doesn't know its layers characteristics until its pull for the first time by the CRI. Thus, this scheduling optimization only kicks in when a container image is deployed for the second time.

### PoC

The main issue for this plugin is to acquire the layers size and locality. We have created a prototype for this scheduler, and followed the example of the image locality plugin. The CRI expose layers characteristics with an annotation. I already was told that a more standard field would be better, but we would like some feedback before going forward. We also added a new "Layers" field into the Node.Status API and add new filed in the scheduler snapshoter to have it exposed to the plugin. 

We modified Cri-O to expose the layers into annotations:
https://github.com/RyaxTech/cri-o/compare/v1.22.1...image-layer-locality-scheduler

Here are the changes that we've made on our Kubernetes fork:
https://github.com/RyaxTech/kubernetes/compare/v1.22.6...image-layer-locallity-scheduler

### Discussion

Exposing layers info for each of the nodes might have an impact on the message size, and thus the overall Kubernetes performance, but most of the images have only 2 or 3 layers (and they might be shared) so the overhead should be very limited. Also, to cope with this issue, we can add some mechanism to make the CRI only expose layers if their size is above a certain threshold or simply expose the N biggest layers. 

It is far from perfect for now, but we would really like to have feedback. Let me know if you're interested!

(Originally posted here: https://github.com/kubernetes/community/issues/7379)
