title: kubelet: lookup node address logic for external provider assign wrong PodIPs to hostNetwork pods
body:
The kubelet  logic used to get the Node addresses when using an external provider, temporary assigns an address discovered from the node , this address can be overriden later by the external cloud provider

https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/0241da314e0e69817d66313b45a69c19d1ce7327/pkg/kubelet/nodestatus/setters.go#L123-L131


This was implemented in https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/pull/75229 to improve the  bootstrapping problems with some external cloud providers

The side effect of this behavior is that if the external cloud provider sets a different address/es, then the pods with `HostNetwork: true` will be showing the "first" addresses as their `PodIPs`, since we don't mutate those IPs once set to avoid problems

https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/0241da314e0e69817d66313b45a69c19d1ce7327/pkg/kubelet/kubelet_pods.go#L1770-L1786

I think that we should revert the existing logic for external cloud providers, since is causing a temporary and inconsistent state and it seem to address mainly a problem with kubeadm https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/pull/75229#issuecomment-516592142 but kubeadm folks seems to not need this functionality https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/pull/75229#issuecomment-516580449

Announced mailing list https://groups.google.com/g/kubernetes-sig-cloud-provider/c/u8DH2hNY_FI/m/arryQvlzAQAJ

/kind bug
/sig network
/sig node

title: StatefulSet reports wrong replica count after pod creation
body:
### What happened?

StatefulSet controller updates the status of a StatefulSet object with `Replicas`, which is the count of all existing pods. Immediately after successfully creating pods, StatefulSet ignores them, showing a lower replica count than expect. The replica count is updated correctly the next time StatfulSet object is processed (usually within a couple of seconds).

The status self-recovers quickly. However, as the same value is used in some checks related to rolling update, the impact can be serious, as seen in #119685. These checks are being fixed in #120731, but we should also fix the status.

Proposed solution: update creation timestamp of successfully created replicas (around https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/master/pkg/controller/statefulset/stateful_set_control.go#L420). They should be processed correctly then.

### What did you expect to happen?

StatefulSet should immediately calculate the replica count correctly.

### How can we reproduce it (as minimally and precisely as possible)?

* Enable logging StatefulSet status.
* Increase the replica count.
* Observe that immediatly after successfully creating missing pods, replica count remains equal to previous one (excludes pods created in this iteration).

Alternatively, StatefulSet status can be monitored in another way (for example frequently fetched via k8s API) and correlated with pod creation times.

### Anything else we need to know?

_No response_

### Kubernetes version

1.28.0 and later
1.27.4 and later

### Cloud provider

N/A

/sig apps

title: `poststarthook/apiservice-registration-controller` check blocks apiserver readiness for 1 minute if discovery cannot be completed
body:
### What happened?

I’m seeing some odd behavior with 1.28.2 that was not present in earlier releases, with regards to aggregated api services. It appears that the `poststarthook/apiservice-registration-controller` is now blocking the apiserver from becoming ready for 1 minute, if discovery for an aggregated apiservice is not available when the apiserver is started. Note that this only happens if the apiservice is marked available when the apiserver is started; if it is unavailable at startup (Available status: false), or the service has no endpoints, the health check does not block and readyz returns `ok` without delay.

I am seeing this behavior in 1.28.1 and 1.28.2, but not v1.27.6 or v1.27.5

### What did you expect to happen?

apiserver becomes ready without any additional delays

### How can we reproduce it (as minimally and precisely as possible)?

1. Deploy metrics-server to a Kubernetes cluster
2. Wait for api registration for `v1beta1.metrics.k8s.io` to complete (Available status is `true`).
3. Kill the kubelet and pods on the node hosting the metrics-server pod, such that the metrics-server service continues to show available endpoints, but the endpoint is not reachable.
4. Restart the apiserver before the `v1beta1.metrics.k8s.io` apiservice is marked unavailable
5. Note that the `poststarthook/apiservice-registration-controller` check blocks readiness for 1 minute. After 1 minute the Available status is updated to `false`, and the health check passes.

### Anything else we need to know?

Other notes:
* Does not appear to make any difference if `AggregatedDiscoveryEndpoint` feature-gate is set to false.
* If the metrics-server service has no endpoints available, the apiservice status reason is updated to `MisssingEndpoints` and the check passes quickly.
* If there is an available endpoint, but it is not reachable, the check seems to be stuck retrying the endpoint, with the following message repeated in the logs:
    `Sep 18 20:37:01 systemd-node-1 k3s[8000]: E0918 20:37:01.403911    8000 available_controller.go:460] v1beta1.metrics.k8s.io failed with: failing or missing response from https://10.42.0.2:10250/apis/metrics.k8s.io/v1beta1: Get "https://10.42.0.2:10250/apis/metrics.k8s.io/v1beta1": net/http: request canceled while waiting for connection (Client.Timeout exceeded while awaiting headers)`


Odd error from GC that I don't remember seeing in the past:
`Sep 18 20:34:30 systemd-node-1 k3s[7903]: I0918 20:34:30.744555    7903 garbagecollector.go:816] "failed to discover some groups" groups="<internal error: json: unsupported type: map[schema.GroupVersion]error>"`

title: Volumes are forcibly detached when CSI driver installation is broken and KCM switches leader
body:
### What happened?

On an EKS cluster, we observed that volumes are forcibly detached after 6mins (`maxWaitForUnmountDuration`) after KCM leader switches. The EBS CSI Driver is missing at that time. Related logs:
```
14:51:22Z 11 attach_detach_controller.go:440] Error creating spec for volume "pv", pod "sdb"/"scout-14": error performing CSI migration checks and translation for PVC "sdb"/"pv-scout-14": in-tree plugin kubernetes.io/aws-ebs is migrated on node xxx but driver ebs.csi.aws.com is not installed
...
14:57:23Z 11 reconciler.go:227] attacherDetacher.DetachVolume started for volume "nil" (UniqueName: "kubernetes.io/csi/ebs.csi.aws.com^vol-06b79540fd7b6c2cb") on node "xxx" This volume is not safe to detach, but maxWaitForUnmountDuration 6m0s expired, force detaching
```

The EBS CSI Driver was removed from nodes after the volumes were attached to pods. The volumes remained attached until KCM switched leader. When new KCM acquired lease, it restarted the Attach/Detach controller. Due to missing CSI Driver, function `CreateVolumeSpec` failed in `populateDesiredStateOfWorld` (which would only run on the start of A/D controller) - https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/v1.23.17/pkg/controller/volume/attachdetach/attach_detach_controller.go#L440-L446. As a result, `volumeSpec` remained nil. And the volumes were treated as if they were not used by any pods and were forcibly detached after maxWaitForUnmountDuration.

I found the failure mode in CSI migration KEP https://github.com/kubernetes/enhancements/blob/master/keps/sig-storage/625-csi-migration/README.md#troubleshooting, that:

> If the CSI driver is missing but the PVC already exists. Volume attach/detach will fail with the following log in Kube-Controller-Manager:
```
E0125 11:54:12.388111       9 util.go:239] Error processing volume "mypvc" for pod "default"/"web-server": error performing CSI migration checks and translation for PVC "default"/"podpvc-intree": in-tree plugin kubernetes.io/gce-pd is migrated on node kubernetes-minion-group-hsv0 but driver pd.csi.storage.gke.io is not installed
```
So ideally volumes should not be attached/detached when CSI driver is missing, while we observed volumes were detached forcibly by KCM when leader switch occurred, while CSI driver was missing.

### What did you expect to happen?

Volume should not be detached when CSI driver is missing regardless of KCM leader switching.

### How can we reproduce it (as minimally and precisely as possible)?

- Install CSI Driver on some worker nodes of a kubernetes cluster
- Create some pods on these worker nodes and attach volumes to pods
- Break or remove the CSI Driver installation on these nodes
- Let KCM switch leader
- Observe volumes detach event in KCM log

### Anything else we need to know?

The issue was observed on 1.23.17 version cluster, but looks into latest code seems the logic stays the same so suspect the same issue would occur on 1.27 cluster as well.

### Kubernetes version

1.23.17

title: Kubelet didn't respect --resolv-conf when resolv.conf is empty or full of comments
body:
### What happened?

When I passing `--resolv-conf` to kubelet, it did not respect the option, and still copy the `/etc/resolv.conf` to the pod.

What makes it special is that the `resolv.conf` provided by myself is empty.

> https://kubernetes.io/docs/reference/command-line-tools-reference/kubelet/

After skimming the code, I found the logic here is problematic:

https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/v1.28.2/pkg/kubelet/network/dns/dns.go#L225-L274

Because `resolv.conf` is empty, an empty array and no error is returned. Then, if the dnsPolicy is `default` (that is the default config for CoreDNS deployment), the `podDNSType` turns to be `podDNSHost`:

https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/v1.28.2/pkg/kubelet/network/dns/dns.go#L316-L317

Then, containerd will get an empty `dns_config`, so it will copy `/etc/resolv.conf` from the host to the container:

https://github.com/containerd/containerd/blob/v1.7.6/pkg/cri/server/sandbox_run_linux.go#L282-L287

Finally, CoreDNS reports forwarding loop error.

### What did you expect to happen?

Kubelet should refuse to use the wrong empty `resolv.conf` to create a pod, and complains with errors.

### How can we reproduce it (as minimally and precisely as possible)?

1. Pass `--resolv-conf` to kubelet, and make sure the specified `resolv.conf` file is empty.
2. Check the output of CoreDNS, and its `/etc/resolv.conf`.

### Anything else we need to know?

_No response_

title: 1.28 kube-apiserver failed due to nil pointer panic when requests routed to "kube-aggregator"
body:
### What happened?

After control plane nodes recreation and after kube-apiserver being brought again. In some scenarios (we are still investigating the exact scenario), we found some request (mostly `GET openapi/v2`) may cause nil pointer panic in kube-apiserver:

```
I0919 05:56:20.096796       1 handler.go:153] kube-aggregator: GET "/openapi/v2" satisfied by nonGoRestful
I0919 05:56:20.096825       1 pathrecorder.go:241] kube-aggregator: "/openapi/v2" satisfied by exact match
panic: runtime error: invalid memory address or nil pointer dereference
[signal SIGSEGV: segmentation violation code=0x1 addr=0x0 pc=0x16bfbe0]

goroutine 8765 [running]:
k8s.io/kube-openapi/pkg/cached.(*Replaceable[...]).Get(0x5576440)
    vendor/k8s.io/kube-openapi/pkg/cached/cache.go:296 +0x60
k8s.io/kube-openapi/pkg/cached.(*listMerger[...]).prepareResultsLocked.func1()
    vendor/k8s.io/kube-openapi/pkg/cached/cache.go:188 +0x5f
created by k8s.io/kube-openapi/pkg/cached.(*listMerger[...]).prepareResultsLocked
    vendor/k8s.io/kube-openapi/pkg/cached/cache.go:182 +0x9b
```

And it seems to only happen when the request is routed to `kube-aggregator`, no similar issues on `kube-apiserver`, `apiextensions-apiserver`. Also `kube-aggregator` is able to back to normal eventually.

Based on the stack trace, we found in [below block](https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/v1.28.2/vendor/k8s.io/kube-openapi/pkg/cached/cache.go#L296) in `kube-openapi` that the `c.cache.Load()` could be nil which is causing this panic:

```
func (c *Replaceable[T]) Get() Result[T] {
	result := (*c.cache.Load()).Get()

	for {
		cResult := c.result.Load()
		if result.Err != nil && cResult != nil && cResult.Err == nil {
			return *cResult
		}
		if c.result.CompareAndSwap(cResult, &result) {
			return result
		}
	}
}
```



### What did you expect to happen?

Check cache is nil to avoid panic

### How can we reproduce it (as minimally and precisely as possible)?

Still in investigation of why it happens and how to reproduce easily. 

Per the current resource we have, it may happen on a single control plane node cluster with DHCP IP setting. And after recreating the control plane node (IP of the machine is changed), the `kubectl apply` would fail due to this issue.

### Anything else we need to know?

We also found recently there is a big change in `kube-openapi` which is merged into the main branch, need to verify if the nil pointer issue has been handled:

* https://github.com/kubernetes/kube-openapi/pull/405/files
* https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/commit/dad1b2a4306e925fb6e5cd93e5d651bfb2ccdf8b

title: support pod namespace index in cache
body:
### What would you like to be added?

1. Why doesn't the k8s community have a feature to list pods by namespace index when listing pods from apiserver cache?
2. When I try to implement the pod namespace index, I see "we don't support multiple trigger functions defined". What's the reason?

### Why is this needed?

In our cluster, the number of some resources like pods are very large(100k+). When listing a namespace resources like pods from apiserver cache, the apiserver process will firstly get all the resources in all the namespaces and then filter the resources by namespace predicate even it's a very small request. It's heavy for filtering namespaced resource even the resource number in the namespace is very small with many client requests. It consumes lots of cpu & memory that's not expected.

title: Resource Management of ETCD Load
body:
### What would you like to be added?

There should be Resource Management for tracking etcd load. This can then be used as a Resource Quota for Jobs to ensure that they (and potentially kubelet) do not spin up Pods faster than etcd can handle.

K8s Docs:
https://kubernetes.io/docs/concepts/configuration/manage-resources-containers/#extended-resources
https://kubernetes.io/docs/concepts/policy/resource-quotas/



### Why is this needed?

For people dealing with extremely high-throughput batch work (i.e 1000's jobs / second, lasting 1-2 mins each), etcd starts to become a real problem. There should be an in-k8s solution to this.

Whether it is through Resource Quotas or some other medium, I think this is something interesting to be explored. Happy to make this Ticket more detailed as required, and start the KEP if this is something that is interesting to folks.

Links to back up this point:
- https://etcd.io/docs/v3.5/op-guide/performance/
- https://github.com/armadaproject/armada: A scheduling solution partially designed around this problem.

title: [KEP-2400] [Swap]: Verify memory pressure behavior with swap enabled
body:
### What would you like to be added?

A replacement for https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/issues/105023

The issue is for addressing problems related to node pressures and swap.

In short, the problem is that the kernel would try to avoid/defer swapping as much as possible. Therefore, swap generally kicks in when the node is already pressured. On the other hand, kubelet configures node-eviction thresholds so it would be able to reclaim memory before the kernel starts doing so (e.g. with OOM kills).

So, now the flow is as follows:
* Kubelet threshold is exceeded => kubelet reclaims memory by killing pods.
* Swap kicks in.
* Kernel starts reclaiming space (e.g. by OOMing processes).

With this flow, swap does not have the opportunity to free memory space because kubelet starts evicting before it kicks in.

The desired flow is (same as above with different order):
* Swap kicks in.
* Kubelet threshold is exceeded => kubelet reclaims memory by killing pods.
* Kernel starts reclaiming space (e.g. by OOMing processes).

Important pointers:
- See [this comment](https://github.com/kubernetes/enhancements/issues/2400#issuecomment-1693451128).
- Current [discussion in Slack](https://kubernetes.slack.com/archives/C02UCH9N02J/p1695207853069709).

### Why is this needed?

KEP https://github.com/kubernetes/enhancements/tree/master/keps/sig-node/2400-node-swap

title: [Code-generator] `--extra-peer-dirs` flag  is not supported by new `kube-codegen.sh` script
body:
### What would you like to be added?

Earlier it was possible to pass `--extra-peer-dirs` flag to `conversion-gen` while calling `generate-internal-groups.sh` script. 
Now with the new `kube-codegen.sh` script, `conversion-gen` is called under `kube::codegen::gen_helpers` which doesnot support any other flags apart from `--input-pkg-root`, `--output-base` and `--boilerplate`.

As it can be seen here there is no option to pass flag to conversion-gen
```
 "${gobin}/conversion-gen" \
            -v "${v}" \
            -O zz_generated.conversion \
            --go-header-file "${boilerplate}" \
            --output-base "${out_base}" \
            "${inputs[@]}"
```
https://github.com/kubernetes/code-generator/blob/e4611069dfb4b0c04c7751afae1b9fef64828964/kube_codegen.sh#L203-L208

Earlier in the `generate-internal-groups.sh`  script, it was considering all the inputs passed
```
  echo "Generating conversions"
  "${gobin}/conversion-gen" \
      --input-dirs "$(codegen::join , "${ALL_FQ_APIS[@]}")" \
      -O zz_generated.conversion \
      "$@"
```

### Why is this needed?

`--extra-peer-dirs` flag is supported by `conversion-gen` under the hood, but the `kube::codegen::gen_helpers` function in `kube-codegen.sh` script is not allowing the flag.

title: NoExecute taint is added with extra 5s delay when a Node's ready condition becomes Unknown
body:
### What happened?

When investigating a delay of Pod eviction on unreachable Node, I found it always took 5s longer than the desired duration.
Looking at the timestamps, I found an odd one: the timestamp when `node.kubernetes.io/unreachable` NoExecute taint was added.

```
# Node taints:
taints:
- effect: NoSchedule
  key: node.kubernetes.io/unreachable
  timeAdded: "2023-09-21T06:32:41Z"
- effect: NoExecute
  key: node.kubernetes.io/unreachable
  timeAdded: "2023-09-21T06:32:46Z"    # This one is 5s later than all other timestamps

# Node conditions:
conditions:
- lastHeartbeatTime: "2023-09-21T06:31:55Z"
  lastTransitionTime: "2023-09-21T06:32:41Z"
  message: Kubelet stopped posting node status.
  reason: NodeStatusUnknown
  status: Unknown
  type: MemoryPressure
- lastHeartbeatTime: "2023-09-21T06:31:55Z"
  lastTransitionTime: "2023-09-21T06:32:41Z"
  message: Kubelet stopped posting node status.
  reason: NodeStatusUnknown
  status: Unknown
  type: DiskPressure
- lastHeartbeatTime: "2023-09-21T06:31:55Z"
  lastTransitionTime: "2023-09-21T06:32:41Z"
  message: Kubelet stopped posting node status.
  reason: NodeStatusUnknown
  status: Unknown
  type: PIDPressure
- lastHeartbeatTime: "2023-09-21T06:31:55Z"
  lastTransitionTime: "2023-09-21T06:32:41Z"
  message: Kubelet stopped posting node status.
  reason: NodeStatusUnknown
  status: Unknown
  type: Ready

# Pod conditions:
- lastProbeTime: null
  lastTransitionTime: "2023-09-21T06:32:41Z"
  status: "False"
  type: Ready
```

This can be reproducd consistently by terminating kubelet on a Node. The 5s delay of tainting adds 5s delay to the recovery time of Pods which are supposed to be evicted by the taint and recreated on other Nodes sooner. And I can't think of a reason why this taint alone should be added 5s later after the other taint and all other status changes. After investigating the relevant code for how the 5s is introduced, I think it should be an unwanted effect:

`processTaintBaseEviction()` uses the last observed ready condition of the Node instead of the current one to determine whether it should add the Node to the taint queue. When a Node is set to unreachable due to missing heartbeats, the last observed ready condition is still `true` and the current ready condition is `unknown`, we should use the latter for `processTaintBaseEviction()`. Otherwise the taint can only be added when `monitorNodeHealth()` runs another time (5s later) during which the current ready condition becomes the last observed ready condition, like the following logs show:
https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/cde6a46a483a0cc7d3f2404db506e1c24ecd4e9d/pkg/controller/nodelifecycle/node_lifecycle_controller.go#L741


title: Fixes in cel-go breaks backward compatible of CRD validation rules between 1.27 and 1.28 release
body:
### What happened?

We were using cel-go v0.12.7 in Kubernetes 1.27 release and cel-go v0.16.0 in Kubernetes 1.28 release. There are many changes from cel-go side between those two releases and some may break backward compatible of CRD validation rules.

An example would be the estimated cost for CRD validation rules(Thanks to @inteon who brought this to our attention with the following example).
In the example CRD validation rules below:
```
---
apiVersion: apiextensions.k8s.io/v1
kind: CustomResourceDefinition
metadata:
  name: resources.example.com
spec:
  group: example.com
  names:
    kind: Resource
    listKind: ResourceList
    plural: resources
    singular: resource
  scope: Namespaced
  versions:
  - name: v1alpha1
    schema:
      openAPIV3Schema:
        properties:
          apiVersion:
            type: string
          kind:
            type: string
          metadata:
            type: object
          spec:
            items:
              properties:
                a:
                  type: string
                b:
                  type: string
                c:
                  type: string
                d:
                  type: string
                e:
                  type: string
                f:
                  type: string
              type: object
              x-kubernetes-validations:
              - message: must have exactly one field set
                rule: '(has(self.a) ? 1 : 0) + (has(self.b) ? 1 : 0) + (has(self.c)
                  ? 1 : 0) + (has(self.d) ? 1 : 0) + (has(self.e) ? 1 : 0)
                  + (has(self.f) ? 1 : 0) == 1'
            type: array
        type: object
    served: true
    storage: true
    ...
```
It will pass perfect in Kubernetes 1.27 version but fail in Kubernetes 1.28 with error:
`Forbidden: estimated rule cost exceeds budget by factor of 1.6x (try simplifying the rule, or adding maxItems, maxProperties, and maxLength where arrays, maps, and strings are declared) `

This is due to the estimator fix happened in cel-go([cel fix 1](https://github.com/google/cel-go/pull/651), [cel fix 2](https://github.com/google/cel-go/pull/798))

### What did you expect to happen?

The changes should not cause backward incompatible of CRD validation rules. OR a stability test suite should be in place to prevent the changes causing backward compatible issue before GA.

### How can we reproduce it (as minimally and precisely as possible)?

Apply the above CRD in Kubernetes 1.27 and 1.28, 1.27 cluster should pass and 1.28 cluster should fail.

### Anything else we need to know?

Since the fix in cel-go side makes sense to me and the feature is in Beta now, I am not quite sure how strict we should be on backward compatible.  cc @liggitt 

As a followup, a stability test suite for estimate cost is worth adding before GA to make sure any future changes be caught before the feature promoted to GA.

title: Support for kubelet node capacity overrides
body:
### What would you like to be added?

I would like to propose adding new kubelet options which would allow users to override values for node CPU and memory capacity which are currently detected using cadvisor and which are used by kubelet internally and reported as node’s capacity to API server. 

Values of those options would take precedence over the values read from cadvisor. Those would be used both internally by kubelet for instance for pod addmission logic and node allocatable resources calculation but also externally as node capacity reported to API server.

As overriding node capacity could invalidate some of host CPU and memory low-level metadata like for instance CPU topology, functionalities in kubelet like CPU manager should not be supported together with the capacity overrides - enabling them at the same time should cause a kubelet panic during the startup.


### Why is this needed?

An option to override node capacity would be useful for many testing and bootstrapping use cases where [Kind](https://kind.sigs.k8s.io/) and [minikube](https://minikube.sigs.k8s.io/docs/start/) clusters are currently used. In those use cases current kubelet logic always takes the full host capacity as a node capacity.

This is problematic in use cases where:

- We want to provide a fixed amount of resources for a Kubernetes node regardless of the size of the host on which they are running. This may be useful for instance when running on hosts of different sizes.

- We want to run a multi-node cluster on a single host and we do not want each node to have access to a full VM capacity but instead we would like to provide each node with a part of host capacity.

Those use cases are currently only partially supported through a kube reservation override which requires calculating it based on an actual host size or through a manipulation of the sys filesystem as seen by kubelet which is quite a complicated solution and it is hard to maintain.

title: Support node allocatable and capacity managed by external controller
body:
### What would you like to be added?

I would like to propose adding new kubelet options which would stop kubelet from detecting, calculating and updating information about CPU and memory capacity and allocatable resources. Instead those values would need to be set by a dedicated external controller which could use any logic to provide them. Kubelet in such a setup would be watching for node CPU and memory capacity and allocatable resources changes on an API node resource status and react accordingly when those change.

### Why is this needed?

Many open source and commercial virtualization solutions like [KVM](https://www.linux-kvm.org/page/CPUHotPlug) and VMWare support dynamic CPU and memory hotplugging without the need to restart a VM. With those solutions we would like to have a way to update node capacity and allocatable resources to match the current VM state without a need to restart kubelet.

Moreover in cases when some resources are removed we would like to update node resources values before the actual change in resources is effective to avoid race conditions and situations when for instance some recently scheduled pods would need to be killed just after node capacity has been reduced or situations where pods require some grace period before being killed but the resources available on the node has already been changed. Because of those relying on kubelet to retrospectively detect the node capacity changes by itself is not sufficient.

Other situations when kubelet may not be able to detect resources available on a node on its own is when there are some non containerized workloads running on the same host. In this situation kubelet cannot properly detect how much resources on a given host are actually available for running pods. This information could be obtained from some external source be a node agent or a controller responsible for running those non containerized workloads and communicated to kubelet by updating node allocatable resources status.

A different solution to a similar problem has been proposed in [KEP-3953: Dynamic node resize](https://github.com/kubernetes/enhancements/pull/3955). This proposal addresses some issues with the other proposal by providing more flexibility when it comes to logic used to detect node capacity and allocatable resources and timing when those should be changed.

title: SideCar startupProbe on 1.28
body:
### What happened?

There seems to be a bit of a time sync or race condition between the intiContainer doing its thing and the startup probe , take this example:
```
  containers:
    - name: myapp
      image: alpine:latest
      command: ['sh', '-c', 'tail -F /opt/logs.txt']
      volumeMounts:
        - name: data
          mountPath: /opt
  initContainers:
    - name: logshipper
      image: alpine:latest
      restartPolicy: Always
      command: ['sh', '-c', 'sleep 3 ; echo "containerId: $(cat /proc/1/uid_map  | awk "{ print $3 }") logging $(date +%s)" >> /opt/logs.txt']
      startupProbe:
        exec:
          command: ["true"]
        periodSeconds: 1
        initialDelaySeconds: 0
      volumeMounts:
        - name: data
          mountPath: /opt
```
This example passes the startupProbe and the container `myapp` starts ok , but if i remove the `sleep` or if i reduce it to anything shorter than `3` seconds ,  the `myapp` container never start.

`myapp` should of start as a result of `startupProbe` passing ,  but it seems to take too long to exec

title: Critical: Node reboot could lead to data loss due to broken volume lifecycle management
body:
### What happened?

In certain situations, rebooting a Kubernetes node could lead to:
- Best case: A volume not getting mounted, despite it being a healthy volume
- Worse case: A volume getting mounted in an (ephemeral) empty host directory
- Worst cast: The wrong volume getting mounted inside the pod

### What did you expect to happen?

The right volume must be mounted in the right pod.

### How can we reproduce it (as minimally and precisely as possible)?

- Create a PVC, and make sure all ongoing pod creations happen on the same node
- Create a deployment with long termination grace period, say 600 seconds, that uses that PVC, wait for it to become Ready
- Delete the deployment, which should result in the pod getting stuck in `Terminating` state
- Create another deployment that uses the same PVC
- Reboot the underlying node

After the reboot, one of the two happens:
- CSI node driver receives `NodePublishVolume` before receiving any `NodeStageVolume` requests, meaning the CSI will try to `Publish` using an invalid stage directory, which could lead to the CSI not being able to publish it (Best case) or it mounting the wrong volume (Worst case)
- CSI node driver does not receive any requests, and kubelet goes ahead and mounts the empty directory inside the pod, leading to the "Worse case" scenario described above.

These steps almost always results in one of the undesired outcomes to happen.

### Anything else we need to know?

After realizing that the issue was a regression, we bisected it, and it looks like this was first introduced in 1.23.15. We've verified that the issue disappears after downgrading node's kubelet to 1.23.14, but 1.23 and 1.24 have reached their EOL already.
Based on the history of changes on kubelet's volume manager code, the issue might've had been introduced in [this commit range](https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/compare/75b8b1ebfd55e1c5042cdc33d3f30d8080bd707e%5E...390fc21359561b9094eff93e60176e244f3af54b).

### Kubernetes version

All currently supported kubelet versions (> 1.25) are affected.

title: When deleting pods on the same node in batches, the exited container may remain, causing pod records to remain.
body:
### What happened?

During performance testing, I found that when deleting pods on a node in batches, such as 100, the problem of pod deletion failure may occur. The exited container may remain, causing pod records to remain. I think this problem is related to the implementation of pod_container_deletor.go that containerDeletorBufferLimit is only 50. and in the func (p *podContainerDeletor) deleteContainersInPod, when the worker channel is full, it discards the event. I think using work queue instead of channel is a better solution. And the processing logic of runtime.DeleteContainer needs to be optimized. The processing can be skipped for containers that have been externally deleted or cannot be found. 

And i found it still almost the same solution in podContainerDeletor. The master branch may also have the same problem.

I will submit a PR later for this issue.



### What did you expect to happen?

pods and containers can be deleted successfully

### How can we reproduce it (as minimally and precisely as possible)?

batch delete over than 100 pods that on same node

### Anything else we need to know?

_No response_

### Kubernetes version

<details>


title: Delete STS, the pod associated with the STS cannot be automatically cleaned up
body:
### What happened?

We have a problem scenario, we have a single node k8s cluster with 1.25.3.
I deleted an STS on the client side and recreated it immediately. It happened that there was a network failure, but after I fixed the network failure, the status of the STS was incorrect. In addition, an error message is displayed in the log, indicating that the pod already exists and cannot be created again. I also checked that the pod's owner reference was old sts and confirmed by the UID that it was indeed the old one.
As shown below:
![image](https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/assets/46313756/1cc4edd3-65b6-44c5-9ba5-279806413b3e)
![image](https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/assets/46313756/1d5ac8f3-e3ca-4bff-943e-8e7f2364f576)

When I restart kube-controller-manager, the old Pod is automatically cleared. After debug the code, I found that the owner of the pod is no longer available, then the old Pod is automatically cleared by GCController.

I have tried to add some log to `pkg/controller/garbagecollector/graph_builder.go:136` and found that no delete event was received.


### What did you expect to happen?

When sts is deleted, pods that are not referenced should be cleaned up.

### How can we reproduce it (as minimally and precisely as possible)?

The following steps may not accurately reproduce the problem.
- Create a simple STS
- Constructing a Network Fault
- Delete STS, and recreate it

So I modified the code to ignore the STS deletion event when I received it, and even if I restarted the APIServer, those list&watch requests re-initiated, the pod would not be deleted.
![image](https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/assets/46313756/a4a066ed-ca55-4923-8c72-83515f86c366)

title: External service UDP fails while TCP works due to definition processing asymmetry
body:
### What happened?

I have a single node k3s installation. I'd like to use it as an entry point even if some services are installed on separate VMs, not on K8s. External services work nicely when the service is available via TCP, but not when it's UDP as the system thinks UDP service doesn't have Endpoint definition and creates deny rules for iptables. The YAML is symmetric to the TCP one.

Working TCP:
````
apiVersion: v1
kind: Service
metadata:
  name: bugreport-works
  namespace: mate
spec:
  type: LoadBalancer
  ports:
  - port: 4321
    name: works-tcp
    protocol: TCP
    targetPort: 4321
---
kind: Endpoints
apiVersion: v1
metadata:
  name: bugreport-works
  namespace: mate
subsets:
  - addresses:
      - ip: 192.168.122.108
    ports:
      - port: 4321
        name: works-tcp
````

Not working UDP:
````
apiVersion: v1
kind: Service
metadata:
  name: bugreport-fails
  namespace: mate
spec:
  type: LoadBalancer
  ports:
  - port: 4321
    name: fails-udp
    protocol: UDP
    targetPort: 4321
---
kind: Endpoints
apiVersion: v1
metadata:
  name: bugreport-fails
  namespace: mate
subsets:
  - addresses:
      - ip: 192.168.122.108
    ports:
      - port: 4321
        name: fails-udp
````

For UDP I see these generated rejection rules (for TCP, there is no any similar):
```
-A KUBE-EXTERNAL-SERVICES -d 192.168.31.133/32 -p udp -m comment --comment "mate/bugreport-fails:fails-udp has no endpoints" -m udp --dport 4321 -j REJECT --reject-with icmp-port-unreachable
-A KUBE-EXTERNAL-SERVICES -p udp -m comment --comment "mate/bugreport-fails:fails-udp has no endpoints" -m addrtype --dst-type LOCAL -m udp --dport 31974 -j REJECT --reject-with icmp-port-unreachable
-A KUBE-SERVICES -d 10.43.215.148/32 -p udp -m comment --comment "mate/bugreport-fails:fails-udp has no endpoints" -m udp --dport 4321 -j REJECT --reject-with icmp-port-unreachable
```

### What did you expect to happen?

TCP and UDP definitions should work identically

### How can we reproduce it (as minimally and precisely as possible)?

Modify the definitions above according to your environment. Get an external host (VM, node, etc), netcat is the easiest to test it.
On caller client (first for TCP, second for UDP)
```
root@hu1l2022978:~# nc 192.168.31.133 4321
a
b
^C
root@hu1l2022978:~# nc-u 192.168.31.133 4321
a
root@hu1l2022978:~#
```
On backend host (first for TCP, second for UDP)
```
root@matelin:~# nc -ul 4321
^C
root@matelin:~# nc -l 4321
a
b
root@matelin:~# nc -ul 4321
```

In case of applying the UDP definition, on K8S node you immediately see the rejection rules (see above)

### Anything else we need to know?

title: Curl request gets pretty printed by default
body:
### What happened?

```
curl http://localhost:8080/api/v1/namespaces/my-namespace/pods/my-pod
```

= 64K bytes

```
curl http://localhost:8080/api/v1/namespaces/my-namespace/pods/my-pod?pretty=false
```

= 32k bytes



### What did you expect to happen?

API call defaults to pretty=false

The docs say: https://kubernetes.io/docs/reference/generated/kubernetes-api/v1.26/
```
pretty	If 'true', then the output is pretty printed.
```

It does not mention that there is a default. So to me, that implies that pretty is not set/true

### How can we reproduce it (as minimally and precisely as possible)?

Curl an object with and without the arg `pretty=true` and diff the response size

title: move GetKernelVersion out of `pkg/proxy/ipvs`
body:
The ipvs proxy has code to check the kernel version (including a mockable interface), and this has ended up getting used outside of that code; currently in kubelet (`pkg/kubelet/sysctl`) for figuring out what sysctls are available (for pods to request to be set), and in the future in https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/pull/120354, for figuring out if a certain conntrack hack is needed.

We should move that code somewhere more generic.

title: Serving watch requests takes large memory space in goroutine's stack
body:
### What would you like to be added?

Optimize the memory usage of goroutine stack for serving watch requests. According to the [traceback](https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/issues/117777#issuecomment-1723055664) of handling a watch request, the stack memory is 0x3768, which is very close to 16 KiB and Golang runtime will double it to 32 KiB once exceeded. In fact, it does exceed if we print the traceback deeper and take the fact that extra stack memory reserved by Golang itself into consideration. 

A naive optimization is to run as much as preparation handlers in a separate goroutine and then move the actual serving to another goroutine, so the former routine can free the stack memory earlier and make it more memory efficient.

### Why is this needed?

Given the extensive use of watch requests, 32 KiB per watch could add up to a very high amount of memory overhead for `kube-apiserver`. A typical watch request commonly lasts for 30s or longer, which means this memory will be active for quite long. I see a great improvement in memory efficiency to do this optimization.

title: About the future of existing PV generated from the in-tree format yaml once the CSI migration is complete
body:
### What would you like to be added?

As the title mentions, our customers are concerned about the future of existing PV generated from the in-tree format yaml once the CSI migration is complete.
I am stuck on this and would really like to know what the SIG storage policy is on this matter.

### Why is this needed?

CSI Migration allows PVs with Specs in in-tree format to be manipulated via CSI, but PVs with Specs in CSI format are treated differently from in-trees,
our customers is concerned about whether In-tree Spec and PVs generated from In-tree format yaml files will work forever in the future, or whether we need to convert from PVs generated from In-tree format yaml files to CSI PVs once the CSI migration is complete, and do we have to recreate the deployment via CSI spec if the in-tree format yaml file is no longer available.

I believe some translate functions that translate In-tree PV Spec into the CSI PV format have been added in https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/pull/83098 ,
could I ask that when will these functions be maintained ?
Will it be maintained forever and not deleted in the future? And is it okay if I assume that existing In-tree PVs will continue to be used in the future?  (Specs will remain as In-tree PVs and will not need to be modified, but will be converted by translate functions and will always be processed by CSI plugins forever in the future).

I would like to know what is the policy of SIG storage. Thank you very much.

/sig storage

title: Default RBAC role "admin" does not allow for ephemeral container usage
body:
### What happened?

Hey folks,
I noticed the default clusterrole admin does not have enough permissions for the newish Ephemeral Containers functionality https://github.com/kubernetes/enhancements/blob/master/keps/sig-node/277-ephemeral-containers/README.md

My team provides an EKS-based platform for development teams in which we provision a namespace (e.g. "bogus") and grant them the default ClusterRole of "admin" inside that namespace via a RoleBinding to a Group, and then use aws-auth to map an AWS IAM Role to the respective group. 

The role has this subset of APIs "write-enabled" for the Pods endpoints:

```
- apiGroups:
  - ""
  resources:
  - pods
  - pods/attach
  - pods/exec
  - pods/portforward
  - pods/proxy
  verbs:
  - create
  - delete
  - deletecollection
  - patch
  - update
```
My expectation is that every namespaced Kubernetes functionality would be available to those users.

### What did you expect to happen?

Users should be able to use `kubectl debug` to debug any pods with in their namespace if they have the default ClusterRole admin bound to a namespace with a RoleBinding, or use it in any namespace with a ClusterRoleBinding.

### How can we reproduce it (as minimally and precisely as possible)?

- Get a RoleBinding in namespace foo to the default ClusterRole admin with a subject that you can easily authenticate as.
- Follow the necessary authentication method to access the cluster with that subject.
- kubectl run nginx --image=nginx --restart=Never -n foo
- kubectl debug nginx -it --image=nginx -n foo

You will get a forbidden error such as

```
Error from server (Forbidden): pods "nginx" is forbidden: User "foo-admin" cannot patch resource "pods/ephemeralcontainers" in API group "" in the namespace "foo"
```

title: Regression? Deleting Pod marked as terminated while volumes are being unmounted
body:
### What happened?

In k8s 1.23
1. pod is running which mounts some volumes
2. stop csi-driver
3. delete pod using `kubectl delete pod xxx`
4. pod cannot be deleted completely because of unmounted volume
5. kube-scheduler cannot execute `deletePodFromCache` method to clear pod from node info https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/1635c380b26a1d8cc25d36e9feace9797f4bae3c/pkg/scheduler/eventhandlers.go#L223

In k8s 1.27
1. pod is running which mounts some volumes
2. stop csi-driver
3. delete pod using `kubectl delete pod xxx`
4. pod cannot be deleted completely because of unmounted volume
5. `But` kube-scheduler `can` execute `deletePodFromCache` method to clear pod from node info 
https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/bdfb880a198495e94a9092575d160936aa42b824/pkg/scheduler/eventhandlers.go#L215

### What happened?

We are running our custom csi provider to mount zfs via iscsi, this is operating since at least 1.20 and never showed any issues.

It does not implement the NodeStage / NodeUnstage apis, and only uses the NodePublishVolume / NodeUnpublishVolume.

Since upgrading to 1.28.2 the Unmount progress gets stuck and the zfs pool keeps busy indefinitely.

Do not keep the mounted volume busy when Unmounting via CSI providers.

title: Possible data race in code
body:
### What happened?

In file: [evented.go](https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/46dea3015f46261cecefe71d28d4511664e2b590/pkg/kubelet/pleg/evented.go#L171C23-L171C41), there is a possible data race in `watchEventsChannel` while accessing `eventedPLEGUsage`. 

In line [176](https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/46dea3015f46261cecefe71d28d4511664e2b590/pkg/kubelet/pleg/evented.go#L176), there is a goroutine invocation. Inside the goroutine, in line [183](https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/46dea3015f46261cecefe71d28d4511664e2b590/pkg/kubelet/pleg/evented.go#L183), there is a call to `e.Stop()`. Inside that function's implementation, there is an invocation of function `setEventedPLEGUsage` in line [134](https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/46dea3015f46261cecefe71d28d4511664e2b590/pkg/kubelet/pleg/evented.go#L134). Inside that method, in line [59](https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/46dea3015f46261cecefe71d28d4511664e2b590/pkg/kubelet/pleg/evented.go#L59), the value of  `eventedPLEGUsage` is written.

However, in line [201](https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/46dea3015f46261cecefe71d28d4511664e2b590/pkg/kubelet/pleg/evented.go#L201), this value is accessed in a readonly manner when the function `isEventedPLEGInUse` is called which reads `eventedPLEGUsage`.

Even though inside the function  `isEventedPLEGInUse` and `setEventedPLEGUsage` , the [read](https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/46dea3015f46261cecefe71d28d4511664e2b590/pkg/kubelet/pleg/evented.go#L48) and [write](https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/46dea3015f46261cecefe71d28d4511664e2b590/pkg/kubelet/pleg/evented.go#L56) accesses to `eventedPLEGUsage` are guarded by locks, the global order of these function invocations are non-deterministic. In one interval, `isEventedPLEGInUse` in the main routine may be called before the other; in another interval, this may happen the other way. 


### What did you expect to happen?

This is not reported by a run time observation. This is reported by a static analysis tool.

### How can we reproduce it (as minimally and precisely as possible)?

This is not reported by a run time observation. This is reported by a static analysis tool.

### Anything else we need to know?

This work is done by the security researchers from OpenRefactory and is supported by the [Open Source Security Foundation (OpenSSF)](https://openssf.org/): [Project Alpha-Omega](https://alpha-omega.dev/). Alpha-Omega is a project partnering with open source software project maintainers to systematically find new, as-yet-undiscovered vulnerabilities in open source code - and get them fixed – to improve global software supply chain security.

The bug is found by running the Intelligent Code Repair (iCR) tool by OpenRefactory and then manually triaging the results.

title: Undocumented enableServiceLinks behaviour
body:
### What happened?

In a pod spec, if `enableServiceLinks == false`, no services' information should be injected into the pods. That's according to the [document][1]. However, according to [the code][2], information on the services in the *master service* namespace, `kube-system` by default, is always injected.

> We always want to add environment variabled for master services

The code has this comment without explaining why we should always do this.

[1]: https://kubernetes.io/docs/reference/generated/kubernetes-api/v1.28/#pod-v1-core
[2]: https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/9050c510e640f325d008792a517fe85808b34150/pkg/kubelet/kubelet_pods.go#L523

### What did you expect to happen?

When `enableServiceLinks == false` on a pod, no services' information should be injected into the pod.

### How can we reproduce it (as minimally and precisely as possible)?

Create a few pods with `enableServiceLinks == false` and associated service, then observe if the services' information is injected into the pods.

title: Split etcd /health endpoint to /livez and /readyz
body:
### What would you like to be added?

k/k tracking issue for https://github.com/etcd-io/etcd/issues/16007

etcd currently has a single health endpoint for etcd /health which is used in Kubernetes distros as both liveness and readiness checking. In order to be fully api-compliant, etcd should have both a liveness check (i.e. /livez) which checks that this individual etcd member is "alive" and does not need to be restarted and a readiness check (i.e. /readyz) which signals that the etcd member is ready to accept traffic.

We are seeking feedbacks for the plan and we also need to change the default etcd health check configs in kubeadm after that is done. 

### Why is this needed?

We are trying to make etcd fully api-compliant.

title: We might benefit from a "network should continue working in cases that resemble syn_cookie or syn_flood" test...
body:
### What happened?

There are kernel bugs such as https://bugs.launchpad.net/ubuntu/+source/linux-hwe-5.4/+bug/1981658, which we've found on ubuntu versions, which only are visible if a node is pushed to the point that it "Switches" the way it processes packets, to the syn_cookie kernel path...

Now, Looking at https://access.redhat.com/solutions/30453, it doesnt look like we really want this to be a normal scenario...... 
```
        Note, that syncookies is fallback facility.
        It MUST NOT be used to help highly loaded servers to stand
        against legal connection rate. If you see SYN flood warnings
        in your logs, but investigation shows that they occur
        because of overload with legal connections, you should tune 
        another parameters until this warning disappear.
        See: tcp_max_syn_backlog, tcp_synack_retries, tcp_abort_on_overflow.
```

**Status**
I ran our existing e2es (iperf, networkpolicies, and sig-network tests) at high concurrency, and wasnt able to force a synflood/syncookie fallback at any point, but i know of clusters where kubelets have failed due to that path in the kernel.

**Goal**
Would be nice if we had a sig-network e2e that simulated this ?  Feel free to close if one of the existing tests already does this. 

This may or may not be possible.  I THINK that the way to do this would be to fire off lots of TCP connections.... and somehow keep them open for a long time (i.e. maybe serve very large packets?) 



### What did you expect to happen?

Kubernetes sig-net or similar e2e's would be able to simulate overloaded service/endpoints where non-normal TCP connection handling start happening. 

### How can we reproduce it (as minimally and precisely as possible)?

Not sure, thats the purpose of this test :). But... I suppose we might be able to reproduce syn-floods if theres too many TCP asks coming in at agiven time, in parallel (see above linked RH article).

title: Kubernetes ephemeral storage exhausted by a pod, rendering the cluster unusable
body:
### What happened?

https://kubernetes.io/docs/concepts/policy/resource-quotas/
When several users or teams share a cluster with a fixed number of nodes, there is a concern that one team could use more than its fair share of resources.
Resource quotas are a tool for administrators to address this concern.
AND

https://kubernetes.io/docs/concepts/configuration/manage-resources-containers/#meaning-of-cpu
If the user doesn't specify the ephemeral-storage resource limit in the Pod spec, the resource quota is not enforced on ephemeral-storage.

This is FATAL to production level use of a Kubernetes cluster.
In one occurrence a pod using a web based file browser interface allowed uploading files.
Uploading a real big file e.g. 5 GB causes the NGINX pod(s) to exhaust ephemeral storage.

This renders ANY application running on the cluster to become UNREACHABLE through the NGINX ingress controller.

A pod should not be allowed to do this - especially if there is a resource quota already introduced.

However "If the user doesn't specify the ephemeral-storage resource limit in the Pod spec, the resource quota is not enforced on ephemeral-storage." totally cripples this safety mechanism.

### What did you expect to happen?

Not to have Nginx become unavailable due to one pod exhausting ephemeral storage.


### How can we reproduce it (as minimally and precisely as possible)?

deploy a pod that allows uploading files using e.g.
image: filebrowser/filebrowser:v2.22.4

Use the Webgui to upload a file that is larger than the ephemeral storage available to node running the (E.g) nginx pod 

Watch the memory of nginx grow along with the size of the file uploaded and eventually "blow up"

### Why is this needed?

This is required to [GA the feature](https://github.com/kubernetes/enhancements/pull/4251) but it's also useful in general.

To the best of my knowledge, it's very hard to observe the behavior of memorymanager without peeking into the pod and/or use the podresources interface (kubelet >= 1.24). But even for the latter, no well known components expose metrics consuming this information.

I believe anyway kubelet some expose some basic metrics about memoryumanager behaviour, while deferring more fine grained metrics to external components (NFD, node_exporter, is fine)

title: Ability to validate kubectl exec/attach requests in the Admission Controller based on requestor source IP address
body:
### What would you like to be added?

Request : Expose the source IP address in the AdmissionReview Object.

Context :

We would like to have Admission Controller make decisions on a particular exec/attach request depending upon where the request originated from i.e the client source IP address.

The source IP address is not available in the AdmissionReview object so it is currently not possible to do validation on IP address at Admission Control.

The requestor's IP address is available in the K8S API server (the api server audit logs contain the IP address information) however this information is not passed along to Admission Controller.

### Why is this needed?

Due to a security policy, we want users to interact (exec, attach) with their K8S workloads only from certain machines and dis-allow all interactions from all other machines.

title: E2E Service Test assumes node name matches node's hostname
body:
### Which jobs are failing?

https://testgrid.k8s.io/kops-misc#e2e-kops-do-calico-dns-none

### Which tests are failing?

Kubernetes e2e suite.[It] [sig-network] Services should respect internalTrafficPolicy=Local Pod and Node, to Pod (hostNetwork: true)

### Since when has it been failing?

For as long as we have retention history on the e2e job

### Testgrid link

https://testgrid.k8s.io/kops-misc#e2e-kops-do-calico-dns-none

### Reason for failure (if possible)

This test creates an "echo hostname" server pod with hostNetwork. It then verifies that the pod's hostname matches the name of the node it runs on:

https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/3bfa9482fca675803c456ecbe4252b6525c9d021/test/e2e/network/service.go#L2665-L2670

These names match in the most common cluster configurations in GCP and AWS, but isn't a documented requirement. In other cluster configurations this test will fail due to this invalid assumption even though the behavior the test intends to verify is working as expected.

### Anything else we need to know?

Looking at a cluster-info dump of the cluster being tested, [the nodes](https://storage.googleapis.com/kubernetes-jenkins/logs/e2e-kops-do-calico-dns-none/1709688569984978944/artifacts/cluster-info/nodes.yaml) have a Hostname address that is the fully qualified name reported on the host and in the test's unexpected response.

I think it would be more appropriate for this test to compare against a node's unqualified Hostname address if one exists, otherwise falling back to the node name. Similar nodes on [AWS](https://storage.googleapis.com/kubernetes-jenkins/pr-logs/pull/kops/15996/pull-kops-e2e-k8s-aws-calico/1710078083949662208/artifacts/cluster-info/nodes.yaml) and [GCP](https://storage.googleapis.com/kubernetes-jenkins/pr-logs/pull/kops/15996/pull-kops-e2e-k8s-gce-cilium/1710078084008382464/artifacts/cluster-info/nodes.yaml) have Hostname addresses that (when unqualified) match their node names, so this test would continue to pass on these clusters.

Note that this test failure is on a Kops e2e job and relates to https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/issues/120989

/sig testing
/sig network

title: Should the completed pods be evicted?
body:
### What would you like to be added?

During using the kubernetes, I found a case:
1. Create a pod that will finally complete.(may be controlled by a job). 
2. Suppose this pod is scheduled on to node1 and completed. Taint node1 with `NoExecute`.
3. The competed pod is **evicted** by the taint manager.

 The completed pods do not occupy node resources, so is it necessary to evict it?

### Why is this needed?

Users may need some informations of this completed pod, and if it's evicted, they will have to create a same pod again.

title: kube-proxy SNAT policy for nodeport should only be performed on traffic originating from the pod on the current host
body:
### What happened?

Pod A runs on host node-1, where there are multiple network cards (eth0:10.10.11.1, eth1:192.168.10.11). Pod A is associated with service A, which is a nodeport type and provides a nodeport 30001; Pod B runs on host node-2, and accesses Pod A through 192.168.10.11:30001. At this time, the source IP obtained inside Pod A is the IP of eth0 on node-1, and the expected IP is eth1.

### What did you expect to happen?


The source IP should be displayed as the IP of the network card through which the traffic actually passes. Some gateway applications require the setting of an x-forwarded for request header, which may be used in security policies. When multiple network cards exist, it is necessary to set the x-forwarded for to the correct business network card IP address.


### How can we reproduce it (as minimally and precisely as possible)?

create nginx pod and config x-forward-for header，access nginx using pod host ip and service nodeport。

### Anything else we need to know?

kube-proxy add this rule for nodeport traffic:
-A KUBE-POSTROUTING -m comment --comment "kubernetes service traffic requiring SNAT" -j MASQUERADE

MASQUERADE rule will change the source ip to the network card with the highest priority on the host.

title: Schedule a CronJob on a final day of the month
body:
### What would you like to be added?

As of today, Kubernetes doesn't allow scheduling a CronJob on the last day of the month. After searching around the Internet, this seems to be popular problem, fixed in some implementations of cron syntax [via `L` special character][1] in the day-of-month position (e.g. [AWS's EventBridge](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/eventbridge/latest/userguide/eb-create-rule-schedule.html) is among parties, who support it natively).

One popular way to overcome this involves a wrapper script, that runs on the last four days of each month (days 28-31), and checks the exact day, before executing the command. While works, this makes the original intent obscure, and is prone to human errors.

Note that Kubernetes relies on `github.com/robfig/cron/v3` in parsing the CronJob's schedule. The feature to support the "L" in the library was proposed in https://github.com/robfig/cron/pull/325 (in 2020) but it seems that the library was abandoned by the maintainer. As part of this feature request, I also suggest exploring if having the parts of k8s's API (part of the CronJob spec), to be one-to-one dependent on the capabilities of a (potentially unmaintained) library, is something that needs an attention.

[1]: https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cron#Cron_expression

### Why is this needed?

Running periodic tasks on the last day of the month is common a problem in different sorts of enterprise applications.

title: [KCCM]: service update while node sync is processing might impact ingress
body:
### What happened?

The Kubernetes cloud controller manager uses resource watchers to sync load balancers, a Node/Service watcher. The Node watcher is slower by nature since any Node event will sync all service load balancers on the cluster. The service watcher is quicker since it only syncs the service load balancer which the event relates to. 

How slow a Node sync is will vary on the cluster, i.e: amount of Services of `type: LoadBalancer` and Nodes, but on big clusters with a lot of churn: the time to process one Node sync can be sufficiently slow to have the cache of Nodes go stale w.r.t the actual cluster state. The cache of Nodes is here the resource informer cache. When syncing Nodes the Node control loop will list all Nodes in its cache and then iterate over all Services and sync their load balancers in parallel, see: https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/master/staging/src/k8s.io/cloud-provider/controllers/service/controller.go#L799-L818

If any Service experiences an update needing a load balancer sync, the Service controller will also list the Nodes in the informer cache, but retrieve a more up-to-date copy, see: https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/master/staging/src/k8s.io/cloud-provider/controllers/service/controller.go#L438-L451. 

During upgrades or similar operations where a lot of Nodes get added/deleted: it's rather easy for the following to occur;

1. Node sync is processing, N load balancers are synced
2. NodeY is added
2. Service update triggers sync for load balancer X. It lists and adds NodeY to the load balancer set
3. Node sync processes load balancer Y and removes NodeY from the load balancer set 

This add + remove from the load balancer set might impact ingress SLOs for any application running on NodeY after its creation. 

/sig network
/cc @thockin @aojea 

### What did you expect to happen?

Any node added to the load balancer set which doesn't have a reason (i.e: [predicate](https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/master/staging/src/k8s.io/cloud-provider/controllers/service/controller.go#L996-L1016)) to be removed should not be removed from the load balancer's set of backend nodes.  

### How can we reproduce it (as minimally and precisely as possible)?

Update a Service while an upgrade is on-going. Nodes risk being added/removed/added from the load balancer's set of backend nodes at sporadic moments. Alternatively, I have written a unit tests that exhibits the issue and while file a fix PR where this can be seen.  

### Anything else we need to know?

title: [KCCM]: handle coalesced node updates in the service controller
body:
### What happened?

On big clusters with a lot of churn, Node updates can be frequent. The service controller in the Kubernetes cloud controller manager (KCCM) uses an edge-triggered resource watcher for what concerns handling the Update events, see: https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/master/staging/src/k8s.io/cloud-provider/controllers/service/controller.go#L160-L176

This means that Node events which should trigger a sync (ex: the addition/removal of the label `exclude-from-load-balancer`) can be missed if multiple updates occur on the same object in a short amount of time. 

The `UpdateFunc` doc bloc even explicitly warns about patterns such as the one described above, see: https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/master/staging/src/k8s.io/client-go/tools/cache/controller.go#L207-L212

This pattern has always been used in the KCCM, but I believe that since some Node conditions which used to trigger re-syncs have been removed since 1.26, the error can be triggered more often now. Specifically on < 1.26, the `NotReady` condition on the Node used to trigger a re-sync. This condition usually occurs when the Node stabilizes, sometime after its initial creation. This covered the existing issue.    

/sig network
/sig cloud-provider
/cc @aojea @thockin 


### What did you expect to happen?

All Node events should get enqueued. The Node controller will compare the current set of nodes in its informer cache to the last set of Nodes it synced, if a change is observed the load balancer is synced, see: https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/master/staging/src/k8s.io/cloud-provider/controllers/service/controller.go#L746-L751 - this shouldn't even lead to additional syncs because of this.  

### How can we reproduce it (as minimally and precisely as possible)?

This can be observed on upgrading clusters with a lot of Nodes and Services of `type: LoadBalancer`. Some Nodes might get excluded from the load balancer's backend, not because they should be excluded but because the update which should include it is missed.

title: [KCCM]: service controller predicates might impact ingress SLO on GCP with InstanceGroup based Load Balancing
body:
### What happened?

In 1.26 the service controller in the Kubernetes cloud controller manage (KCCM) introduced a new mechanism for syncing load balancers based on predicates. The predicates applied will depend on "service classes", specifically if it's `externalTrafficPolicy: Local` or `Cluster`, see: https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/release-1.26/staging/src/k8s.io/cloud-provider/controllers/service/controller.go#L944-L947

This implementation is not well suited for internal GCP load balancers which use InstanceGroups. @People from Google, feel free to correct me: any cluster has all nodes grouped together into an instance group. Service of `type: LoadBalancer` have individual GCP load balancers, but these load balancers end up referencing the same instance group (which is the cluster's instance group). This means that the inclusion/exclusion predicates for any service, will trickle down and impact the cluster's global instance group, thereby impacting other services which don't necessarily apply the same set of predicates. Ex: `externalTrafficPolicy: Cluster` services exclude `NotReady` nodes, whereas `externalTrafficPolicy: Local` do not. A Node going `NotReady` will therefore be removed from all backends for `externalTrafficPolicy: Cluster` services, however on GCP with load balancer solution based on InstanceGroups: this means that the same node will be removed from all backends for `externalTrafficPolicy: Local` services too.    

This is NOT a problem on >= 1.27 using the feature `StableLoadBalancerNodeSet`, because all services on 1.27 using that feature gate will have the same set of predicates. 

### What did you expect to happen?

Node updates requiring the removal of the instance from load balancers belonging to services of `externalTrafficPolicy: Cluster` should not impact other services of `externalTrafficPolicy: Local`. 

### How can we reproduce it (as minimally and precisely as possible)?

Bring up a cluster using "Internal load balancers" on GCP. Define two services, one being `externalTrafficPolicy: Cluster` and the other `externalTrafficPolicy: Local`. Have one node go `NotReady`. The instance corresponding to that Node might be removed from the InstanceGroup backend of the `externalTrafficPolicy: Local` service. This will depend on the order the services are synced, if the `externalTrafficPolicy: Cluster` service is synced last then the instance will be removed.  

### Anything else we need to know?

This is actually not really _that_ bad, because the only different predicate between both is the readiness condition - and a node should go back to `Ready` if all is fine, and finally be included. But I wanted to raise this for issue for completeness sake so that it is known. 

### Kubernetes version

```console
$ kubectl version
```

title: Foreground deletion should only delete and wait for objects with `blockOwnerDeletion: true` set.
body:
### What happened?

According to the [docs](https://kubernetes.io/docs/concepts/architecture/garbage-collection/#foreground-deletion) the `foreground` and `background` delete modes have inconsistent behavior. For the `background` option a resource goes away when all owner objects disappear. For the `foreground`, any object owned by the object currently in the “deletion in progress” state is getting removed immediately. It does not matter if it is not directly attached to it.

### What did you expect to happen?

The `foreground` option should only affect objects with the `blockOwnerDeletion: true` set. These objects should be removed in a group. When an owner object is removed, garbage collection should issue delete requests only for those nodes on a graph, which are reachable by the ownership references with `blockOwnerDeletion: true` set.

The rest of the resources, owned by removed object should be removed using the default garbage collection setting.

### How can we reproduce it (as minimally and precisely as possible)?

Create any set of objects with valid ownership references being set, and observe the difference in behavior.

title: After upgrading k8s to version above 1.24, PVC is blocked in the UmountDevice stage
body:
### What happened?

After upgrading k8s from 1.20 to 1.24, we deleted  a pod using csi pvc on the node that had not been evicted before the upgrade. The pod was deleted successfully, but pvc was till mounted and attached to the node, if a new pod use the same pvc in another node, it will report Multi-Attach Error. In the kubelet log, we found the  error: 

Aug 22 14:51:36 ncije4dedvch9fjdtj8s0 kubelet[2444519]: E0822 14:51:36.720426 2444519 nestedpendingoperations.go:348] Operation for "{volumeName:kubernetes.io/csi/ebs.csi.volcengine.com^vol-k4ucb4dmcffxuv3316ea podName: nodeName:}" failed. No retries permitted until 2023-08-22 14:53:38.720408461 +0800 CST m=+12441.648359884 (durationBeforeRetry 2m2s). Error: GetDeviceMountRefs check failed for volume "pvc-230ac950-e2c6-46ee-add4-bc3138858b4a" (UniqueName: "kubernetes.io/csi/ebs.csi.volcengine.com^vol-k4ucb4dmcffxuv3316ea") on node "172.28.25.127" : the device mount path "/var/lib/kubelet/plugins/kubernetes.io/csi/ebs.csi.volcengine.com/493ac2db47f5eb2e95c0a7ba237e94ac3221f60c2be498cf70bd802123bc52f8/globalmount" is still mounted by other references [/var/lib/kubelet/plugins/kubernetes.io/csi/pv/pvc-230ac950-e2c6-46ee-add4-bc3138858b4a/globalmount /mnt/vdb/kubelet/plugins/kubernetes.io/csi/pv/pvc-230ac950-e2c6-46ee-add4-bc3138858b4a/globalmount /mnt/vdb/kubelet/plugins/kubernetes.io/csi/ebs.csi.volcengine.com/493ac2db47f5eb2e95c0a7ba237e94ac3221f60c2be498cf70bd802123bc52f8/globalmount]

### What did you expect to happen?

the csi pvc can be umount and detach successfuly after deleting pod, and new pod can be created successfully.

### How can we reproduce it (as minimally and precisely as possible)?

1. Deploy a k8s cluster with a version lower than 1.24, such as 1.23, 1.22
2. Running a pod that mounts a csi pvc needing mountDevice(representing NodeStageVolume in CSI call)
3. upgrading k8s version to 1.24 (for testing, we can only update kubelet binary and restart it)
4. delete the pod created in step 2
5. umountDevice the pvc will fail

### Anything else we need to know?

It is judged that the cloud disk pvc cannot be successfully unmounted because pvc failed in the UmountDevice stage. Further analysis of the root cause is as follows:
1. k8s version 1.24 has modified the global stagePath of pvc. For related background, please see https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/pull/107065
2. After upgrading kubelet, kubelet will be remounted in the new global stagePath.
3. If there are still pods using the pvc running on the node before upgrading kubelet, when the pod is deleted,  pvc enters the UmountDevice stage. Since the mount record of the old stagePath still exists,  it will report the error "is still mounted by other references" and the umountDevice cannot be successful.
https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/eafebcc9e368d6aeaab0ce5ec4fd56b94174d0c4/pkg/volume/util/operationexecutor/operation_generator.go#L951-L959

title: APF: Add a separate flowSchema (and priorityLevelConfiguration) for SubjectAccessReview
body:
### What would you like to be added?

Add a separate flowSchema (and priorityLevelConfiguration (PLC)) for SubjectAccessReview and other that related to authorization.
Option 1: add a new default `flowSchema` and corresponding PLC
Option 2: add a new default `flowSchema` that maps to a PLC like workload-high


### Why is this needed?

We have seen a common use case that user uses HPA controller that talks to a metrics server (an extension apiserver). 
HPA (part of kube-controller-manager) is in `kube-system` namespace and uses `workload-high` PLC.
Metrics server (e.g. prometheus adaptor) is commonly not in `kube-system` namespace and uses `workload-low` PLC.

The related workflow is linked here:
https://kubernetes.io/docs/tasks/extend-kubernetes/configure-aggregation-layer/#authentication-flow

HPA can have 500s when there is APF throttling in `workload-low` PLC that causes metrics server's `SubjectAccessReview` to be dropped (step 7 in the flow).
This issue is very non-trivial for users to understand and troubleshoot. In order to make users have a better experience and also hide some unnecessary complexity from users. I want to propose to adding additional default APF config as mentioned above. 

![authentication-flow](https://d33wubrfki0l68.cloudfront.net/3c5428678a95c3715894011d8dd4812d2cf229b9/e745c/images/docs/aggregation-api-auth-flow.png)

title: uneven Pods spreading across domains
body:
## What 

Implement an uneven Pod spreading constraints between domains. Like domainA:domainB = x:y.

This requires us to introduce a new field to `topologySpreadConstraints` (name it `domains` for now). 
When `domains` field is non-empty, `maxSkew` should be nil. (vise-versa)

```yaml
- topologySpreadConstraints:
    # ...
    domains:
      - topologyLabel: "domainA"
        weight: 7
      - topologyLabel: "domainB"
        weight: 3
```

## Usecases

### Usecase1: spread Pods between zones

```yaml
- topologySpreadConstraints:
    whenUnsatisfiable: DoNotSchedule
    labelSelector:
       matchLabels:
         app: foo
    topologyKey: "zone"
    domains:
      - topologyLabel: "zonea"
        weight: 7
      - topologyLabel: "zoneb"
        weight: 3
```

We have a DB in zoneA, so we want to schedule the Pods mostly to zoneA for better latency.
But, want to schedule smaller part of them to zone-b in case of zone failure.

### Usecases2: spread Pods for on-demand/spot

```yaml
- topologySpreadConstraints:
    labelSelector:
       matchLabels:
         app: foo
    topologyKey: "node-availability"
    domains:
      - topologyLabel: "on-demand"
        weight: 7
      - topologyLabel: "spot"
        weight: 3
```

So, we want to keep a large part of Pods running in on-demand Nodes because the spot instance might be deleted suddenly.
But, we're greedy, we want to keep some Pods in the spot Nodes for sure for the cost saving.

### Usecase3: gradual infrastructure migration

```yaml
- topologySpreadConstraints:
    labelSelector:
       matchLabels:
         app: foo
    topologyKey: "nodepool"
    domains:
      - topologyLabel: "old-nodepool"
        weight: 9 # will be reduced gradually
      - topologyLabel: "new-nodepool"
        weight: 1 # will be increased gradually
```

When we migrate workloads from one domain to another, we want to do it gradually.

## Why
 
Our company has one huge cluster to accommodate tons of Pods.

Currently, in order to achieve such uneven spreading, we need to choose either:
- create multiple deployments (+ HPA etc), one per domain. And somehow keep them to a specific ratio via some custom autoscaling solution.
  - It's hard to prepare multiple deployments in the first place when doing that for many services.(the usecase 2 / 3)
- use one deployment, but create the mutating webhook to add the required nodeaffinity to each Pod based on the current number of Pods in each domain. Also, descheduling should be done somehow.
- EDIT: Or follow [a similar way of Karpenter](https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/issues/121211#issuecomment-1761840082). 

All are not simple solutions, which require engineering effort a lot and could cause serious problems in case of bugs.

Also, again we're greedy, we want to have a fallback mechanism like https://github.com/kubernetes/enhancements/issues/3990 when it comes to usecase 2. So, there could be a stockout problem in spot instance↓, and have to fallback to on-demand if necessary. That is something very hard to achieve with a custom solution, but can be _hopefully_ done with this proposal + the enhancement mentioned earlier.

> Spot VMs have no availability guarantees. Design your systems under the assumption that GKE might reclaim any or all your Spot VMs at any time, with no guarantee of when new instances become available.
https://cloud.google.com/kubernetes-engine/docs/concepts/spot-vms

/kind feature
/sig scheduling
/assign @sanposhiho

title: The description of NodeStatusUpdateFrequency is inaccurate.

### What happened?

```
// nodeStatusUpdateFrequency is the frequency that kubelet computes node
// status. If node lease feature is not enabled, it is also the frequency that

// changing the constant, it must work with nodeMonitorGracePeriod in nodecontroller.
```

I noticed that the comment about NodeStatusUpdateFrequency is as before, `when NodeLease is enabled by default, it should not automatically post node status to the master.`

`
