title: New feature to allocate specific devices using DRA - usecase and design proposal
body:
### What would you like to be added?

Feature to allocate a specific device to a Pod using webhook to generate appropriate DRA resources from user's intention in Pod manifest.

![design drawio](https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/assets/7124738/9b3ece40-7424-4335-b25a-33c50ec9d708)

- Steps
  1. User appends node name and device ID (PCI address) to `.metadata.annotation` to Pod manifest
  2. Webhook converts the designation in `.metadata.annotation` into a set of resource claim and resource claim template
  3. DRA resource controller schedules the Pod to the designated node
  4. DRA driver allocates the designated device to the container(s) of the Pod

### Why is this needed?

Allocating a specific device to a Pod is meaningful in the following usecases.

1. **Efficient device allocation:** allocate an AI device which is located near a NIC on a PCI-Express bus to accelerate RDMA (e.g., `AI Device 2` is better for apps running both on `Node1` and `Node 2` in the picture below) - this can also be used by some automated tool to schedule Pods to the best location with certain cards w.r.t. co-working Pods
2. **Debugging:** allocate an unhealthy AI device to a debug-purpose Pod

![device-location drawio](https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/assets/7124738/afe55114-e36d-458b-9b2b-c6c9ca82b515)

In the current Kubernetes architecture, several challenges exist for the usecases.

1. With classic device plugin, no parameters like device ID can be specified in Pod manifest
2. With DRA, parameters can be defined in device class parameters and claim parameters, and therefore we need some additional mechanism if user wants to specify per-Pod parameters

title: dra helper: check and enhance error messages
body:
In https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/89dfbebe2e823bd0b13e4b65b8460a058c7258a3/staging/src/k8s.io/dynamic-resource-allocation/controller/controller.go#L386-L391
we have some generic fallback code that logs errors when putting an item back into the work queue.

This currently logs update conflicts as error:
```
        E1207 07:52:16.337365    3643 controller.go:386] "processing failed" err="update unsuitable node status: Operation cannot be fulfilled on podschedulingcontexts.resource.k8s.io \"test-dra279vm\": the object has been modified; please apply your changes to the latest version and try again"
```

We should only log errors when something needs the attention of an admin. This isn't the case here, the normal retry loop will take care of it.

With patching, that error goes away, but might be slower (see https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/issues/113700).

Some potential improvements:
- ignore "not found" on PodSchedulingContext status updates
- ignore "has been modified" on PodSchedulingContext status updates
- ignore "failed to allocate" on claim syncs:


        E1207 08:43:04.132072   19595 controller.go:388] "processing failed" err=<
                claim test-drakgxsp-resource-1a-c8nx2: failed allocating claim 2b8ded2d-0883-4dc5-b1c8-129151fb08bd

         >

title: Follow up #121985: Conformance test regarding the access of "/"
body:
### What happened?

The issue is to follow up discussions in #121985: running conformance test with the commonly used tool, sonobuoy, failed because the tool's test runner is lack of permission towards `/`. The original issue was resolved by changing the e2e (conformance) test of `/` to an integration test. Several problems remained:

1. The privilege requirement in [conformance-tests.md](https://github.com/kubernetes/community/blob/master/contributors/devel/sig-architecture/conformance-tests.md) is outdated. 
    > it is non-privileged (e.g., does not require root on nodes, access to raw network interfaces, or cluster admin permissions)
2. Root discovery is one of the least-privileged permissions, and is expected to be granted to every authenticated user but is not actually.
3. Should the result returned by `/` should be part of conformance?

1st and 2nd are straightforward to fix, not sure about 3rd, should we add a separate test or add a verification step in existing one like https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/pull/121283? With the fix of 2nd, e2e for `/` should no longer fail with any test runner.


cc @liggitt @sttts @BenTheElder @neolit123 @aojea 

### What did you expect to happen?

1. conformance-tests.md should be reflect the accurate permission requirement
2. Root discovery permission should be granted to all authenticated users.
3. Conformance test should check the result returned by `/`.

title: asw cache has different outerVolumeSpecName if populated by Reconstruction than by the mountAttachedVolumes in volumemanager reconciler
body:
### What happened?

Some of the pods on EKS Fargate gets stuck in ContainerCreating state with following error which auto resolves eventually.

```
  Warning  FailedMount      86s    kubelet            Unable to attach or mount volumes: unmounted volumes=[persistent-storage], unattached volumes=[persistent-storage kube-api-access-xbk2s]: timed out waiting for the condition
```

This issue might not be specific to EKS on Fargate.

### What did you expect to happen?

Pods should not get stuck in ContainerCreating state with FailedMount errors when other pods in the same replicas go into Running state. 

### How can we reproduce it (as minimally and precisely as possible)?

Create an EKS cluster with Fargate - https://eksctl.io/usage/fargate-support/#

Create an EFS fs - https://docs.aws.amazon.com/efs/latest/ug/getting-started.html

Apply PV, PVC and deployment with atleast 50 replicas - https://github.com/kubernetes-sigs/aws-efs-csi-driver/blob/master/examples/kubernetes/multiple_pods/README.md#multiple-pods-read-write-many

Out of 50 atleast 1 or 2 replicas will get stuck in ContainerCreating state due to FailedMounts.

### Anything else we need to know?

ActualStateOfWorld (ASW) cache is populated with volumes and its mounted pods by two ways.
* Through reconstruction in volume reconciler which marks the volumes as Uncertain and sets the OuterVolumeSpecName to the one read from PVC
* If volumes go though mounts in the reconciler even before the reconstruction and when mounts are successful, volumes are marked as Mounted and name is set to one read from podSpec

title: kubernetes/client-go:.github/PULL_REQUEST_TEMPLATE.md is unhelpful plus suggestion about SIG labelling
body: ### What happened? Drafting a PR to the [kubernetes/client-go repo](https://github.com/kubernetes/client-go) results in an unhelpful message with prose, but, no links, and the referenced content is a number of indirections away from anything remotely helpful. ### What did you expect to happen? The contents of the pr template should include links to relevant and helpful files. -- The `README.md` text should be a link to the master/HEAD file (this won't hurt someone who decides to edit the readme file in the repository or has already done so), and a reference to contributing should be a link to something that's useful and doesn't require following multiple links to get to an actual contributing file with useful information. ### How can we reproduce it (as minimally and precisely as possible)? 1. do the work to construct a code commit for a repository 2. prepare to create a PR: https://github.com/kubernetes/client-go/compare/master...jsoref:client-go:issue-1321?expand=1 3. read the message 4. Note that `README.md` and `CONTRIBUTING.md` aren't links to anything which means you now have to go back **x** pages just to try to find them 5. Assuming you've decided that the `README.md` isn't applicable, you now have to browse to (many steps, especially if you didn't start in the repository itself, which you won't in most cases, e.g. here, ...) and open [`CONTRIBUTING.md`](https://github.com/kubernetes/client-go/blob/master/CONTRIBUTING.md) 6. Read that text and realize that there was no need for the previous document to reference it -- the relevant text could have been inlined and the reference could have been to "the same [contributing guide](https://git.k8s.io/kubernetes/CONTRIBUTING.md)" 7. Open https://git.k8s.io/kubernetes/CONTRIBUTING.md 8. Read that even shorter text and realize that it too was a waste of reading (if you haven't gotten frustrated yet, you're doing way better than a newcomer, please let go of your prior knowledge, slow down, and recognize that all of these links and pages are actually frustrating) 9. Get to "check out the [Contributor's Guide](https://git.k8s.io/community/contributors/guide/)" and sigh. 10. Follow another link to another "Contributor's Guide" (https://github.com/kubernetes/community/tree/master/contributors/guide 11. Note that this one randomly dumped you into a directory instead of an _anything_, so you'll probably have to scroll past all of the files to get to the readme -- if you haven't asked "why is this happening", you're using too much experience -- take a break, come back pretending that you don't know much about k8s and do understand that links **can** and **should** take you somewhere useful instead of dumping you into a [gopher menu](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gopher_(protocol)) from 1991. 12. Scroll down to https://github.com/kubernetes/community/tree/master/contributors/guide#readme 13. Read some metadata 14. Scroll down to https://github.com/kubernetes/community/tree/master/contributors/guide#getting-started 15. Read a ToC 16. title: postContainer - something to run after container success exit
body:
### What would you like to be added?

We have the ability of an initContainer for pods.  It would be nice to have postConatiner that would run after the pod has exited successfully.  

```apiVersion: batch/v1
kind: Job
metadata:
  name: big-job
spec:
  template:
    spec:
      initContainers:
      - image: 192.168.4.120:5000/s3-pull:v1.000
        command:
        - "dotnet"
        - "s3Pull.dll"
        - "http://192.168.4.120:4566"
        - "/data/input"
        name: s3-pull
        volumeMounts:
        - name: shared-dir
          mountPath: /data
      containers:
      - name: big-job
        image: 192.168.4.120:5000/job-test:v1.001
        command: ["dotnet",  "jobTest.dll"]
        volumeMounts:
        - name: shared-dir
          mountPath: /data
      postContainers:
      - image: 192.168.4.120:5000/s3-push:v1.000
        command:
        - "dotnet"
        - "s3Push.dll"
        - "http://192.168.4.120:4566"
        - "/data/output"
        name: s3-push
        volumeMounts:
        - name: shared-dir
          mountPath: /data
      volumes:
      - name: shared-dir
        emptyDir: {}
      restartPolicy: Never
  backoffLimit: 4
```

### Why is this needed?

I have a situation where I'm receiving containers from a 3rd party.  I can use an initContainer to load files from s3 into the pod's directory so that the 3rd party doesn't have to worry about s3, key distribution etc.  The contain then executes and places the results in a specific location.  However, currently I have to put those in persistent volume claim and have a separate process monitoring it to push the data into s3.  It would be very nice to have a postContainer that runs after the job has completed and has access to the job's directory that could push the files to s3.

title: return a bookmark event with bookmarkafterresourceversion immediately to reduce WatchList time cost
body:
### What happened?

the resource version of the bookmark event returned by watchlist maybe larger than bookmarkafterresourceversion. which means there need more 1 ~ 1.25s to return even the event with bookmarkresourceversion already received in cacher.

### What did you expect to happen?

return a bookmark event with bookmarkafterresourceversion immediately when to sendWatchCacheEvent in cacheWatcher if the resource version already not elder than bookmarkafterresourceversion.
DON‘T wait another cycle of bookmark timer.

### How can we reproduce it (as minimally and precisely as possible)?

https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/master/staging/src/k8s.io/apiserver/pkg/storage/cacher/cacher.go#L899
there is a bookmark timer triggered every 1 ~ 1.25s.
https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/master/staging/src/k8s.io/apiserver/pkg/storage/cacher/cache_watcher.go#L527-L529
```golang
if event.ResourceVersion > resourceVersion || (event.Type == watch.Bookmark && event.ResourceVersion == resourceVersion && !c.wasBookmarkAfterRvSent()) {
    c.sendWatchCacheEvent(event)
}
```
the resourceversion passed to process function is just bookmarkafterresourversion.
consider the following scenario

1. bookmark event come at t1 with resourceversion < bookmarkresourceversion, no action
2. normal event come at t2 with resourceversion = bookmarkresourceversion, no action
3. normal event come at t3 with resourceversion > bookmarkresourceversion, then the event will be send to client
4. bookmark event come at t4 with resourceversion > bookmarkresourceversion, then the bookmark will be set with an special annotation and return to client

t4 - t1 = 1s ~ 1.25s

the final bookmark event can be send back to client at t1. this will reduce one bookmark timer cycle for watchlist request in some scenario. In extreme cases, this time factor may lead to a timeout for the watchlist request.

### Anything else we need to know?

_No response_

title: topologySpreadConstraints not working as expected if the topologyKey is not set in the nodes
body:
### What happened?

When setting topologySpreadContraints with ScheduleAyway whenUnsatisfiable param set the scheduling is not working as it expected if multiple constraints are set at the same time
Instead of splitting workload among all available workers , all workloads goes to the same node or they are note evenly distributed.

No other affinities nor nodeSelector are set

### What did you expect to happen?

All the replicas should be evenly distributed among all available workers

### How can we reproduce it (as minimally and precisely as possible)?

Create any deployment with the following topologySpreadConstraints:

```yaml
spec:
  replicas: 3
  selector:
    matchLabels:
      app: foo
  template:
    metadata:
      labels:
        app: foo
    spec:
      topologySpreadConstraints:
      - maxSkew: 1
        topologyKey: kubernetes.io/hostname
        whenUnsatisfiable: DoNotSchedule
        labelSelector:
          matchLabels:
            app: foo
      - maxSkew: 1
        topologyKey: topology.kubernetes.io/zone
        whenUnsatisfiable: ScheduleAnyway
        labelSelector:
          matchLabels:
            app: foo
```

Check created pods are not evenly distributed

### Anything else we need to know?

**It seems if we remove the zone constraint, the scheduler works fine again**

Important note: it only fails if the nodes doesn't have the label which is configured in the constraint present

In GA of swap, our goal would be that users/admins can enable swap for their nodes. It could be possible to have a heterogenous cluster where some nodes have swap enabled and others do not.

This could cause problems with scheduling.

We should investigate and see if there is ways to control this on a heterogeneous cluster.

title: Pod Container.Command doesn't respect ulimit set in `etc/bash/bash.rc`
body:
### What happened?

There's a good chance I'm misunderstanding how the command runs against the container, but from what I understand, this is doing `exec -- bin/bash -c <command>` and so I'd expect the ulimit to apply there as well but it doesn't. 


With the following dockerfile:

<details>

```

ARG DEBIAN_FRONTEND=noninteractive
```

```
spec:

    resources:
```

title: NodeAffinity/NodeUnschedulable QueueingHint may miss Node related events that make Pod schedulable
body:
### What happened?

/kind bug
/triage accepted
/priority urgent
/sig scheduling
/assign

NodeAffinity QueueingHint may miss Node related events that make Pod schedulable because of preCheck.
It's similar to: https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/pull/119177#issuecomment-1820091877

So:
1. Node is added. But, it's filtered out by preCheck (due to node's unready or whatever) and the scheduling queue doesn't receive NodeAdded. (noderesourcefit cannot receive NodeAdded.)
2. Node is updated and ready now. But, this event is NodeUpdated.

In such scenarios, NodeAffinity may return `QueueSkip` to the event due to (2).
https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/master/pkg/scheduler/framework/plugins/nodeaffinity/node_affinity.go#L94-L131

### What did you expect to happen?

We have to loosen the filtering in `isSchedulableAfterNodeChange` until preCheck is removed.
https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/issues/110175

### How can we reproduce it (as minimally and precisely as possible)?

1. Create a Pod with NodeAffinity under the situation where no Node can accommodate the Pod.
2. Create a new Node.

It may cause the above problematic scenario.

title: Already API-evicted Pods do not get evicted by the kubelet eviction manager (memory pressure, ephemeral storage pressure)
body:
### What happened?

When pods have a long _terminationGracePeriod_ and get evicted by downscaling or some other reason (via API) the eviction is initiated which respects that long _terminationGracePeriod_. This works fine.

If the pods need to be evicted due to memory pressure on the node after the already initiated API eviction there is no more eviction done with the specified _evictionMaxPodGracePeriod_ of the kubelet. This means that the second eviction due to e.g. memory pressure cannot be successful at all when you have large _terminationGracePeriod_ on your pod and there was a prior unrelated API eviction.

![image](https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/assets/28532557/9d83248f-7dfe-49b0-88b0-7b7e9f73faf6)


### What did you expect to happen?

The eviction manager triggered eviction due to memory pressure should still be issued with the specified _evictionMaxPodGracePeriod_ even if there was a prior API based eviction with a large terminationGracePeriod.



### How can we reproduce it (as minimally and precisely as possible)?

- Create a workload pod that does ignore sig-terms
- Specify a large _terminationGracePeriod_ for that pod, do not set any memory limits for the pod
- Specify a small _evictionMaxPodGracePeriod_ for the kubelet on the node
- API evict the Pod
- Make sure the kubelet wants to evict the pod (e.g. by allocating memory inside pod until the node is under memory pressure)


### Anything else we need to know?

The bug was not present in k8s 1.25.x

title: A mechanism to fail a Pod that is stuck due to an invalid Image
body:
### What would you like to be added?

A mechanism to set a Pod into phase=Failed when the image pull has failed for a number of times (perhaps configurable).
Currently, the Pod just stays in phase=Pending

### Why is this needed?

This is especially problematic for Jobs submitted through a queueing system.

In a queued environment, the time when the job starts running (pods created) might be hours or even days after the Job is created. Then, the user that submitted the job might not realize their mistake until it's too late. Since these Pods block resources in the cluster, it might cause other pending Jobs not to start.

If the Pods stay in phase=Pending, the job controller cannot do anything about them, as it only does "failure handling" once the Pods actually terminate with a phase=Failed.

title: Change Reclaim Policy from default "Delete" for Dynamic PV via PVC manifest

### What would you like to be added?

The ability to change the default ReclaimPolicy from "Delete" to "Retain" or "Recycle" for a dynamic PV.
This should be via PVC manifest which creates this dynamic PV.

### Why is this needed?

Currently this can only be done manually which makes it difficult to manage via tools like Kustomize.
Storage class can be set to Retain. But this is required in scenarios where only few PVs need to be set at Retain. This feature would make it easy to make this change.

title: Deletion of upgrade-health-check during the upgrade preflight could fail  due to a race condition and surfaced as CreateJob failure
body:
### What happened?

I have seen false positives in the upgrade preflight where `CreateJob` fails because `kube-system/upgrade-health-check` job is not found when trying to delete it.

Looking at the code, there is a bit of inconsistent treatment in the creation and the deletion of the job during the cluster health check.

When creating the job to test if a job can be created on the cluster, [the job creation accounts for a possibility of race condition and have a retry to mitigate this](https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/master/cmd/kubeadm/app/phases/upgrade/health.go#L154-L163).

However, the deletion code doesn't take care of the same race condition in two places:
1. https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/master/cmd/kubeadm/app/phases/upgrade/health.go#L142-L147
2. https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/master/cmd/kubeadm/app/phases/upgrade/health.go#L149-L152

Specifically, I think [deleteHealthCheckJob](https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/master/cmd/kubeadm/app/phases/upgrade/health.go#L197-L204) should ignore `NotFound` errors to be resilient to the cases where the job was deleted by another client (basically `--ignore-not-found=true` is what we want here).


### What did you expect to happen?

Ignore `NotFound` error when attempting to delete the `upgrade-health-check` job.

### How can we reproduce it (as minimally and precisely as possible)?

With 3 control plane node setup and run `kubeadm upgrade plan` on three nodes at the same time and this probably happens once in a while.

### Anything else we need to know?

If the requested change sounds reasonable, I can work on making the changes.

ref: https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/pull/122289#issuecomment-1853266698
/sig scheduling
/kind cleanup
 
Part of: https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/issues/122284#issuecomment-1853346333.

---

The unit test `TestPriorityQueue_MoveAllToActiveOrBackoffQueue` in the scheduling queue only assumes the case where the queueing hint is enabled. We should make another unit test to confirm `MoveAllToActiveOrBackoffQueue` works without QHint.
`TestPriorityQueue_MoveAllToActiveOrBackoffQueue` should have been existing since before we introduced QHint. So, just bring the old one back should be fine.

title: Implement the integration tests for requeueing scenarios
body:
/sig scheduling
/priority important-soon
/kind feature

Part of: https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/issues/122284#issuecomment-1853346333.


We have few tests to check the scheduler's requeueing scenario in the integration test. 
We should have the one so that we can catch a bug like https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/issues/122284, which only happens the scheduling queue is actually working.

---

Here's the list of plugins with QueueingHint.
Basically, I believe we can just pile up the test cases in the existing [TestCoreResourceEnqueue](https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/746f08a8da0a45e8b1a46362822db05cb11ed294/test/integration/scheduler/queue_test.go#L188).
Also, note that we have to cover major scenarios only, don't have to cover minor ones within the integration test.

title: plugins that register nodeAdd in EventsToRegister must register nodeUpdate
body:
/sig scheduling
/priority important-soon
/assign
/kind feature

Part of: https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/issues/122284#issuecomment-1853346333.

---

Plugins may miss Node-related events that make Pod schedulable because of preCheck.
It's similar to: https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/pull/119177#issuecomment-1820091877

1. Node is added. But, it's filtered out by preCheck (due to node's unready or whatever) and the scheduling queue doesn't receive NodeAdded. (noderesourcefit cannot receive NodeAdded.)
2. Node is updated and ready now. But, this event is NodeUpdated.

So, no matter whether plugins have QueueingHint or not, plugins must register NodeUpdate event when they're interested in NodeAdd. Also, in case they have QHint, they should take this scenario into consideration.

title: False MountVolume.NodeExpandVolume failure warning message for readOnly pods
body:
### What happened?

Created a RWX volume and mounted it on a pod having readOnly flag set to true.

While the volume provisioning happened successfully, we did observe some warning message on describing the pod:

`Warning  FileSystemResizeFailed  27m   kubelet                  MountVolume.NodeExpandVolume failed for volume "pvc-d766a8a5-a6ba-49f4-a560-0c5e15b4ab74" requested read-only file system
 `

It seems like this message is being triggered from here: https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/master/pkg/volume/util/operationexecutor/operation_generator.go#L2079


But we never did an expand volume call, so we should not be seeing warning message. It can be confusing to see this warning message.

### What did you expect to happen?

The warning message should not be displayed when expand volume was not even called.

### How can we reproduce it (as minimally and precisely as possible)?

title: vSphere CSI migration is broken in 1.29.0
body:
### What happened?

A pod that uses in-tree vSphere volume never starts in Kubernetes 1.29.0.

### What did you expect to happen?

Such pod should start as usual.

### How can we reproduce it (as minimally and precisely as possible)?

See above

### Anything else we need to know?

Feature gate `CSIMigrationvSphere` removal deleted [migratedPlugins entry](https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/pull/121291/files#diff-32db45470d72c3ae912f67283391dbab2b744291c16825458c05d72f401031b9L239-L241) that vSphere volumes are migrated to CSI. So the CSI volume plugin ignores in-tree vSphere volumes and does not translate them to CSI.

body:
### What happened?


I am running a Kubernetes cluster with version 1.20.11 and Containerd as the runtime. I am currently experiencing an issue where if a node does not have any pods scheduled on it for a period of time, when a pod is eventually scheduled on that node, all pods on the node are restarted. title: the score of TaintToleration
body:
### What happened?

```
// Score invoked at the Score extension point.
func (pl *TaintToleration) Score(ctx context.Context, state *framework.CycleState, pod *v1.Pod, nodeName string) (int64, *framework.Status) {
	nodeInfo, err := pl.handle.SnapshotSharedLister().NodeInfos().Get(nodeName)
	if err != nil {
		return 0, framework.AsStatus(fmt.Errorf("getting node %q from Snapshot: %w", nodeName, err))
	}
	node := nodeInfo.Node()

	s, err := getPreScoreState(state)
	if err != nil {
		return 0, framework.AsStatus(err)
	}

	score := int64(countIntolerableTaintsPreferNoSchedule(node.Spec.Taints, s.tolerationsPreferNoSchedule))
	return score, nil
}

// CountIntolerableTaintsPreferNoSchedule gives the count of intolerable taints of a pod with effect PreferNoSchedule
func countIntolerableTaintsPreferNoSchedule(taints []v1.Taint, tolerations []v1.Toleration) (intolerableTaints int) {
	for _, taint := range taints {
		// check only on taints that have effect PreferNoSchedule
		if taint.Effect != v1.TaintEffectPreferNoSchedule {
			continue
		}

		if !v1helper.TolerationsTolerateTaint(tolerations, &taint) {
			intolerableTaints++
		}
	}
	return
}

```
Why the greater the number of intolerable stains, the higher the score? For PreferNoSchedule, the system will try to avoid placing a pod that does not tolerate the taint on the node.  How this is done?



### What did you expect to happen?

The more stains that cannot be tolerated, the lower the score.

title: Support skip watch Headless Service in server-side.
body:
### What would you like to be added?

Support watch service with field-selector spec.clusterIP!=None to skip headless service in kube-apiserver. And kubelet/kube-proxy can skip watch headless-service in the future.
![image](https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/assets/42128207/55a3df12-e70d-4b09-b5a4-a5a6ebff890e)

Now, endpoints will be added labels [service.kubernetes.io/headless](https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/master/pkg/controller/endpoint/endpoints_controller.go#L518) for headless service  by endpoints-controller,  and kube-proxy will ignore  event for it by label-selector. https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/master/cmd/kube-proxy/app/server.go#L913. But headless service haven't be added label and kube-proxy  still watch for it.

For kubelet, it watch service to add service-env for pods , but it ignores headless service when  build service-env-map(https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/master/pkg/kubelet/kubelet_pods.go#L549). So kubelet don't need to watch headless service either.

### Why is this needed?

In a large-cluster with more then 5000 nodes,  when we run kubeflow task( tfjob:pod:headlessService=1:10:10) with qps 10, it can save huge network bandwidth and cpu for kube-apiserver.

title: The status of asw in attachDetachController is inconsistent with the actual node status
body:
### What happened?

We are operating a Kubernetes (k8s) cluster that utilizes a scheduler extender to schedule pods from a StatefulSet onto fixed nodes respectively. And then, these pods would mount some volumes. We routinely delete and restart pods, performing this operation thousands of times weekly. However, we encounter an issue every few weeks where, after deleting a pod and scheduling it back to its original node, the associated volume fails to mount. As a result, this causes the pod to enter a perpetual ContainerCreating state.
```shell
# kubectl describe pod x
  Warning  FailedMount  105s (x30 over 67m)  kubelet, h34b07425.na61  Unable to mount volumes for pod "*": timeout expired waiting for volumes to attach or mount for pod "*". list of unmounted volumes=[*]. list of unattached volumes=[*]
```

We have traced the issue to the attach/detach (ad) controller. It appears that the node volume does not successfully attach, yet the actual state of the world (asw) cache within the ad controller mistakenly believes that it has. This discrepancy prevents the pod from proceeding with the mount operation.

Upon reviewing the kube-controller-manager logs, we noticed the following:
```shell
I1211 00:42:07.780851       1 node_status_updater.go:106] Updating status "{\"status\":{\"volumesAttached\":[{\"devicePath\":\"\",\"name\":\"kubernetes.io/csi/csi-hostpath^6583bc90-0677-11ee-a5d3-506b4b2b7da6\"}]}}" for node "h34b07425.na61" succeeded. VolumesAttached: [{kubernetes.io/csi/csi-hostpath^6583bc90-0677-11ee-a5d3-506b4b2b7da6 }]
...
I1211 00:42:08.261836       1 node_status_updater.go:106] Updating status "{}" for node "h34b07425.na61" succeeded. VolumesAttached: [{kubernetes.io/csi/csi-hostpath^6583bc90-0677-11ee-a5d3-506b4b2b7da6 } {kubernetes.io/csi/csi-hostpath^3d7384a6-068e-11ee-a5d3-506b4b2b7da6 }]
```
The issue seems to stem from a delay in the informer syncing the node information from the API server after a DetachVolume has been invoked, resulting in the informer not accurately reflecting the node's most recent status. It incorrectly assumes that the volume is still attached to the node. 

```go
// pkg/controller/volume/attachdetach/reconciler/reconciler.go
func (rc *reconciler) reconcile(ctx context.Context) {
		err = rc.nodeStatusUpdater.UpdateNodeStatusForNode(logger, attachedVolume.NodeName)
		...
		err = rc.attacherDetacher.DetachVolume(logger, attachedVolume.AttachedVolume, verifySafeToDetach, rc.actualStateOfWorld)
	...
	rc.attachDesiredVolumes(logger)

	// Update Node Status
	err := rc.nodeStatusUpdater.UpdateNodeStatuses(logger)
	...
}
```
After the pod schedules back to the original nodes and ad-controller finishes the AttachVolume operation, the nodeStatusUpdater.updateNodeStatus() function returns nil without retrying, regardless of whether there were any updates. 
```go
// pkg/controller/volume/attachdetach/statusupdater/node_status_updater.go
func (nsu *nodeStatusUpdater) processNodeVolumes(logger klog.Logger, nodeName types.NodeName, attachedVolumes []v1.AttachedVolume) error {
	nodeObj, err := nsu.nodeLister.Get(string(nodeName))
	...
	err = nsu.updateNodeStatus(logger, nodeName, nodeObj, attachedVolumes)
	...
}

func (nsu *nodeStatusUpdater) updateNodeStatus(logger klog.Logger, nodeName types.NodeName, nodeObj *v1.Node, attachedVolumes []v1.AttachedVolume) error {
	node := nodeObj.DeepCopy()
	node.Status.VolumesAttached = attachedVolumes
	_, patchBytes, err := nodeutil.PatchNodeStatus(nsu.kubeClient.CoreV1(), nodeName, nodeObj, node)
	if err != nil {
		return err
	}
	logger.V(4).Info("Updating status for node succeeded", "node", klog.KObj(node), "patchBytes", patchBytes, "attachedVolumes", attachedVolumes)
	return nil
}
```
As a consequence, the asw is misled by the informer to believe that all volumes that should be attached to the node have been successfully attached. However, by inspecting the output of kubectl, it is evident that status.volumesAttached does not include the said volume. 

**TL; DR**

```shell
Below is the steps where the problem occurred, with the timeline proceeding from top to bottom.
1. kubectl delete pod
2. ad-controller watch pod deleted, call dsw.Deletepod()
3. ad-controller reconciler() every 100ms period: 
		3.1 asw.RemoveVolumeFromReportAsAttached()
		3.2 nodeStatusUpdater.UpdateNodeStatusForNode()  // remove volume from node status.volumesAttached
		3.3 attacherDetacher.DetachVolume()
4. kube-controller-manager recreate the pod, and the pod is scheduled back to the original node
5. ad-controller watch pod created, call dsw.AddPod()
		3.4 attacherDetacher.AttachVolume()
		3.5 nodeStatusUpdater.UpdateNodeStatuses() // nsu.nodeLister.get() get a cached node, with the volume has not been removed by step-3.2. Since the pod is scheduled to the original node, the volumesAttached of the node is the same as before(step-3.2), thus the update operation will do nothing.
```


### What did you expect to happen?

If nodeStatusUpdater.updateNodeStatus() patches nothing by comparing with the informer's nodes, there should be a retry. 

### How can we reproduce it (as minimally and precisely as possible)?

it's hard to reproduce. But you may make it by these steps:
1. Use scheduler-extender to schedule pods onto fixed nodes
2. Increase apiserver load manually(let the informer sync delay)
3. Delete large mounts of statefulset pods with volumes for several times


### Anything else we need to know?

Our Kubernetes version is v1.13.3, but The problem still exists in the latest version

title: Kubernetes conflicts with AppLocker on Windows PCs
body:
Dear Kubernetes Team,
We have a considerable number of users who utilize your software tools such as kube forwarder, k9s, kubectl etc. for a variety of tasks, a number that is consistently growing.
However, we are encountering recurring issues due to conflicts between your software and our security solutions, notably AppLocker, Microsoft's application control feature. 
This primarily stems from the fact that you have opted not to sign your software or situate it within program files. As a result, we are compelled to authorize the software based on its filehash, but this obviously changed at each software update.
This situation is not only causing administrative difficulties for us (Without a doubt other customer as well), but it is also proving problematic for the developers who use your software tools.
I hope you will consider this, as it will make your software way more enterprise friendly.
BR

there is a note above hostAliases that this feature does not work with hostNework=true, yet it seems it does:
https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/master/staging/src/k8s.io/api/core/v1/types.go#L3672-L3679

> This is only valid for non-hostNetwork pods.

when testing with a hostNetwork pod + hostAliases, there are no errors in kubelet logs at --v=10 related to this, in fact i don't see any hostAlias entries at all in there.

i could not find anything blocking this in the kubelet, in fact there is normal handling of hostNetwork:
https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/master/pkg/kubelet/kubelet_pods.go#L330

i could not find any validation performed on the hostAliases field of PodSpec if hostNetwork is true on the API level.
https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/38f4f9d8c4c0519917464b40997e8bcb478c8f8c/pkg/apis/core/validation/validation.go#L3888

i could not find any unit tests or e2e tests related to this.

### What did you expect to happen?

- the godoc should contain valid information
- if the feature is not supposed to work, it must be patched to not have the entries in the hosts file (perhaps?)
- we should have tests that ensure this type of requirement is guaranteed

### How can we reproduce it (as minimally and precisely as possible)?

these steps confirm that a static pod with hostNework (deployed by kubeadm) does make use of hostAliases.

- create a kubeadm single node cluster directly with `kubeadm init` or one with `kind create cluster`
- modify the `/etc/kubernetes/manifests/kube-apiserver.yaml` to include:
```
  hostAliases:
  - hostnames:
    - kubernetes
    ip: 127.0.0.1
```
- wait some time for the new static pod spec to resync
- find the PID of the kube-apiserver
```
ps -ax | grep kube-apiserver
```
- get the hosts file
```
cat /proc/<pid>/root/etc/hosts
```

```
# Kubernetes-managed hosts file (host network).

127.0.1.1	lubo-it

# The following lines are desirable for IPv6 capable hosts
::1     ip6-localhost ip6-loopback

ff00::0 ip6-mcastprefix
ff02::1 ip6-allnodes
ff02::2 ip6-allrouters
```

```
...
  hostNetwork: true
```

- k8s e2e test framework uses SSH client to fetch logs etc.

title: K8s cluster, issue with access timeout of 1 second
body:
Background:    Now we are preparing to launch ISIO and have built a new K8S environment. When switching traffic again, we found many 502 and other issues.
The k8s version is 1.26.9
The Istio version is http://docker.io/istio/pilot:1.18.2 And http://docker.io/istio/proxyv2:1.18.2
Containerd is 1.6.26
Calico is http://docker.io/calico/kube-controllers:v3.26.1
Phenomenon: Through shell script loop curl, it is found that there will be a link timeout exceeding 1 second (normally 3-5 milliseconds) (directly curl the nodeport of istio)
Troubleshooting process:
1. Try switching to different virtual machines, changing the host of the virtual machine, upgrading the kernel, upgrading the operating system, and adjusting kernel parameters; Some machines have been restored after adjustment, but the same operation cannot be performed on other machines.
2. So, in the development and testing environment, containerd was downgraded to version 1.6.10, and it was found that the development environment was improved, with 1.8 million attempts without any timeout. The frequency of timeout in the testing environment has decreased, to 1.5 million times, with approximately 2000 timeouts.
3. I tested the SVC Nodeport of the internal services of the cluster without using Istio, and found that there were no issues with me
I don't know if it's an issue with Istio, because some machines can pass through Istio without any problems.
4. When testing different nodes in the cluster, it was found that the timeout frequency of limited nodes was relatively high, and some did not find timeouts.
5. The packet capture has been reset, as detailed below:

title: Topology Aware Routing: Unable to allocate minimum required endpoints to each zone without exceeding overload threshold
body:
### What happened?

Given that we have 3 availability zones and even spread of nodes/CPU across all of those topology domains, we end up with a cpu ratio of `[0.333, 0.333, 0.333]`

Given that the workload has `HorizontalPodAutoscaler`, it can scale up and down with random assignment to zones but never with a skew of more than 1.

The workload had a spread of `[4, 4, 3]` across topology domains (a total of 11 `Pods` / `EndPoints`). This leads to an error of `Unable to allocate minimum required endpoints to each zone without exceeding overload threshold (11 endpoints, 3 zones)`

Given the [code logic here](https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/755b4e2bc493518f916e1b1ba11652a44b9fdc58/staging/src/k8s.io/endpointslice/topologycache/topologycache.go#L315C46-L331):
- `cpuRatiosByZone` of `[0.333, 0.333, 0.333]`
- `numEndpoints` of 11
- => `remainingMinEndpoints` ends up being `-1`
- => removes hints

![image](https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/assets/9448877/f10b8d01-44c6-4b14-b145-f706df94dc3b)



### What did you expect to happen?

Spread of `[4, 4, 3]` is capable of handling same zone traffic so I would expect the hints to not be removed.

### How can we reproduce it (as minimally and precisely as possible)?

- Set up nodes across 3 zones
- Setup a Deployment or StatefulSet with 9 replicas evenly spread across zones (can use `topologySpreadConstraints` of `DoNotSchedule` with `topology.kubernetes.io/zone` key and `maxSkew` of 1)
- Observe a spread of `[3, 3, 3]` across zones
- Observe that hints are created
- Scale to 11 replicas to force a spread of `[4, 4, 3]`
- Observe that hints are removed

### Anything else we need to know?

title: QueueingHints(Pod/delete) have to consider that "unassume Pod" is treated as Pod/delete
body:
### What happened?


> Side question: What if the unscheduled Pod was assumed?
https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/pull/122360#discussion_r1431547953

This question made me wonder what if the Pod was unassumed. 

1. Only one Node which can accomodate only one Pod exists. 
2. Pod-a is assumed to the Node. (but not yet actually bound)
3. Pod-b is rejected because the scheduler assumes Pod-a.
4. Pod-a is somehow unassumed. **It's treated as Pod/delete event.**
5. Pod-a goes to the scheduling queue. Now, the Node has a free space though, will Pod-b be retried? Well, it's depending on the implementation of QHints of Pod/delete...

---

These are plugins that have this problem.

- [ ] nodeports
- [ ] noderesource

For example, nodeports:

> // If the deleted pod is unscheduled, it doesn't make the target pod schedulable.
https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/42ab3b7b40c34e91b63589ae905ed918752a4a36/pkg/scheduler/framework/plugins/nodeports/node_ports.go#L136

This is not true, because if the deleted pod is assumed Pod, it makes the target pod schedulable.


### What did you expect to happen?

1. Only one Node which can accomodate only one Pod exists. 
2. Pod-a is assumed to the Node. (but not yet actually bound)
3. Pod-b is rejected because the scheduler assumes Pod-a.
4. Pod-a is somehow unassumed. **It's treated as Pod/delete event.**
5. Pod-a goes to the scheduling queue. **noderesourcefit receives Pod/delete event by (4), and it moves Pod-b to activeQ/backoffQ.**


### How can we reproduce it (as minimally and precisely as possible)?

The above scenario.

title: Backport docker/distribution patch to k8s 1.26 and 1.27
body:
### What would you like to be added?

[This patch PR](https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/pull/118036/files) was applied earlier this year to k8s >=1.28. As a vulnerability that shows up in the Federal compliance scans/reports that are binding to enterprises operating in the Federal space, it should be included in security patches of all supported k8s release lines, including 1.26 and 1.27. Without that, we are put in the position of having to rush out major releases with breaking changes to attain a security patch. 

The CVE in question is https://nvd.nist.gov/vuln/detail/CVE-2023-2253
It was resolved in https://github.com/distribution/distribution/releases/tag/v2.8.2. And the PR above bumps kubernetes to use v2.8.2, so I think all the work is done; it just needs a backport.

### Why is this needed?

Resolves https://nvd.nist.gov/vuln/detail/CVE-2023-2253

body:
### What happened?

Hi, all. The option `align-by-socket` doesn't work in my env. Here are the steps:
1. Change the kubelet config (/var/lib/kubelet/config.yaml) and add the following configs:
```
cpuManagerPolicy: static
systemReserved:
  cpu: 500m
  memory: 256M
kubeReserved:
  cpu: 500m
```
2. Add the `align-by-socket` option in the `/var/lib/kubelet/kubeadm-flags.env`:
```
KUBELET_KUBEADM_ARGS="--feature-gates=CPUManagerPolicyAlphaOptions=true --container-runtime-endpoint=unix:///run/containerd/containerd.sock --pod-infra-container-image=registry.k8s.io/pause:3.9 --cpu-manager-policy-options=align-by-socket=true"
```

The cpuset of these pods should align by socket.

### How can we reproduce it (as minimally and precisely as possible)?

Create a nginx yaml and scale it to 6:

```
apiVersion: apps/v1
```

We're upgrading from K8S 1.20 to 1.28.(4) EKS and naturally encountering things that don't work.

title: Faster ResourceQutoa Replenishment
body:
### What would you like to be added?

An enhancement to make the resource quota replenishment faster when resources are updated or deleted. 

### Why is this needed?

The resource quota controller does full sync of resource quotas periodically. And the resource update/delete events are put into the same queue which handles the full sync objects. In a cluster with large amount of namespaces and resource quota objects, the queue becomes too long and makes the quota replenishment slow.

But I got an error: `Post "http://10.108.198.121:9040/v1/bind": dial tcp 10.108.198.121:9040: connect: connection timed out`.

I suppose  `ignorable` work fine in predicate path, but not work fine in bind path.

The Ignorable logic in kube-scheduler:
_pkg/scheduler/schedule_one.go: 637:_

title: Projected Service Account Tokens: Ability to specify multiple Audiences
body:
### What would you like to be added?

The Property `Audience` of  `ServiceAccountTokenProjection` is currently a `string`. (see [here]( https://kubernetes.io/docs/concepts/storage/projected-volumes/#serviceaccounttoken) and [here](https://github.com/kubernetes/enhancements/blob/master/keps/sig-auth/1205-bound-service-account-tokens/README.md#api-change))

Would be helpful if this could be an array of type string (`Audiences []string`)
  






### Why is this needed?

1. If the token is passed to a service for authentication and that service uses exactly that token to authenticate on the k8s token review api endpoint, then at least two audiences are necessary. First for the service itself and second the k8s api server audience. (Example Hashicorp Vault K8s Auth Plugin: see [here](https://github.com/hashicorp/vault-plugin-auth-kubernetes/blob/6f9c733333c1d5f86166db8db0016eda7bfb21bf/path_login.go#L456) and [here](https://github.com/hashicorp/vault-plugin-auth-kubernetes/blob/6f9c733333c1d5f86166db8db0016eda7bfb21bf/token_review.go#L71))

2. To be consistent with the manual `TokenRequest` api, which also allows to create tokens with multiple audiences (see [here](https://github.com/kubernetes/enhancements/blob/master/keps/sig-auth/1205-bound-service-account-tokens/README.md#api-changes))

body:
### What would you like to be added?

/metrics/slis was added for several components (apiserver, kube-controller-manager, kube-scheduler, kubelet, cloud-controller-manager) in https://kep.k8s.io/3466

This is to propose adding metric `process_start_time_seconds` to these components  for /metrics/slis to support cumulative metric `kubernetes_healthchecks_total`

### Why is this needed?

Missing start time metric in metrics/slis will result in inaccurate cumulative metrics.

Even though the start time metric is available in /metrics, it requires the metrics collector to scrape two endpoints at once and sync them to prepare the cumulative metric data.

title: Namespace resource reservation per node
body:
### What would you like to be added?

An object named NodeReservation :
- with one CPU entry
- if one pod of a namespace wants to be scheduled on a node the latter must have NodeReservation.cpu non requested and free CPU
- if at least one pod of this namespace run on a node, any pod of another namespace cannot consume the CPU reserved
- sum of all pod CPU limits of the namespace concerned by the NodeReservation, per node, cannot be greater than the NodeReservation.cpu
- CPU throttling of these pods happens if they try to consume more CPU than the NodeReservation.cpu
- pods of this namespace are never evicted

### Why is this needed?

Many applications are migrated to kubernetes.
Often these applications avoid to be evicted because they have not been originally designed to relaunch interrupted tasks or the cost to rerun a long task can be considered too high.
Also these applications come from the VM world, where there's no CPU limit per process but a global VM CPU capacity is shared between all processes running inside.
When migrating to kubernetes, finding good pod CPU limits and dealing with CPU throttling can be difficult to address.
It is not obvious to take a global VM CPU capacity an convert it to per pod CPU limits.

Some operators/developers would like their main application pods without CPU limits but also avoid them being evicted.

Is there a way to reserve a CPU capacity per namespace per node ?

Such a feature may not be desirable from a kubernetes point of view, but I am also curious to have hints to how address this issue differently with such applications without rewriting them from scratch or chose an oversized pod request = limit to either avoid eviction and CPU throttling. 

By the way, happy new year !

title: Service account token gets invalidated while terminating pod is re-deleted
body:
### What happened?

Attempting to kill a pod while it's already terminating causes its bound service account token to be invalidated.

This can happen, for example, when pod termination takes a long time, and an impatient user will re-attempt to delete it, this time with a short grace-period (e.g., via `kubectl delete pod --now`, which sets a grace-period=1s).



### What did you expect to happen?

I expect the service account token to remain valid throughout the entire lifetime of the pod, and for k8s API calls from within the pod to succeed (well, at least to authenticate successfully).

### How can we reproduce it (as minimally and precisely as possible)?

1. Create a role binding that allows the default service account to read pods:
```sh
kubectl create rolebinding --clusterrole view --serviceaccount default:default test
``` 
2. Create the following test pod.
The PreStop hook of the pod repeatedly runs `kubectl get pods`, and logs any error encountered:
```yaml
kubectl apply -f - << EOF
apiVersion: v1
kind: Pod
metadata:
  name: test
spec:
  terminationGracePeriodSeconds: 100000
  containers:
  - name: test
    image: bitnami/kubectl
    command:
    - "bin/sh"
    - "-c"
    - "sleep 100000000"
    lifecycle:
      preStop:
        exec:
          command:
          - "bin/sh"
          - "-c"
          - |
            echo "PreStop started at $(date +%T)" >> /tmp/prestop.log
            while true; do
              resp=$(kubectl get pods 2>&1)
              if [ $? -ne 0 ]; then
                echo "kubectl failed at $(date +%T)" >> /tmp/prestop.log
                echo $resp >> /tmp/prestop.log
              fi
              sleep 1
            done
EOF
```
3. Wait for the pod to become ready
```sh
kubectl get pod test --watch
```
4. Gracefully delete the pod, and immediately delete it again with gracePeriod=1 (== `--now`):
```sh
kubectl delete pod test --wait=false && kubectl delete pod test --wait=false --grace-period=1
```
5. Tail the logs of the PreStop hook:
```sh
kubectl exec -it test -- tail -f /tmp/prestop.log
```

The observed output is:
```
PreStop started at 07:14:25
kubectl failed at 07:15:30
error: You must be logged in to the server (Unauthorized)
kubectl failed at 07:15:31
error: You must be logged in to the server (Unauthorized)
kubectl failed at 07:15:32
error: You must be logged in to the server (Unauthorized)
kubectl failed at 07:15:33
error: You must be logged in to the server (Unauthorized)
```
6. Finally, cleanup by force deleting the pod.
(note - this only cleanups the pod, but the container remains dangling in the background):
```sh
kubectl delete pod test --force
```

### Anything else we need to know?

Based on several attempts to reproduce it, it seems that the token gets invalidated after about [60 seconds] + [grace-period seconds] + [a few seconds] - relative to when the pod was initially deleted.

Hence, different grace-period values yielded different token invalidation times:
- grace-period=1 --> invalidated after ~63s from initial pod deletion
- grace-period=30 --> ~95s
- grace-period=120 --> ~187s

On the other hand, if the 2nd delete command is issued at some later time (e.g., delete, sleep, delete --grace-period), then the token seems to be invalidated as soon as the 2nd deleted command is issued (+ [a few seconds]):
- sleep 120 + grace-period=1 --> ~127s
- sleep 120 + grace-period=30 --> ~126s

And yet on another hand (?!?!):
-sleep 120 + grace-period=120 --> ~3m
- sleep 90 + grace-period=300 --> ~6m

So, the invalidation timing seems to depend on multiple factors.
Hopefully this yields some useful clues.

### Kubernetes version

<details>

Tested on K8s v1.27.3(GKE), but also reproduced on v1.28.X (GKE + vanilla/kOps)
```console
$ kubectl version
Client Version: v1.28.4
Kustomize Version: v5.0.4-0.20230601165947-6ce0bf390ce3
Server Version: v1.27.3-gke.100
```

  - [x] add basic CI (unit tests, gofmt, ...?) to `kubernetes-sigs/knftables` (https://github.com/kubernetes-sigs/knftables/pull/3)

  - This wasn't discussed in the KEP, but it's fallout from other changes that were happening at the same time; we have a better way of dealing with this bug now (`--conntrack-tcp-be-liberal`) so we should remove the ugly hack from the nftables proxy and push people to use that instead if they need it.
- [x] ensure unit test parity with iptables. (I think all that's left here is adding unit tests for the packet tracing code in `helpers_test.go`.) (@npinaeva, https://github.com/kubernetes-sigs/knftables/pull/2, https://github.com/kubernetes-sigs/knftables/pull/6, #123389)

  - [Discussion in the KEP](https://github.com/kubernetes/enhancements/blob/master/keps/sig-network/3866-nftables-proxy/README.md#session-affinity). I'm not sure if anyone has suggested any particular benefits of the ipvs-like behavior vs the iptables-like behavior.
  - other discussion about changes to affinity behavior: #112806
  - also relevant on the LoadBalancer side (#123714); some LB implementations can't implement the current semantics.
  - Resolve the `UNRESOLVED` section of the KEP after a decision is made.
- [x] decide if we are using comments well in the ruleset. (I GUESS SO?)
  - We don't need many of the comments the iptables ruleset uses because our chain names are self-documenting.
  - In general I tried to put comments on objects (chains, sets, maps) rather than on individual rules, but there is some inconsistency. (But also, note that you won't see the chain/set/map comments with kernels < 5.10.)
  - Individual rules and set/map elements should have comments in some cases. E.g., [elements of `@no-endpoint-services` and `@no-endpoint-nodeports` have comments](https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/v1.29.0/pkg/proxy/nftables/proxier_test.go#L575-L577) so that you can see which IP/port goes with which service. But [elements of `@service-ips` and `@service-nodeports` don't](https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/v1.29.0/pkg/proxy/nftables/proxier_test.go#L570-L573) because you can already figure that out from the names of the chains that they jump to.

- [ ] optimize memory allocation:
  - reuse the buffers used for building the `nft -f -` input, [like iptables does](https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/v1.29.0/pkg/proxy/iptables/proxier.go#L185-L192). This could be done in a few ways. (Have `Proxier` keep buffers around like iptables does and pass a buffer to `nft.Run()`; have `knftables.realNFTables` keep buffers around itself and pass them to the `Transaction`; have `knftables.realNFTables` keep `Transaction`s around and reuse them (with the transaction storing its buffer); ...)
    - (@aroradaman, https://github.com/kubernetes-sigs/knftables/pull/9)
  - maybe reuse the `knftables.Transaction.operation` arrays somehow?
  - consider optimizing `knftables.Rule` generation wrt `knftables.Concat`. Some discussion [here](https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/pull/121046#discussion_r1367736334).

This could be done by making sure there is always a separate rule to catch 127.0.0.1:nodeport rather than letting it be caught by a generic rule, and then checking the counters on those rules and exporting some metric with the result. (@aroradaman, https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/pull/125015)

title: kubectl auth can-i command behaviour is wrong for impersonated users
body:
### What happened?

The kubectl auth can-i command behaves differently when using the --user and --as options.
The --as option only checks the explicit permissions granted to the user via roles and bindings. It does not check the permissions which a user acquires through its associated group.
The --user option works correctly (provided the user is in the kubeconfig file)

### What did you expect to happen?

The --as option should also check the permissions that a user acquires through its associated group.

### How can we reproduce it (as minimally and precisely as possible)?

Either a minikube or kubeadm cluster with kubectl installed. openssl is needed to generate CSRs.

1. Create a new `clusterrolebinding` that binds the `cluster-admin` role to a new dummy group called `example-masters`
```
cat <<EOF | kubectl apply -f -
apiVersion: rbac.authorization.k8s.io/v1
kind: ClusterRoleBinding
metadata:
  name: example-cluster-admin
roleRef:
  apiGroup: rbac.authorization.k8s.io
  kind: ClusterRole
  name: cluster-admin
subjects:
- apiGroup: rbac.authorization.k8s.io
  kind: Group
  name: example:masters
EOF
```

2. Create a new user and associate it with the `example:masters` group
```
openssl genrsa -out poweruser.key 2048
openssl req -new -key poweruser.key -out poweruser.csr -subj "/CN=poweruser/O=example:masters"
```

3. Get the base64 encoded output of the csr
cat poweruser.csr | base64 | tr -d "\n"

4. Create a new certificatesigningrequest by passing the base64 output
```
cat <<EOF | kubectl apply -f -
apiVersion: certificates.k8s.io/v1
kind: CertificateSigningRequest
metadata:
  name: poweruser
spec:
  request: 
  signerName: kubernetes.io/kube-apiserver-client
  expirationSeconds: 86400  # one day
  usages:
  - client auth
EOF
```

5. Approve the CSR
`kubectl certificate approve poweruser`

6. Extract the certificate in a file called poweruser.crt
`kubectl get csr poweruser -o jsonpath='{.status.certificate}'| base64 -d > poweruser.crt`

7. Add the new credentials to the kubeconfig
`kubectl config set-credentials poweruser --client-key=poweruser.key --client-certificate=poweruser.crt --embed-certs=true`

8. Add a new context
`kubectl config set-context poweruser --cluster=minikube --user=poweruser`

9. Try the kubectl auth can-i command to verify the permissions on the new user by passing the --user option
```
kubectl auth can-i create pods --user=poweruser
yes
```
This is the correct output as the user has cluster-admin permission via the example:masters group.

10. Try the kubectl auth can-i command to verify the permissions on the new user by passing the --as option
```
kubectl auth can-i create pods --as=poweruser
no
```
**_This result is not as per expectation. The logical output should have been ```yes``` as ```poweruser``` has the cluster-admin role via the example:masters group._** 

11. We can prove this by actually performing an action to create a pod by acting as the poweruser
Switch to the context just created
`kubectl config use-context poweruser`

12. Try to create a pod and it is successful.
`kubectl run nginx-poweruser --image=nginx`

```
kubectl get pod nginx-poweruser 
NAME              READY   STATUS    RESTARTS   AGE
nginx-poweruser   1/1     Running   0          26s
```



### Anything else we need to know?

This is reproducible on a minikube cluster as well as a cluster created through kubeadm.

body:
### What happened?

While validating nftable mode using conformance test, the following error logs were produced consistently:
```
E0104 17:21:56.957351       1 proxier.go:941] "Unable to delete stale chains; will retry later" err=<
        /dev/stdin:1:28-90: Error: Could not process rule: Device or resource busy
        delete chain ip kube-proxy service-QZNVUP4F-endpointslice-3291/example-named-port/tcp/http

        delete chain ip kube-proxy endpoint-A6Z5NSSV-endpointslice-3291/example-named-port/tcp/http__10.244.2.28/3001
                                   ^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^

E0104 18:43:05.945300       1 proxier.go:941] "Unable to delete stale chains; will retry later" err=<
        /dev/stdin:1:28-93: Error: Could not process rule: Device or resource busy
        delete chain ip kube-proxy endpoint-EVHUKXWZ-services-4440/externalsvc/tcp/__10.244.1.80/9376
                                   ^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^
 
I0104 18:43:06.986202       1 proxier.go:935] "Deleting stale nftables chains" numChains=3
I0104 18:43:16.462808       1 proxier.go:935] "Deleting stale nftables chains" numChains=1
E0104 18:43:16.517339       1 proxier.go:941] "Unable to delete stale chains; will retry later" err=<
        /dev/stdin:1:28-99: Error: Could not process rule: Device or resource busy
        delete chain ip kube-proxy endpoint-FJWEGLAR-services-6954/affinity-nodeport/tcp/__10.244.2.70/9376
                                   ^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^

I0104 18:50:42.968934       1 proxier.go:935] "Deleting stale nftables chains" numChains=8
I0104 18:50:55.643712       1 proxier.go:935] "Deleting stale nftables chains" numChains=1
E0104 18:50:55.677064       1 proxier.go:941] "Unable to delete stale chains; will retry later" err=<
        /dev/stdin:1:28-100: Error: Could not process rule: Device or resource busy
        delete chain ip kube-proxy endpoint-TK32CM73-services-3530/affinity-clusterip/tcp/__10.244.2.99/9376
                                   ^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^
```

I thought it was because a known issue described here: https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/09a5049ca785024edd4955eb82e855d9b5657491/pkg/proxy/nftables/proxier.go#L1519-L1524
However, the error was produced for every run and every kube-proxy instance, which doesn't seem related to the kernel bug.

After some investigation, I think it's caused by a bug: in some cases a chain could change from stale to active, but once it's added to `staleChains` it will always be deleted once. When the proxier tries to delete a previously stale but currently active chain, it would fail and lead to these errors, though it won't cause real problem thanks to kernel's validation.

cc @danwinship 

### What did you expect to happen?

kube-proxy shouldn't try to delete active chains and produce such error logs.

### How can we reproduce it (as minimally and precisely as possible)?

The e2e test case can reproduce it consistantly:
```
sonobuoy run --e2e-focus "should create Endpoints and EndpointSlices for Pods matching a Service"
```

### What happened?

Addresses like `fd00::10.0.0.34` should work, as they do for proxy-mode ipvs and iptables

What "canonical" really is can be debated. The [rfc5952](https://datatracker.ietf.org/doc/html/rfc5952) seems to accept "embedded ipv4", as long as the prefix follows the rules. So, as I understand it, `fd00::10.0.0.34` *is* a canonical IPv6 address.

title: E2E test is not setting the EndpointSlices conditions to ready
body:
The test create custome EndpointSlices to validate some behaviors sending traffic, so it is clear that it expects the EndpointSlices to be ready, 

https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/b529e6ff1c7edb3bb1eaca185b9662d8e42ac2d0/test/e2e/network/endpointslice.go#L698-L712

The API doc is vague about this situation and leaves room to interpret the "unknown behavior", quoting @danwinship

> I was going to say that the API docs say that Ready: nil means it is ready, but actually it says "A nil value indicates an unknown state. In most cases consumers should interpret this unknown state as ready". FTR, kube-proxy interprets nil as true for Ready and Serving, and false for Terminating. It's possible we should update the API docs to make that official. Or if not, probably we should change the e2e tests to not rely on undefined values

Since the test expects the EndpointSlices to be Ready we should set them, if we decide to change the API behavior, then we should add an additional e2e test to validate this behavior, but not use the same test to validate two different things

title: Assigned Pod add/update events don't requeue Pods without PodAffinity
body:
### What happened?

/sig scheduling
/kind bug

- AssignedPodAdded(): https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/b529e6ff1c7edb3bb1eaca185b9662d8e42ac2d0/pkg/scheduler/internal/queue/scheduling_queue.go#L1044
- AssignedPodUpdated(): https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/b529e6ff1c7edb3bb1eaca185b9662d8e42ac2d0/pkg/scheduler/internal/queue/scheduling_queue.go#L1069


When assigned Pods are created/updated, cluster events (Pod/Add or Pod/Update) should be delivered for all plugins that subscribe those events. But, actually `getUnschedulablePodsWithMatchingAffinityTerm` pre-filters Pods to receive those events based on Pods' affinity and `pod.Status.Resize`. - meaning only PodAffinity/NodeResourceFit receive them actually.

The problem here is similar to #110175 - in in-tree plugins, PodAffinity, PodTopologySpread and NodeResourceFit subscribe Pod add and/or update events. And, Pods rejected by PodTopologySpread will never be requeued to activeQ by Pod-related events. The same happens for custom plugins registering pod add and/or update events.


### What did you expect to happen?

All Pods will get chances to get back to activeQ by Pod-related events.

### How can we reproduce it (as minimally and precisely as possible)?

Run ↓ in https://github.com/sanposhiho/kubernetes/tree/pod-bug-repro.

title: ValidatingAdmissionPolicy using CRDs as paramKind always fails after restarting kube-apiserver
body:
### What happened?

I'm using ValidatingAdmissionPolicy(VAP) with setting my own CRD to paramKind in my on-premise cluster. It works fine, but once I restarted one of the kube-apiserver instances it changed to reject both valid and invalid requests with the error message like:

```
error: failed to create rolebinding: rolebindings.rbac.authorization.k8s.io "view" is forbidden: ValidatingAdmissionPolicy 'test-vap' denied request: failed to configure policy: failed to find resource referenced by paramKind: 'example.com/v1alpha1, Kind=Foo'
```

### What did you expect to happen?

VAP using CRDs as paramKind should continue to work fine even when one of kube-apiserver instances is restarted.

### How can we reproduce it (as minimally and precisely as possible)?

You can reproduce it locally using kind cluster by following procedure.

<details>

```
$ cat kind.yaml         
kind: Cluster
apiVersion: kind.x-k8s.io/v1alpha4
nodes:
- role: control-plane
  kubeadmConfigPatches:
  - |
    kind: ClusterConfiguration
    apiServer:
      extraArgs:
        feature-gates: "ValidatingAdmissionPolicy=true"
        runtime-config: "admissionregistration.k8s.io/v1beta1=true"

$ kind create cluster --image=kindest/node:v1.29.0 --config kind.yaml
Creating cluster "kind" ...
 ✓ Ensuring node image (kindest/node:v1.29.0) 🖼

Set kubectl context to "kind-kind"
You can now use your cluster with:

Thanks for using kind! 😊

$ cat << EOF | kubectl apply -f -

  scope: Namespaced
  versions:
  - name: v1alpha1
    schema:
      openAPIV3Schema:
        properties:
          apiVersion:
            type: string
          kind:
            type: string
          metadata:
            type: object
          spec:
            properties:
              foo:
                type: string
            type: object
        type: object
    served: true
    storage: true
EOF
customresourcedefinition.apiextensions.k8s.io/foos.example.com created

$ kubectl create ns test                                                                           
namespace/test created

$ cat << EOF | kubectl apply -f -
apiVersion: admissionregistration.k8s.io/v1beta1
kind: ValidatingAdmissionPolicy
metadata:
  name: test-vap
spec:
  failurePolicy: Fail
  paramKind:
    apiVersion: example.com/v1alpha1
    kind: Foo
  matchConstraints:
    resourceRules:
    - apiGroups: ["rbac.authorization.k8s.io"]
      apiVersions: ["v1"]
      operations: ["CREATE", "UPDATE"]
      resources: ["rolebindings"]
  validations:
  - expression: "object.subjects.all(s, s.name == params.spec.foo)"
    messageExpression: "'subject must be ' + string(params.spec.foo)"
---
apiVersion: example.com/v1alpha1
kind: Foo
metadata:
  name: for-vap
  namespace: test
spec:
  foo: foo
---
apiVersion: admissionregistration.k8s.io/v1beta1
kind: ValidatingAdmissionPolicyBinding
metadata:
  name: test-vap-binding
spec:
  policyName: test-vap
  validationActions: [Deny]
  paramRef:
    name: for-vap
    namespace: test
    parameterNotFoundAction: Deny
EOF

foo.example.com/for-vap created
validatingadmissionpolicybinding.admissionregistration.k8s.io/test-vap-binding created

# Before restart, you can create the RoleBinding that matches to the VAP rule.

$ kubectl delete rolebinding view -n test
rolebinding.rbac.authorization.k8s.io "view" deleted

$ docker exec -it kind-control-plane sh -c 'crictl stop $(crictl ps | grep kube-apiserver | awk '\''{print $1}'\'')'
$ kubectl get po -n kube-system  | grep kube-apiserver

# After restarting of the kube-apiserver, you cannot create the same RoleBinding.
$ kubectl create rolebinding view --clusterrole=view --group=foo -n test
```

### Anything else we need to know?

title: OpenAPI handler fails on duplicated path
body:
### What happened?

When installing the metrics-server to implement the metrics.k8s.io API and the prometheus-adapter to implement the custom.metrics.k8s.io API, it is possible to make the OpenAPI handler fail to initialize with this error log in apiserver: https://github.com/kubernetes/kube-openapi/blob/master/pkg/aggregator/aggregator.go#L343
```
handler.go:159] Error in OpenAPI handler: failed to build merge specs: unable to merge: duplicated path /apis/metrics.k8s.io/v1beta1/pods
handler.go:159] Error in OpenAPI handler: failed to build merge specs: unable to merge: duplicated path /apis/metrics.k8s.io/v1beta1/namespaces/{namespace}/pods
handler.go:159] Error in OpenAPI handler: failed to build merge specs: unable to merge: duplicated path /apis/metrics.k8s.io/v1beta1/nodes
handler.go:159] Error in OpenAPI handler: failed to build merge specs: unable to merge: duplicated path /apis/metrics.k8s.io/v1beta1/nodes/{name}
handler.go:159] Error in OpenAPI handler: failed to build merge specs: unable to merge: duplicated path /apis/metrics.k8s.io/v1beta1/nodes
```
This will result in kubectl discovery calls to /openapi/v2 to fail with a 503:
```
{
  "kind": "Event",
```

The OpenAPI handler should not fail to initialize if both metrics.k8s.io and custom.metrics.k8s.io are serving the same path for different API groups/versions.

### How can we reproduce it (as minimally and precisely as possible)?

I can provide exact installation steps if needed, however, a high-level repro is:
- install metrics-server to serve v1beta1.metrics.k8s.io  
- install prometheus-adapter to serve v1beta1.custom.metrics.k8s.io

### What happened? We wanted to start using the SLI for kubelet pod start duration, as per: - https://github.com/kubernetes/community/blob/master/sig-scalability/slos/pod_startup_latency.md - https://github.com/kubernetes/community/blob/master/sig-scalability/slos/slos.md#steady-state-slisslos - https://github.com/kubernetes/community/pull/2204 - https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/pull/111930 ...but it turns out that it seems to report unexpected/unusable **negative** values in the `sum` metric of the histogram, i.e: `kubelet_pod_start_sli_duration_seconds_sum` ### What did you expect to happen? As it's a duration, only positive values would be expected. ### How can we reproduce it (as minimally and precisely as possible)? `count(kubelet_pod_start_sli_duration_seconds_sum < 0) / count(kubelet_pod_start_sli_duration_seconds_sum)` is `1` over time, i.e. all values are negative. For example: `rate(kubelet_pod_start_sli_duration_seconds_sum[10m])` gives negative durations: > ### Anything else we need to know? title: Ubuntu Remove Snap LXD + Vanilla Kubernetes + Restart = kubelet fails
body:
### What happened?

Ubuntu has a package manager called snapd.  I do not use snaps, so I decided to remove it.
After removing snapd, kubelet fails to start.
Update: Snap runs lxd which appears to be a dependency.

### What did you expect to happen?

No impact as Kubernetes should not depend on snapd or lxd.

### How can we reproduce it (as minimally and precisely as possible)?

Install Ubuntu 22.04
Install Kubernetes 1.29
Install cri-o 1.28

Use kubeadm init vanilla.
kubeadm init --apiserver-advertise-address=xxx --control-plane-endpoint=xxx --pod-network-cidr=10.244.0.0/16

Upon completion kubelet is running:
```
`● kubelet.service - kubelet: The Kubernetes Node Agent
     Loaded: loaded (/lib/systemd/system/kubelet.service; enabled; vendor preset: enabled)
    Drop-In: /usr/lib/systemd/system/kubelet.service.d
             └─10-kubeadm.conf
     Active: active (running) since Wed 2024-01-10 10:34:39 UTC; 20min ago`
```
Now remove snapd:
`apt-get autoremove -y --purge snapd && apt-mark hold snapd`

Or alternatively:
`snap remove --purge lxd`

Power off the machine (cold).
Power on the machine.

body:
### What happened?

The event `RecreatingTerminatedPod` is emitted ~10 times simultaneously after evicting pods of a Statefulset.



### What did you expect to happen?

The event should only be emitted at most once.

### How can we reproduce it (as minimally and precisely as possible)?

- Create a 1.29 kind cluster:
```
kind create cluster --image kindest/node:v1.29
```
 (tested with `sha256:eaa1450915475849a73a9227b8f201df25e55e268e5d619312131292e324d570`)

- Deploy a statefulset:

```
apiVersion: apps/v1
kind: StatefulSet
metadata:
  name: web
spec:
  replicas: 2
  selector:
    matchLabels:
      app: nginx
  template:
    metadata:
      labels:
        app: nginx
    spec:
      containers:
      - name: nginx
        image: nginx
        ports:
        - containerPort: 80
          name: web
```

```
kubectl get events  --field-selector involvedObject.kind=StatefulSet,involvedObject.name=web,reason=RecreatingTerminatedPod -o json | jq '.items[].count'
```

(shoud return nothing)

```
kubectl taint nodes kind-control-plane foo=bar:NoExecute
```

```
kubectl get events  --field-selector involvedObject.kind=StatefulSet,involvedObject.name=web,reason=RecreatingTerminatedPod -o json | jq '.items[].count'
```

`fieldPath="" kind="StatefulSet" apiVersion="apps/v1" type="Normal" reason="SuccessfulDelete" message="delete Pod web-0 in StatefulSet web successful"` is confusing as well.

- The same problem occurs with the event `RecreatingFailedPod`, deploy the statefulet:

```
apiVersion: apps/v1
kind: StatefulSet
metadata:
  name: web
spec:
  replicas: 2
  selector:
    matchLabels:
      app: nginx
  template:
    metadata:
      labels:
        app: nginx
    spec:
      containers:
      - name: nginx
        image: nginx
        command:
        - /bin/sh
        - -c
        - |
          sleep 3;
          exit 1
        ports:
        - containerPort: 80
          name: web
```

title: kube-scheduler memory leak issue in v1.28.3
body:
### What happened?

We have identified a memory leak issue in kube-scheduler after upgrading to version v1.28.3. Despite a stable number of pods/nodes, we have noticed a continuous increase in kube-scheduler memory usage over time.

![image](https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/assets/95034/4f363977-720f-468a-860f-833fb4ee4059)

Upon analyzing the pprof dump, it was observed that a significant portion of the memory is consumed by watch.(*StreamWatcher).receive

The kube-scheduler(v1.28.3)memory usage is expected to keep stable

title: UDP connections of Services are not preserved after restarting kube-proxy
body:
### What happened?

When running kube-proxy with log level 4, I found it always clears all UDP contrack entries for all service IPs and NodePorts unconditionally after it's restarted even when the Services and Endpoints/EndpointSlices don't change.

Clearing UDP conntrack entries could cause UDP connections to switch to other endpoints. Although UDP is stateless, endpoint change may unnecessarily disrupt connections for some protocols built on UDP, e.g. QUIC. 

From the code, the reason why these UDP conntrack entries need to be deleted seems to be: if service traffic towards a service IP arrive before the iptables/nftables rules for the services IP, it could produce a conntrack entry which will keep black hole subsequent packets after the iptables/nftables rules are installed. And it uses zero endpoints -> non-zero endpoints change as the trigger for the cleanup. However, when kube-proxy restarts, in the first sync, all services will meet the condition, so all UDP conntrack entries of services are deleted.

After investigating what's the "black hole" conntrack entry, I realize it may be just a normal conntrack entry with no destination IP translation. When a packet to a service IP arrives, if there is no DNAT rule for it (because iptables/nftables rules are not installed yet), it will likely be forwarded to the primary network interface by matching the default route, creating a conntrack entry with no destination IP translation, which causes subsequent packets bypass NAT table.
